pages.title: Introduction
pages.summary: What Rail22 is, what you can build with it, and how these docs are organized.
pages.html:
Rail22 is a workflow automation platform. You draw a workflow on a canvas: a trigger that starts it, and steps connected one after another. Rail22 runs it for you each time the trigger fires: on a schedule, when an email or a web request arrives, when someone fills in a form or uploads a file, or when you press Run.

What you can build

A few examples of what teams automate with Rail22:

  • Email processing: read the messages that arrive in a mailbox, pick out the order number or the attachment, store them in a data table and reply.
  • Approvals: a form starts the workflow, a Human task asks a manager to approve or reject, and the workflow continues with the answer.
  • Integrations: call any HTTP API, move files over FTP / SFTP, work with Google Drive, Sheets, Gmail and Calendar, or Microsoft 365 (Outlook, OneDrive / SharePoint, Excel, Teams).
  • AI steps: summarize, classify or extract data with Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or a model you run yourself (Ollama, Lemonade, LM Studio).
  • Scheduled jobs: every night, fetch a report, compare it with yesterday's and send the differences by email.

The main parts

PartWhat it is for
Workflow designerThe canvas where you add steps, connect them and set them up. It saves as you work and shows errors before you run.
TriggersWhat starts a workflow: Manual, Schedule, Webhook, Form, File upload, Email (inbound).
StepsThe actions and the logic: If, Switch, Loop, Merge, Set, Wait, Code, HTTP Request, emails, data tables, human tasks, AI and the integrations.
Credentials & variablesThe passwords, API keys and OAuth connections the steps use, and the project's shared values. They are kept encrypted, so they never appear in a workflow.
Data tablesSimple tables inside Rail22 that workflows read and write, without a database of your own.
Knowledge basesYour documents (files, web pages, texts), searched by meaning and by words, so that workflows and AI steps answer from your own content.
Forms and My tasksThe pages where people take part in workflows: they fill in forms and complete the tasks assigned to them.
Executions and logsEvery run: its state, a log of what each step did, the variables and the error, if any.

How these docs are organized

  • Getting started: the concepts and a first workflow, built step by step.
  • Building workflows: the designer, every trigger and step, expressions, errors, publishing and executions.
  • Guides: modeling a workflow, using data tables, and complete examples.
  • Workspace: forms, tasks, data tables, knowledge bases, files, credentials and variables, the Assistant.
  • Account administration: users, roles, sign-in (MFA, LDAP, SAML), usage and the audit logs.
  • Self-hosting: installing and running Rail22 on your own server.
  • Developers: webhooks, the MCP server, the expression language and plugins.

Tip: press / anywhere on this site to search.

Next steps

Read Core concepts for the vocabulary, then build your first workflow in the Quick start.

pages.title: Core concepts
pages.summary: Accounts, projects, workflows, triggers, steps, variables, versions and executions: the vocabulary of Rail22.
pages.html:
This page explains the words used everywhere in Rail22 and in these docs. Each concept has its own page later on. This is the short version.

Account

An account is your organization in Rail22: a company or a team. It holds the users, the projects and everything in them. Its settings, such as the date formats, sign-in rules and how long logs are kept, apply to all of its users. The account's plan may set limits, such as the number of data tables, the space for files and the monthly AI credits, and which integrations are available. Account settings covers the settings, and Usage and AI credits the plan's limits.

Users and roles

Every person who signs in is a user of the account. What a user may do comes from their role. A new account has three roles:

  • Owner: everything, including the account's settings, users and roles.
  • Member: works in the projects they belong to: builds and runs workflows, manages credentials, tables and files.
  • Participant: takes part in workflows without building them: fills in the forms and completes the tasks assigned to them.

An owner can create more roles with their own permissions.

Projects

A project groups related work: its workflows, credentials and variables, data tables and files. A project has an owner and members, each with a role in the project. Only members see a project's content. Switch between projects from the project name at the top of the sidebar.

Workflows

A workflow is an automation: a trigger and the steps that follow it, drawn in the designer. A workflow has exactly one trigger. Every other step must be reachable from it.

Triggers

The trigger is the first step and decides when the workflow runs:

TriggerStarts a run
Manual TriggerWhen you press Run in the designer.
Schedule TriggerAt set times: every few minutes, daily, on certain weekdays…
WebhookWhen another system sends an HTTP request to the workflow's address.
FormWhen someone submits the workflow's form.
File uploadWhen a file is uploaded to the workflow.
Email (inbound)When an email arrives at the workflow's address.

To process a mailbox regularly, start with a Schedule Trigger followed by a Read emails (IMAP), Gmail or Outlook Mail step.

Steps and connections

A step does one thing: sends an email, calls an API, tests a condition, waits. Steps are connected from an output to the input of the next step. Most steps have one output. Some have several, and the run continues only on the matching one:

  • If has a true and a false output.
  • Switch has one output per case.
  • Steps that call other systems can have an error output, so a failure takes another path instead of stopping the run.

Loop repeats the steps inside it for each item of a list. Merge joins branches: it continues once all of them arrived, or at the first one. A Note is a comment on the canvas and is not connected.

Variables and expressions

Steps pass data to each other through variables. A step that produces something stores it in a variable. For example, HTTP Request stores the response in response by default, and a Set step stores the value you give it. Later steps read variables with expressions written between double braces:

Order {{ order.number }} from {{ mail.from }}
{{ response.body.items.length }}
{{ customer.name.toUpperCase() }}

A field that holds only one expression keeps the value's type (a number, a list, an object). Otherwise the result is text. The designer suggests the variables available at each step as you type. Expressions has the details.

Credentials and project variables

Credentials hold what steps need to connect to other systems: passwords, API keys, OAuth connections to Google or Microsoft, SMTP and IMAP servers. They belong to a project and are stored encrypted. A step only refers to a credential by name, so exporting or sharing a workflow never exposes a secret.

Project variables are shared values, such as a base URL or a team's email address. Any workflow of the project reads them as {{ vars.name }}.

Drafts, publishing and versions

What you edit in the designer is the workflow's draft. Its changes are saved automatically. A draft runs only when you press Run: the trigger does not start it.

Publishing saves the draft as a numbered version (v1, v2…) and makes it the one the trigger runs. You can keep editing the draft without affecting the published version, then publish again when ready. You can always see older versions, publish one again, or copy it back into the draft. Unpublishing stops the trigger from starting new runs.

Executions

Each run of a workflow is an execution. It records the version it ran, what started it (for example the webhook request or the email), the variables, and the state of every step:

StateMeaning
RunRunning now.
SleepWaiting: for a Wait step's time, or for a human task to be completed.
CompletedFinished without errors.
ErrorA step failed, and the error message says which and why.

The Executions panel in the designer lists a workflow's runs. For each run it shows the state, the error if any, the log (what each step did) and the variables. The account's execution log keeps a record of all runs.

pages.title: Quick start: your first workflow
pages.summary: Build, run and publish a workflow that calls a web API, checks the answer and stores a value.
pages.html:
In about ten minutes you will build a workflow that calls a web API, checks the answer and stores a value from it. You will run it from the designer, then see how to make it run by itself.

Before you start: sign in to Rail22 with a user that can create workflows in a project, such as an Owner or a Member of the project.

1. Create the workflow

  1. In the sidebar, next to Workflows, click +.
  2. The new workflow opens in the designer. To give it a name, click the gear icon in the toolbar, type My first workflow and save.

The canvas is empty, with a + button in the middle: "Add the first step: a trigger starts the workflow".

2. Add a trigger

  1. Click the + in the middle of the canvas. The step list opens, with a search box.
  2. Type manual and choose Manual Trigger.

A Manual Trigger has no settings: it starts a run when you press Run. It is the easiest trigger to try things with.

3. Call a web API

  1. Click the small + next to the trigger's output and choose HTTP Request. The new step is connected to the trigger, and its settings open.
  2. Set Method to GET and URL to https://httpbin.org/json. This public test API answers with a small JSON document.
  3. Leave Response variable as response, and close the settings.

When this step runs, response holds the answer: response.ok, response.status (200 when all went well), response.headers and response.body. JSON bodies are decoded, so you can reach into them with dots.

4. Check the answer

  1. Click the + next to the HTTP Request's output and choose If.
  2. In the first condition, set Test to {{ response.status }}, the operator to equals and Value to 200.

The If step now has two outputs, true and false. The run continues on the one that matches.

5. Store a value

  1. Click the + next to the If's true output and choose Set.
  2. Set Variable to title, and Value to {{ response.body.slideshow.title }}. As you type after {{, the designer suggests the variables available here.

Your workflow now reads: Manual Trigger → HTTP Request → If → (true) Set.

Note: the designer saves every change. The status at the right of the toolbar shows Saved. The bug icon opens the list of errors and warnings, such as a missing setting or a step that is not connected. A workflow with errors is saved, but it cannot be run or published until they are fixed.

6. Run it

  1. Click Run (the green play icon in the toolbar).
  2. The Executions panel opens at the bottom and shows the new run. It refreshes every few seconds while the run is in progress.
  3. When it is Completed, look at its Log (one line per step) and its Variables: response holds the API's answer, and title is Sample Slide Show.

If a step fails, the execution's state is Error, with the message of the step that failed. For example, change the URL to https://httpbin.org/status/404 and run again. The If now continues on its false output, because response.status is 404.

7. Make it run by itself

A Manual Trigger only runs when you press Run. To run the workflow automatically:

  1. Delete the Manual Trigger and add a Schedule Trigger in its place, for example every hour. Then connect its output to the HTTP Request's input.
  2. Open the status menu in the toolbar (it says Draft) and choose Publish the draft as v1. You can add a note about what changed.

The button turns green: v1 published. From now on the trigger starts a run every hour, and each run appears in the Executions panel. If you edit the workflow later, the draft is marked draft changed, while the trigger keeps running v1 until you publish again.

What next

  • Learn the canvas in The designer.
  • Browse the triggers and steps.
  • Store the API key of a real service in a credential, then use it in the HTTP Request.

Before your next workflow, read Modeling a workflow, and see the examples.

pages.title: The designer
pages.summary: The canvas where you build a workflow: adding and connecting steps, their settings, saving, undo, and the panels.
pages.html:
Open a workflow from the sidebar (under Workflows) and it opens in the designer: a canvas with the workflow's steps and their connections, and a toolbar above it.

Note: the designer works best on a computer. On a phone you can still open, view and run a workflow.

The toolbar

ControlWhat it does
Errors / warnings badgesThe number of problems found in the workflow. Point at a badge to see the list.
Status menu (Draft, v3 published…)Publish, unpublish, versions, duplicate and delete. See Publishing and versions.
Zoom out / Fit / Zoom inThe canvas zoom. Fit shows the whole workflow.
Run (play icon)Runs the draft now. See Executions.
Executions (clock icon)Opens the panel with the workflow's runs.
Debug (bug icon)Opens the panel with the errors and warnings.
Settings (gear icon)The workflow's name and icon.
Undo / RedoSteps back and forward through your changes. Shortcuts: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y).
Save statusSaved, Saving… or Not saved. Click it to retry a failed save.

Adding steps

  • The first step: on an empty canvas, click the + in the middle. A workflow starts with a trigger.
  • After a step: click the small + next to one of its outputs. The new step is placed to the right and already connected.
  • Anywhere: click the green + at the top left of the canvas to open the step list. Click a step to add it in the middle of the view, or drag it onto the canvas.

The step list has a search box: type part of a name, move with the arrow keys and press Enter to add the highlighted step, or Esc to close the list. A new step opens its settings right away.

The steps are grouped by what they work with: Triggers, Flow, Data, Email, Web & files, Google, Microsoft, Databases, Security, Backup, Monitoring, Virtualization, Domains & DNS, AI, Regional (the steps of a country, from a regional plugin), SAP (from the SAP plugin) and Developer. Click a group's name to close or open it.

Some steps are marked advanced: they need some technical knowledge, such as HTTP Request, Code, the database steps, LDAP, FTP / SFTP, GravityZone Investigation and GravityZone API, Veeam Restore and Veeam API, FortiGate API, Sophos Firewall API, Wazuh API, Checkmk API, Zabbix API, VMware API, Proxmox API, Hyper-V PowerShell, Namecheap API, Shopify GraphQL, Nextcloud API, Jira API, HubSpot API, Salesforce API, GLPI API, Intune API, the Webhook trigger and the self-hosted AI servers. Every step is available to everyone. The Advanced switch at the top of the step list only chooses whether the advanced steps are listed. The search always finds them. Your choice is remembered for your user, in every browser. New users start with the switch off.

Connecting steps

Drag from a step's output (on its right side) to another step's input (on its left side). To remove a connection, click it, then click the ✕ that appears in its middle.

Steps with several outputs show the name of each: true / false for If, the cases for Switch, success / error when a step continues on errors. An output may have several connections: the run then goes on along each of them.

Moving around

  • Drag the empty canvas to move the view. Use the mouse wheel to zoom, or pinch on a touch screen.
  • Drag a step by its body to move it. Drag its corner to resize it.
  • Click a step to select it. Press Delete or Backspace to delete the selected step, or use the trash icon on the step.

Step settings

Double-click a step, or use the pencil icon on it, to open its settings. The dialog is laid out the same way for every step:

  • On the first line: the step's name (shown on the canvas) and the variable it sets, if any.
  • Then the credential and the operation, for steps that connect to other systems.
  • Then the step's own settings.
  • Last, Advanced…: the technical settings, which have defaults that suit most workflows (for example the model's temperature, the request headers, the sort order of the files), then what happens on an error, the limits and the timeout.

The Advanced… section is closed when the dialog opens. Click it to open it. It opens by itself when one of its settings is not at its default, or when one of them has a problem when you click OK.

Fields marked for expressions accept {{ }}. As you type after {{, the designer suggests the variables that exist at this point of the workflow, with their fields: for example response. suggests status, body, headers… See Expressions.

Steps that set a variable show its name on the canvas, under the title, so you can see where each variable comes from.

Saving

Every change is saved automatically a moment after you make it. You don't need a Save button: Ctrl+S only saves right away. If a save fails, for example when the connection drops, the designer tries again every few seconds and shows Not saved until it succeeds.

A draft is saved even when it has errors, such as a missing required setting. It cannot be run or published until they are fixed.

Errors and warnings

The designer checks the workflow as you build it:

  • Errors stop Run and Publish. Examples: The workflow has no trigger, Only one trigger is allowed, A trigger cannot be inside a loop, This step is connected to itself, and missing or invalid settings.
  • Warnings don't stop anything but point at likely mistakes, such as Not connected to the trigger or an expression that uses an unknown variable.

Open the Debug panel (bug icon) for the full list. Steps with a problem are marked on the canvas.

Loops on the canvas

A Loop is a box that holds other steps. Drag steps into it, or add them from an output of a step that is already inside. The steps inside run once for each item. The connection that leaves the loop's own output runs after the last item.

The Assistant

When the Assistant is enabled for your account, the designer has an Assistant panel. Describe what you want in plain words, such as "read new mails from the support mailbox and store the sender and subject in the Tickets table". The Assistant builds or changes the workflow on the canvas. See The Assistant.

pages.title: Triggers
pages.summary: What starts a workflow: Manual, Schedule, Webhook, Form, Chat, File upload, Email (inbound) and more.
pages.html:
Every workflow starts with exactly one trigger. The trigger decides when the workflow runs, and puts what started it into a variable for the next steps: the request, the form's answers, the file, the email.

TriggerStarts a runVariable
Manual TriggerWhen you press Run in the designernone
Schedule TriggerAt set timesschedule_time
WebhookOn an HTTP request to the workflow's addresswebhook
FormWhen someone sends the workflow's formform, form_user
ChatWhen someone writes to the workflow on its chat pagemessage, conversation, user
File uploadWhen a file is uploaded to the projectfile
Email (inbound)When an email arrives at the workflow's addressmail
Called by a workflowWhen another workflow of the project runs it (the Run a workflow step)its inputs, caller
Teams messageWhen someone writes in a Microsoft Teams chat of the credential's account (checked on a schedule)message, conversation, user, teams
GravityZone eventWhen Bitdefender GravityZone sends eventsgz
Veeam eventWhen Veeam Backup & Replication job sessions end (checked on a schedule)veeam
FortiGate eventWhen a FortiGate automation stitch sends an eventfgt
Checkmk problemWhen Checkmk reports a new problem, or one clears (checked on a schedule)cmk
Zabbix problemWhen Zabbix reports a new problem, or one is resolved (checked on a schedule)zbx
Wazuh alertOn new Wazuh alerts of a level and worse (checked on a schedule)alert
VMware alarmWhen a vCenter alarm turns red (or yellow), or one clears (checked on a schedule)alarm
Proxmox taskWhen a Proxmox VE task ends, such as a failed backup (checked on a schedule)task
Hyper-V VM stateWhen a Hyper-V VM stops running or its replication health turns bad, or it recovers (checked on a schedule)hv
Shopify eventWhen a Shopify store sends a webhook (an order created or paid, a product updated, stock changed)shopify
Nextcloud fileWhen files appear or change in a Nextcloud folder (checked on a schedule)file
Jira issueWhen Jira issues are created, or created or updated (checked on a schedule)issue
HubSpot recordWhen HubSpot records are created, or created or updated (checked on a schedule)record
Salesforce recordWhen Salesforce records are created, or created or updated (checked on a schedule)record
GLPI ticketWhen GLPI tickets are created, or created or updated (checked on a schedule)ticket
Intune deviceWhen Intune devices are enrolled, or become noncompliant (checked on a schedule)device

Triggers run the published version

Except for the Manual Trigger, a trigger starts runs only while the workflow is published, and those runs use the published version, not the draft you are editing. Press Run to try the draft. See Publishing and versions.

A workflow that starts with Called by a workflow runs its published version too, or its draft while it has never been published.

Rules

  • A workflow has one trigger. To start the same steps in two ways, make two workflows; to share steps between workflows, put them in a workflow that starts with Called by a workflow and run it from the others.
  • A trigger has no input and cannot be placed inside a loop.
  • Every other step must be reachable from the trigger. Unreachable steps get a warning.

pages.title: Manual Trigger
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when you press Run in the designer.
pages.html:
The Manual Trigger starts a run when you press Run in the designer's toolbar. It has no settings and sets no variables. Use it while building and testing, and for workflows you only start by hand.

Run uses the draft, so you can try your latest changes without publishing.

Note: Run also works with a Schedule Trigger: it starts one run right away, without waiting for the schedule.

pages.title: Schedule Trigger
pages.summary: Runs the published workflow at set times: an interval, daily, weekly, monthly or a cron expression.
pages.html:
The Schedule Trigger runs the workflow at the times you set, as long as the workflow is published. The schedule uses the installation's time zone.

Settings

SettingDescription
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: Every day. Required.
EveryDefault: 15. (Shown for some values of Run.)
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes. (Shown for some values of Run.)
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. (Shown for some values of Run.)
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00. (Shown for some values of Run.)
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1. (Shown for some values of Run.)
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30. (Shown for some values of Run.)

Examples

You wantSet
Every 15 minutesRun: At a regular interval, Every: 15, Units: Minutes
Every day at 07:30Run: Every day, At: 07:30
Every day at 09:00 and 18:00Run: Every day, At: 09:00, 18:00
Monday and Thursday at 09:00Run: Every week, On: Monday, Thursday, At: 09:00
On the 1st of each monthRun: Every month, On day: 1
Weekdays at 08:30Run: Advanced, Cron: 30 8 * * 1-5

With Every month, months that don't have the chosen day are skipped. For example, day 31 skips April.

Variables

VariableTypeDescription
schedule_timestringThe scheduled minute (ISO 8601)

Press Run in the designer to start one run right away, with the draft.

pages.title: Webhook
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when another system sends an HTTP request to the workflow's secret address.
pages.html:
A Webhook trigger gives the workflow its own address: https://<your Rail22>/hook/<token>. When another system sends an HTTP request to it, the published workflow runs with the request in a variable. The address is shown in the step's settings once the workflow is saved.

Warning: keep the address secret: anyone who has it can start the workflow. For more protection, set an Authentication method below.

Settings

SettingDescription
HTTP methodChoices: Any method; GET; POST; PUT; PATCH; DELETE. Default: POST. Required.
Content typeOf the request body (not checked for GET). Choices: Any; JSON (application/json); Web form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data); Plain text (text/*). Default: JSON (application/json). Required.
RespondChoices: When received (202, the workflow runs afterwards); When the workflow ends (200, with its state). Default: When received (202, the workflow runs afterwards). Required.
AuthenticationChoices: None (the secret URL only); Header with a secret value; Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer ...); Basic auth (username / password); HMAC-SHA256 signature of the body. Default: None (the secret URL only). Required.
Header nameHMAC: the header carries the hex signature (or sha256=<hex>). (Shown for some values of Authentication.)
Secret(Shown for some values of Authentication.)
Username(Shown for some values of Authentication.)
Password(Shown for some values of Authentication.)
Request variablee.g. {{ webhook.body }}, {{ webhook.query.id }}. Default: webhook. Required.

Authentication

MethodThe caller must send
NoneNothing: knowing the address is enough.
Header with a secret valueA header, named in Header name, with the Secret as its value.
Bearer tokenAuthorization: Bearer <secret>.
Basic authThe username and password (Authorization: Basic …).
HMAC-SHA256A header with the HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body, keyed with the secret: hex, or sha256=<hex>. Many services (GitHub, Shopify, Stripe-like APIs) sign their webhooks this way.

A request that fails authentication gets 401 and starts nothing. A mode without its secret refuses every request.

The answer

  • When received (default): the caller gets 202 at once, with {"execution": "<id>", "state": "accepted"}. The workflow runs afterwards.
  • When the workflow ends: the caller waits for the run to finish and gets 200 with {"execution": "<id>", "state": "end"} (or error, sleep…). Use this mode only for short workflows. The run is done by the daemon; one still running after 30 seconds is answered 202 with {"execution": "<id>", "state": "queued"}, and the daemon finishes it.

Requests to a workflow that is not published are refused. Request bodies are limited to 1 MB.

Variables

VariableTypeDescription
webhookobjectThe request: { method, path, url, query, headers, content_type, body, raw, ip, received_at }
webhook.methodstringThe HTTP method
webhook.pathstringThe path called (/hook/<token>)
webhook.urlstringThe full URL called, with the query string
webhook.queryobjectThe query string parameters, e.g. query.id
webhook.headersobjectLower-case name => value, e.g. headers["user-agent"] (without authorization, cookie and the secret header)
webhook.content_typestringThe content type of the body, without parameters
webhook.bodyanyThe decoded body (JSON or web form), else the body text
webhook.rawstringThe body text as received
webhook.ipstringThe caller address
webhook.received_atstringISO 8601

Example

curl -X POST https://app.example.com/hook/3f9c…e1 \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"order": 1042, "email": "ana@example.com"}'

In the workflow, {{ webhook.body.order }} is 1042 and {{ webhook.body.email }} is the address.

pages.title: Form
pages.summary: Publishes a form page; each submission starts the workflow with the answers.
pages.html:
A Form trigger gives the workflow a page with a form you design. Each time someone sends it, the published workflow runs with the answers. Project members also find the form under Forms in the sidebar.

Settings

SettingDescription
Who can fill it inChoices: Project members (logged in); Anyone with the link. Default: Project members (logged in). Required.
FormRequired.
ButtonDefault: Send.
Message after sendingDefault: Thank you, your answers were sent..
Answers variableThe answers by key; who sent them: <variable>_user. Default: form. Required.

The page's address is shown in the settings, at /form/<token>. It works once the workflow is published.

Designing the form

The Form setting opens the form designer. Add fields: text, e-mail, web address, long text, number, date, date & time, choice, checkbox, switch and hidden values. Titles, paragraphs, dividers and columns lay the form out. For each one, set its label, its key (the name of the answer in the variable), whether it is required, and its rules. A form needs at least one field.

With Who can fill it in set to Anyone with the link, people without a Rail22 user can fill it in, for example customers or suppliers. With Project members, they must sign in first.

Variables

VariableTypeDescription
formobjectThe answers of the form
form_userobjectWho sent the form (null: someone not logged in)
form_user.idstring
form_user.namestring
form_user.emailstring

For a field with the key amount, the answer is {{ form.amount }}. Who sent the form: {{ form_user.name }}, {{ form_user.email }}. With a public form and a visitor who is not signed in, form_user is empty.

Tip: combine a Form with a Human task for approvals. The form collects the request, and the task asks someone to approve it.

pages.title: Chat
pages.summary: Gives the workflow a chat page in the app, and optionally an embeddable link: each message starts a run, and the workflow answers with Reply to chat.
pages.html:
A Chat trigger lets people talk to a workflow: an agent. Published, it has a chat page in the app, listed under Agents for the people allowed, and optionally a link to embed in another site. Each message starts a run of the published version; the workflow answers with Reply to chat. For an agent that remembers what was said, use an AI step with Continue the conversation. The guide An IT helpdesk agent builds one.

Settings

SettingDescription
PageThe chat page's address. It works once the workflow is published.
Users allowed, Roles allowedWho may talk to it, among the project's members. No user and no role: any project member, Participants too.
DescriptionWhat this agent is for: shown under its name in Agents.
GreetingShown before the first message. Default: Hello, how can I help?
Embeddable pageA page anyone with its link can use, without signing in. Default: off.
Embed linkThe page's address, for an iframe. Its token is made when you save. For a new token: turn Embeddable page off, save, turn it on, save, publish.
Sites that may embed itAddresses separated by commas, such as https://www.example.com. Empty: any site.
Message for a Run in the designerUnder Advanced. What message holds when you press Run. Default: Hello.

Variables

VariableDescription
messageWhat the person wrote, or the value of the button they chose.
conversation{ id, channel, turn, title, history, summary }. channel: app, embed, email or teams. turn: the number of this message. history: the earlier turns, the newest 20, as [ { role, text, at } ]. summary: the older turns summarized, when an AI step has done it.
user{ id, name, email }, who wrote it. A guest of the embedded page has no id and no email.

How a conversation runs

  • One message at a time: while a run answers, or waits for an approval, the page does not send another. Starting a new conversation is always possible.
  • The page shows the answers as they are sent, and says so when the run waits for a person's approval. Answers are not streamed word by word: they appear when Reply to chat runs.
  • A run that fails, or ends without Reply to chat, leaves a short notice on the page. What went wrong is in the run, under Executions. A workflow with no Reply to chat step gets a warning in the designer.
  • Press Run to try the draft: it uses the test message, and its answers go to the run's log, not to anyone.
  • Run again on a conversation's run sends nothing to the person and does not change the conversation, but its tools run again, Remember included.

Embedding it

<iframe src="https://your-server/chat/<embed token>" style="width: 400px; height: 600px; border: 0"></iframe>

Visitors are guests. Their conversation is kept in their browser with a key the server holds only as a hash: nobody else reaches it through the page. Each address may send 60 messages an hour.

Note: anyone with the link can use what the agent can use. Before you turn this on, give the AI step only tools that are safe for strangers, keep approvals on for what changes something, and set its Guardrails and the account's budget: every message costs a call to the model.

pages.title: File upload
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when a file is uploaded to the project's Files.
pages.html:
The File upload trigger runs the published workflow each time a file is uploaded to the project's Files. You can limit it to some file types, for example only PDF and Excel files.

Settings

SettingDescription
Only these file typesFiles uploaded to this project's Files start the workflow once it is published; none chosen: any file.
File variablee.g. {{ file.id }}, {{ file.filename }}. Default: file. Required.

Variables

VariableTypeDescription
fileobjectThe uploaded file: { id, filename, extension, type, size, uploaded_by: { id, name, email } }
file.idstring
file.filenamestring
file.extensionstringLower case, e.g. pdf
file.typestringE.g. PDF, Excel, Image
file.sizenumberBytes
file.uploaded_byobject

Pass {{ file.id }} to the steps that take project files: an AI step's Files, FTP / SFTP Upload, Google Drive or OneDrive upload, email attachments.

pages.title: Email (inbound)
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when an email arrives at the workflow's own address.
pages.html:
The Email (inbound) trigger gives the workflow an email address. Each message sent to it starts the published workflow, with the message, including its attachments, in a variable.

Note: this trigger is available when the installation receives mail (see Inbound mail). Otherwise it is not offered, and a workflow that already has one cannot be published. Addresses start with your account's email prefix, set under Account settings → Inbound mail.

Settings

SettingDescription
AddressMail sent here starts the workflow once it is published (the start is your account's email prefix: Settings, Inbound mail).
Accept mail only fromOne sender address or @domain per line (the envelope sender); empty: anyone.
Save attachments as project filesDefault: on.
Keep conversationsA reply to the workflow's answer continues the same conversation; Reply to chat answers by email. Default: off.
Message variablee.g. {{ mail.subject }}, {{ mail.text }}. Default: mail. Required.

Variables

The message variable (default mail) holds:

FieldDescription
mail.from, mail.from_nameThe sender's address and name.
mail.to, mail.cc, mail.reply_toLists of addresses.
mail.subjectThe subject.
mail.text, mail.htmlThe text and HTML bodies.
mail.dateWhen it was sent (ISO 8601).
mail.attachmentsA list of { filename, contentType, size, disposition, file }. file is the id of the saved project file.
mail.attachment_count, mail.attachment_filesThe number of attachments, and their file ids.
mail.message_id, mail.in_reply_to, mail.referencesFor threading replies.
mail.headersAll headers, lower-case names, e.g. {{ mail.headers["x-priority"] }}.
mail.recipientThe address it was sent to.

Conversations by email

With Keep conversations on, the run also gets the variables message (the text, without what it quotes), conversation and user, as with the Chat trigger. Reply to chat answers the sender from the app's address; a reply comes back to this trigger's address and continues the same conversation, by its In-Reply-To and References.

  • A reply continues a conversation only when it comes from the same sender. Someone else who knows a message's id gets a conversation of their own.
  • Automatic messages are not answered: bounces, out-of-office answers (Auto-Submitted, Precedence: bulk). The answers are marked Auto-Submitted too, and a conversation takes at most 20 messages an hour: agents do not write to each other without end.

Note: email's sender can be forged. Who the message says it is from decides whose conversation and whose long-term memories it reaches, so use Accept mail only from, and keep approvals on for what changes something.

To read an existing mailbox instead (IMAP, Gmail, Microsoft 365), use a Schedule Trigger followed by Read emails (IMAP).

pages.title: Teams message
pages.summary: Talk to a workflow in Microsoft Teams: a message in a chat of the credential's account starts a run, and Reply to chat answers there.
pages.html:
Teams message lets people talk to an agent in Microsoft Teams. It checks on a schedule (every minute by default) for new messages in the chats of a Microsoft Teams credential's account. Each new message starts a run of the published version, and Reply to chat answers in the same chat, as that account. Each chat is one conversation.

Settings

SettingDescription
Teams credentialThe agent reads and answers as this account. Use an account of its own: the trigger ignores that account's own messages, so a person using it would get no answer. Required.
ChatA chat id (the Teams step's List my chats gives them). Empty: every chat of the account, the 50 with the latest messages.
ScheduleHow often it checks. Default: every minute.

Variables

VariableDescription
messageWhat the person wrote, or the value of the button they chose.
conversation{ id, channel, turn, title, history, summary }. channel: app, embed, email or teams. turn: the number of this message. history: the earlier turns, the newest 20, as [ { role, text, at } ]. summary: the older turns summarized, when an AI step has done it.
user{ id, name, email }, who wrote it. A guest of the embedded page has no id and no email.

And teams: { chat, message_id }, where it was written.

Good to know

  • The first check only notes where it starts: earlier messages are not answered.
  • Messages of apps and system events are not read.
  • Reply to chat's buttons become a line of text: the person answers with one of them.
  • The credential needs the Chat.Read permission. A Teams credential connected before this trigger existed must be connected again.
  • Chats only: reading channel messages takes a permission only an administrator can consent to, which every Teams credential would then have to ask for.

pages.title: Called by a workflow
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when another workflow of the project runs it, or an AI step uses it as a tool, with the inputs it declares, and hands back its outputs.
pages.html:
Called by a workflow makes a workflow reusable: other workflows of the project start it with the Run a workflow step, give it its inputs, and get its outputs back when it ends. Use it for steps several workflows need, such as create a customer in the CRM or send the approval email, or to split a large workflow into parts.

Settings

The settings are the workflow's contract: what it takes in and what it gives back.

SettingDescription
InputsWhat the calling workflow gives. Rows of: Name (a variable name), Type (Text, Number, Yes / no, List, Object, Any), Required, Default. Each input becomes a variable of the run.
OutputsRows of: Variable. The variables handed back to the calling workflow when this one ends; one that was never set is handed back as null.
Description for agentsOptional: what it does and when to use it, for the AI steps that may run it as a tool. At most 2000 characters.

The inputs

  • A value of another type is converted when it can be: the text 12 for a Number, yes / no or true / false for Yes / no, a JSON text for a List or an Object. Otherwise the run fails with, for example, the input `tags`: a list is expected.
  • An input not given (or empty) takes its default. A required input that is missing fails the run.
  • The calling step's editor lists the inputs, and warns when a required one is missing.

Used by an AI step

An AI step can run the workflow as a tool: choose it in the AI step's Workflows. The model sees it as wf_ and the workflow's name, with the Description for agents as the tool's description, the inputs as its arguments (their types, the required ones), and gets back { ok, state, execution, outputs, error }.

Write the description for the model: what the workflow does, when to use it and when not to, and what its outputs mean. For example: Asks the SOC team to approve isolating an endpoint, then isolates it. Use it only for an endpoint that is clearly compromised. The approval takes time: the result's state is sleep while it waits.

A workflow that pauses (a Wait, a Human task) goes on by itself; the model gets state sleep and not its outputs. The AI step can also ask a person before running it: Workflows that ask for approval, see AI steps. See Building an agent.

Variables

VariableTypeDescription
each inputas declaredThe value given, or the default
callerobjectThe calling workflow: { workflow, name, execution }; null when started with Run in the designer

Trying it

Press Run in the designer to run it alone: the inputs take their defaults (a required input without a default fails the run). Its runs appear in its own Executions panel, each with a link to the run that called it.

pages.title: GravityZone event
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when Bitdefender GravityZone sends events: detections, incidents, tasks, endpoint changes.
pages.html:
The GravityZone event trigger starts the workflow when Bitdefender GravityZone's Event Push Service sends events: a malware detection, a new incident, a finished task, an endpoint moved. The step has its own address, https://<your Rail22>/gravityzone/<token>, and a secret that GravityZone sends with each request.

Connecting

With Connect on, publishing the workflow sets the push service of the credential's key to the step's address, with its secret and the event types chosen. Unpublishing turns the push service off, if it still points to this workflow. The result shows in a message after publishing.

Warning: a GravityZone API key has one push service. Connecting replaces the key's current push settings, such as a SIEM's. Use a key of its own for the trigger.

The key needs the Push API. GravityZone must be able to reach Rail22's address over HTTPS: for GravityZone Cloud, the address must be public.

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialThe console whose events start the workflow. Required.
ConnectSet GravityZone's push service to this address when published, off when unpublished. It replaces the key's current push settings. Default: on.
Event typesNone chosen: all. Choices: Antimalware; Advanced Threat Control; HyperDetect; Advanced Anti-Exploit; Ransomware activity; Sandbox Analyzer detection; Network Attack Defense; Firewall; Antiphishing; User / Content Control; Data Protection; Exchange malware; Exchange license usage limit; Exchange user credentials; New incident; New extended incident; Incident status changed; Incident assignee changed; Incident priority changed; Incident note created; Incident note updated; Incident note deleted; Task status; Product modules status; Agent installed; Agent uninstalled; Product registration; Hardware ID change; Endpoint moved in; Endpoint moved out; Troubleshooting activity; Security Server status; Security Server overloaded; Update server outdated; Cloud AD integration; Partner changed; Integrations hub status.
RunsChoices: One run per event; One run per batch of events. Default: One run per event. Required.
Event variablee.g. {{ gz.module }}, {{ gz.computer_name }}. Default: gz. Required.

The Address and the Secret are made when the step is added, and can't be changed.

The variable

With One run per event, the variable is the event as GravityZone sends it. Its module is the event type (av, new-incident, …). Its other fields depend on the type, such as {{ gz.computer_name }} or {{ gz.malware_name }}. Rail22 adds received_at.

With One run per batch of events, the variable is { events, count, received_at }. Use a Loop over {{ gz.events }}.

Events of types not chosen are left out. A request with more than 500 events starts 500 runs, and the rest are logged as left out.

Example

Event types Antimalware and New incident, then a Switch on {{ gz.module }}: a ticket in a Data Table for detections, the GravityZone Incidents step for new incidents.

pages.title: Veeam event
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when Veeam Backup & Replication job sessions end with the results chosen: failed, warning, success.
pages.html:
The Veeam event trigger starts the workflow when job sessions of a Veeam Backup & Replication server end with the results you choose: Failed, Warning or Success, of one job or of every job.

How it works

Veeam doesn't call other systems, so the trigger checks the server on its schedule, every 5 minutes by default, while the workflow is published. Each check reads the sessions that ended since the previous one, and starts a run for each new one. Rail22 remembers where it stopped: a session never starts two runs, and a check that fails is simply tried again at the next one.

The first check after publishing only notes the time: sessions that ended before don't start runs. Press Run in the designer to try the workflow with the newest session that matches.

Settings

SettingDescription
Veeam credentialThe backup server whose sessions start the workflow. Required.
Sessions ended withChoices: Failed; Warning; Success. Default: Failed, Warning. Required.
JobIts name (exactly) or its id; empty: every job.
RunsChoices: One run per session; One run per check with sessions. Default: One run per session. Required.
Session variablee.g. {{ veeam.name }}, {{ veeam.result.result }}, {{ veeam.result.message }}. Default: veeam. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 5.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per session, the variable is the session as Veeam gives it: {{ veeam.name }} (the job), {{ veeam.jobId }}, {{ veeam.endTime }}, {{ veeam.result.result }} and {{ veeam.result.message }}.

With One run per check with sessions, it is { sessions, count }. Use a Loop over {{ veeam.sessions }}.

One check starts at most 200 runs. The rest wait for the next check.

Example

Results Failed: a ticket in a Data Table with the job and the message, a Human task asking whether to retry, then Veeam Jobs Retry a job with Job {{ veeam.jobId }}.

pages.title: FortiGate event
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when a FortiGate automation stitch sends an event: a log, an IOC, an HA failover, a configuration change.
pages.html:
The FortiGate event trigger starts the workflow when a FortiGate automation stitch calls it. You choose the event on the FortiGate: an event log ID (such as a failed administrator login), a compromised host (IOC), an HA failover, a configuration change, high CPU, a license about to expire. The stitch's webhook action sends the log to the step's address, https://<your Rail22>/fortigate/<token>, with a secret.

Setting it up

  1. Add the trigger to the workflow. Its settings show the FortiGate setup (CLI): the commands that make the webhook action, with the step's address and secret.
  2. Paste them in the FortiGate's CLI console.
  3. On the FortiGate, under Security Fabric > Automation, create a stitch: choose its trigger, and the action rail22-….
  4. Publish the workflow.

The FortiGate must be able to reach Rail22's address over HTTPS.

Settings

SettingDescription
Event variablee.g. {{ fgt.logid }}, {{ fgt.srcip }}, {{ fgt.devname }}. Default: fgt. Required.

The Address, FortiGate setup and Secret are made when the step is added, and can't be changed.

The variable

The variable is the log the FortiGate sent (%%log%%), with its fields: {{ fgt.logid }}, {{ fgt.type }}, {{ fgt.subtype }}, {{ fgt.level }}, {{ fgt.devname }}, {{ fgt.srcip }}, {{ fgt.msg }} and the others of that log. Rail22 adds received_at. A body that is not JSON is given as {{ fgt.raw }}.

Example

A stitch on the event log ID of failed administrator logins: a If on the source address, then FortiGate Banned IPs Ban IPs with {{ fgt.srcip }}, and a message to the team.

pages.title: Checkmk problem
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when Checkmk reports a new problem (a host down, a service critical), and optionally when it clears.
pages.html:
The Checkmk problem trigger starts the workflow when Checkmk reports a new problem: a host DOWN or UNREACH, a service CRIT (or WARN), of one host or every host. It can also start a run when a problem clears, so a workflow can close what it opened.

How it works

The trigger checks the site on its schedule, every 2 minutes by default, while the workflow is published. Nothing has to be set up in Checkmk. Each check reads the current problems and compares them with the previous check's:

  • A problem starts a run when it is new, or when its state changed (a WARN that turns CRIT).
  • Acknowledged problems and problems in a downtime start no run, unless chosen. They are not taken as cleared either.
  • With When it clears too, a problem that started a run and is gone starts a run with event recovery.
  • The first check after publishing only notes what is already wrong: those problems start no run, and no recovery when they clear.

Press Run in the designer to try the workflow with a current problem.

Settings

SettingDescription
Checkmk credentialThe site whose problems start the workflow. Required.
HostIts name; empty: every host.
ServicesHosts: DOWN and UNREACH. Choices: WARN and worse; CRIT and worse. Default: CRIT and worse. Required.
Also acknowledged problemsDefault: off.
Also problems in a downtimeDefault: off.
When it clears tooA run when a problem that started one is gone (event: recovery). Default: off.
RunsChoices: One run per problem; One run per check with problems. Default: One run per problem. Required.
Problem variablee.g. {{ cmk.host_name }}, {{ cmk.service }}, {{ cmk.stateText }}, {{ cmk.event }}. Default: cmk. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 2.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per problem, the variable is the problem: {{ cmk.event }} (problem or recovery), {{ cmk.kind }} (host or service), {{ cmk.host_name }}, {{ cmk.service }}, {{ cmk.stateText }}, {{ cmk.output }} (the check's output) and {{ cmk.since }}.

With One run per check with problems, it is { problems, count }. One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check.

Example

A Switch on {{ cmk.event }}: for a problem, a ticket in a Data Table and Checkmk Acknowledge & Downtime with the ticket's number; for a recovery, the ticket closed.

pages.title: Zabbix problem
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when Zabbix reports a new problem, and optionally when it is resolved.
pages.html:
The Zabbix problem trigger starts the workflow when Zabbix reports a new problem of a severity and worse, of hosts or host groups, with tags. It can also start a run when a problem is resolved, so a workflow can close what it opened.

How it works

The trigger checks the server on its schedule, every 2 minutes by default, while the workflow is published. Nothing has to be set up in Zabbix. Each check reads the current problems and compares them with the previous check's:

  • A problem starts a run when it is new, or when its severity changed.
  • Acknowledged and suppressed problems (in a maintenance) start no run, unless chosen. They are not taken as resolved either.
  • With When it is resolved too, a problem that started a run and is gone starts a run with event recovery.
  • The first check after publishing only notes what is already wrong: those problems start no run, and no recovery when they are resolved.

Press Run in the designer to try the workflow with the newest current problem.

Settings

SettingDescription
Zabbix credentialThe server whose problems start the workflow. Required.
SeverityChoices: All severities; Information and worse; Warning and worse; Average and worse; High and worse; Disaster. Default: Average and worse. Required.
HostsTheir technical names, separated by commas; empty: every host.
Host groupsTheir names, separated by commas; empty: every group.
Tagstag=value, separated by commas; all must match.
Also acknowledged problemsDefault: off.
Also suppressed problemsIn a maintenance. Default: off.
When it is resolved tooA run when a problem that started one is gone (event: recovery). Default: off.
RunsChoices: One run per problem; One run per check with problems. Default: One run per problem. Required.
Problem variablee.g. {{ zbx.name }}, {{ zbx.host }}, {{ zbx.severityText }}, {{ zbx.eventid }}, {{ zbx.event }}. Default: zbx. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 2.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per problem, the variable is the problem: {{ zbx.event }} (problem or recovery), {{ zbx.eventid }}, {{ zbx.name }}, {{ zbx.severityText }}, {{ zbx.host }} (the technical name), {{ zbx.hostName }}, {{ zbx.tags }}, {{ zbx.opdata }} and {{ zbx.since }}.

With One run per check with problems, it is { problems, count }. One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check.

Example

A Switch on {{ zbx.event }}: for a problem, a ticket in a Data Table and Zabbix Acknowledge & Maintenance acknowledging {{ zbx.eventid }} with the ticket's number; for a recovery, the ticket closed.

pages.title: Wazuh alert
pages.summary: Starts the workflow on new Wazuh alerts of a rule level and worse.
pages.html:
The Wazuh alert trigger starts the workflow on new alerts of a rule level and worse, of agents, rules, groups, MITRE techniques and a query.

How it works

The trigger reads the Wazuh indexer on its schedule, every 2 minutes by default, while the workflow is published. Nothing has to be set up in Wazuh, but the credential needs the indexer.

  • The first check after publishing only notes the time of Wazuh's newest alert: earlier alerts never start a run.
  • Each later check starts a run for each new alert that matches, oldest first, and each alert only once.
  • Alerts reach the indexer a little late and out of order, so each check also looks back 2 minutes. An alert that reaches the indexer later than that is missed.
  • One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check. Choose the level and rules so that a flood of alerts does not become a flood of runs, or use One run per check with alerts.

Press Run in the designer to try the workflow with the newest matching alert.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialWith the indexer: the alerts are read from it. Required.
Level and worseOf the rule, 0 to 16; empty: every level. Default: 10.
AgentsTheir ids or names, separated by commas; empty: every agent.
RulesTheir ids, separated by commas; empty: every rule.
Rule groupsSeparated by commas, any of them, e.g. authentication_failed; empty: every group.
MITRE techniquesTheir ids, separated by commas, e.g. T1110; empty: all.
QueryIn Lucene syntax, e.g. data.srcip:"10.0.0.5" AND NOT agent.name:web*.
RunsChoices: One run per alert; One run per check with alerts. Default: One run per alert. Required.
Alert variablee.g. {{ alert.rule.description }}, {{ alert.rule.level }}, {{ alert.agent.name }}, {{ alert.data.srcip }}. Default: alert. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 2.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per alert, the variable is the alert, as Wazuh wrote it, with _id and _index: {{ alert.rule.level }}, {{ alert.rule.description }}, {{ alert.rule.id }}, {{ alert.rule.groups }}, {{ alert.agent.name }}, {{ alert.agent.id }}, {{ alert.data.srcip }}, {{ alert.full_log }} and {{ alert.timestamp }}. Which data fields it has depends on the rule's decoder.

With One run per check with alerts, it is { alerts, count }.

An alert's content comes from the logs of the monitored machines, so an attacker can influence it. Check values such as {{ alert.data.srcip }} before a workflow acts on them.

Example

On level 10 and worse: Wazuh Inventory reads the packages of {{ alert }}, an AI step summarizes the alert and what it found, and Send email sends it to the on-call address.

pages.title: VMware alarm
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when a vCenter alarm turns red (or yellow) on a VM, host, datastore or any object, and optionally when it clears.
pages.html:
The VMware alarm trigger starts the workflow when an alarm of a vCenter Server is triggered: red (alert), or yellow (warning) and red, on a VM, host, datastore, cluster or any object. It can also start a run when an alarm clears, so a workflow can close what it opened. It uses VI/JSON: vCenter Server 8.0 Update 1 or later.

How it works

vCenter calls no webhook: the trigger checks it on its schedule, every 2 minutes by default, while the workflow is published. Nothing has to be set up in vCenter. Each check reads the alarms triggered now and compares them with the previous check's:

  • An alarm starts a run when it is new, or when its status changed (a yellow alarm that turns red).
  • Acknowledged alarms start no run, unless chosen. They are not taken as cleared either.
  • With When it clears too, an alarm that started a run and is gone starts a run with event recovery.
  • The first check after publishing only notes what is already triggered: those alarms start no run, and no recovery when they clear.

Press Run in the designer to try the workflow with an alarm triggered now.

Settings

SettingDescription
VMware credentialThe vCenter whose alarms start the workflow. Required.
StatusChoices: Yellow (warning) and red; Red (alert) only. Default: Red (alert) only. Required.
OfChoices: Any object; VMs; Hosts; Datastores; Clusters; Datacenters; Networks. Default: Any object.
RunsChoices: One run per alarm; One run per check with alarms. Default: One run per alarm. Required.
Also acknowledged alarmsDefault: off.
When it clears tooA run when an alarm that started one is gone (event: recovery). Default: off.
Alarm variablee.g. {{ alarm.entity.name }}. Default: alarm. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 2.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per alarm, the variable is the alarm: {{ alarm.event }} (alarm or recovery), {{ alarm.alarm.name }} (such as Virtual machine CPU usage), {{ alarm.entity.name }}, {{ alarm.entity.type }} (such as VirtualMachine), {{ alarm.entity.id }}, {{ alarm.status }} (red or yellow), {{ alarm.time }} and {{ alarm.key }}.

With One run per check with alarms, it is { alarms, count }. One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check.

Example

A Switch on {{ alarm.event }}: for an alarm, a ticket in a Data Table and VMware Alarms Acknowledge an alarm with {{ alarm }}; for a recovery, the ticket closed.

pages.title: Proxmox task
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when a Proxmox VE task ends, such as a failed backup.
pages.html:
The Proxmox task trigger starts the workflow when tasks of a Proxmox VE cluster end: failed ones, or every one, of the types chosen (such as vzdump, the backups) and of a node or any. A failed backup can open a ticket, retry the backup or warn someone.

How it works

Proxmox calls no webhook: the trigger checks the cluster's recent tasks on its schedule, every 5 minutes by default, while the workflow is published. Nothing has to be set up in Proxmox. Each task that ended since the previous check and matches starts a run, once. The first check after publishing only notes the time: tasks that ended before start no run.

Proxmox keeps the recent tasks of each node (the last few hundred), so a schedule of minutes misses none.

Press Run in the designer to try the workflow with the newest matching task.

Settings

SettingDescription
Proxmox credentialThe cluster whose tasks start the workflow. Required.
Tasks that endedChoices: Failed; Every result (OK, warnings, failed). Default: Failed. Required.
TypesComma separated, e.g. vzdump, qmigrate; empty: any. Default: vzdump.
NodeEmpty: every node.
RunsChoices: One run per task; One run per check with tasks. Default: One run per task. Required.
Task variablee.g. {{ task.type }}, {{ task.status }}. Default: task. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 5.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per task, the variable is the task: {{ task.type }} (such as vzdump, qmigrate), {{ task.id }} (what it ran on, such as the VMID), {{ task.node }}, {{ task.status }} (OK, WARNINGS: 1 or the error), {{ task.failed }}, {{ task.user }}, {{ task.start }}, {{ task.end }}, {{ task.upid }} and {{ task.log }}, the last 20 lines of its log.

With One run per check with tasks, it is { tasks, count }. One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check.

Example

Failed backups: the trigger with the type vzdump, then Proxmox Backups Back up a guest now for {{ task.id }} with On error set to continue; on its error output, Send email with {{ task.log }}.

pages.title: Hyper-V VM state
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when a Hyper-V VM stops running, or its replication health turns Warning or Critical, and optionally when it recovers.
pages.html:
The Hyper-V VM state trigger starts the workflow when a VM of a Hyper-V host stops running (or on any change of its state), or when its replication health turns Warning or Critical. It can also start a run when the VM recovers: running again, replication Normal.

How it works

Hyper-V calls no webhook: the trigger reads the VMs on its schedule, every 2 minutes by default, while the workflow is published, and compares them with the previous check:

  • With It stops running, a VM that was Running and is now Off, Saved, Paused or in a Critical state starts a run (event stopped). With Its state changes, every change does (state).
  • States a VM passes through (Starting, Stopping, Saving…) are not changes: the trigger waits for the next settled state.
  • With Replication health too, a VM whose replication turns Warning or Critical starts a run (replication).
  • With When it recovers too, a VM that started a run and is running again, or back to Normal, starts a run (recovery).
  • The first check after publishing only notes the VMs. A VM added later is noted at its first check.

Press Run in the designer to try the workflow with a VM that is not running.

Settings

SettingDescription
Hyper-V credentialThe host whose VMs start the workflow. Required.
VMsNames, comma separated; * any text; empty: every VM.
When a VMChoices: It stops running; Its state changes. Default: It stops running. Required.
RunsChoices: One run per event; One run per check with events. Default: One run per event. Required.
Replication health tooWhen it turns Warning or Critical. Default: off.
When it recovers tooRunning again, replication Normal (event: recovery). Default: off.
Event variablee.g. {{ hv.vm.name }}, {{ hv.event }}. Default: hv. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 2.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per event, the variable is the event: {{ hv.event }} (stopped, state, replication or recovery), {{ hv.vm.name }}, {{ hv.vm.id }}, {{ hv.from }} and {{ hv.to }} (the state or replication health before and now), {{ hv.state }}, {{ hv.replicationHealth }} and {{ hv.time }}.

With One run per check with events, it is { events, count }. One check starts at most 200 runs.

Example

A VM that should always run: a Switch on {{ hv.event }}; for stopped, Hyper-V VMs Start for {{ hv.vm.id }} and an email; for replication, a ticket.

pages.title: Shopify event
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when a Shopify store sends a webhook: an order created or paid, a product updated, stock changed.
pages.html:
The Shopify event trigger starts the workflow when a Shopify store sends a webhook of the topics you choose, such as Order created, Order paid, Product updated or Stock level changed. Shopify sends it to the step's address, https://<your Rail22>/shopify/<token>, and signs it: Rail22 checks the signature, so only the store can start the workflow.

Setting it up

  1. Add the trigger, choose a Shopify credential (with its client secret) and the topics.
  2. Publish the workflow. With Connect on, Rail22 subscribes the address to each topic. Unpublishing deletes the subscriptions, and a topic no longer chosen is unsubscribed when you publish again.

The app needs the read scope of each topic, such as read_orders for the order topics. Shopify must be able to reach Rail22's address over HTTPS.

Webhooks made by hand in the store's admin (Settings > Notifications > Webhooks) work too: leave Connect off, give the step's address there, and copy the key shown on that page ("Your webhooks will be signed with …") into Signing key.

Settings

SettingDescription
Shopify credentialThe store; its client secret checks the webhooks' signature.
ConnectSubscribe this address to the topics when published, unsubscribe when unpublished. Default: on.
TopicsThe events that start the workflow (the app needs the matching read scopes, e.g. read_orders). Choices: Order created; Order paid; Order updated; Order fulfilled; Order partially fulfilled; Order cancelled; Order edited; Order deleted; Refund created; Fulfillment created; Fulfillment updated; Draft order created; Checkout created; Product created; Product updated; Product deleted; Stock level changed; Customer created; Customer updated; Customer deleted; App uninstalled. Default: Order created. Required.
Signing keyOnly for webhooks made in Shopify's admin (Settings > Notifications > Webhooks: "Your webhooks will be signed with …"); empty: the credential's client secret.
Event variablee.g. {{ shopify.topic }}, {{ shopify.data.name }}, {{ shopify.data.line_items }}. Default: shopify. Required.

The Address is made when the step is added, and can't be changed.

The variable

VariableDescription
shopify.topicThe topic, such as orders/create.
shopify.shopThe store, my-store.myshopify.com.
shopify.dataWhat Shopify sent, with its own field names: an order has id, admin_graphql_api_id, name, email, total_price, financial_status, line_items, customer, shipping_address, …
shopify.event_id, shopify.webhook_idShopify's IDs of the event and of this delivery.
shopify.api_version, shopify.triggered_at, shopify.received_atThe API version of the payload; when Shopify sent it; when Rail22 received it.

The payload can be given to the Shopify steps as it is: Get an order with order {{ shopify.data }} reads the order in full.

Note: Shopify may deliver an event more than once. When a run must not happen twice (an invoice, a message to the customer), keep {{ shopify.event_id }}, for example in a data table, and skip the ones already seen. Topics not chosen are answered and start nothing. A store other than the credential's is refused.

Example

On Order paid: Shopify Orders Get an order with {{ shopify.data }}, then the invoice through your invoicing integration, then Add tags invoiced.

pages.title: Nextcloud file
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when files appear or change in a Nextcloud folder (checked on a schedule).
pages.html:
The Nextcloud file trigger starts the workflow when files appear in a Nextcloud folder, or, if you choose, when they change. It reads the folder on its schedule, every 5 minutes by default, as the credential's user. Nothing has to be set up in Nextcloud, and no administrator is needed: the folder can be one shared with that user.

The first check only notes the files already there. From then on, each new file (or changed one) starts a run. A file changed is one whose content changed since the last check (its etag).

Settings

SettingDescription
Nextcloud credentialIts user's files are watched. Required.
FolderA path in the files, e.g. /Scans; empty: the top.
SubfoldersLevels below the folder (0: only it). Default: 0.
NamesPatterns, e.g. *.pdf, invoice-*; empty: all.
Start onChoices: New files; New or changed files. Default: New files. Required.
RunsChoices: One run per file; One run per check with files. Default: One run per file. Required.
File variablee.g. {{ file.path }}, {{ file.name }}, {{ file.size }}. Default: file. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 5.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per file, the variable is the file, as Nextcloud Files lists it: {{ file.path }}, {{ file.name }}, {{ file.folder }}, {{ file.size }}, {{ file.modified }}, {{ file.contentType }}, plus {{ file.change }}: new or changed.

With One run per check with files, it is { files, count }. Use a Loop over {{ file.files }}.

One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check. A check reads at most 10,000 files: for larger folders, watch a subfolder.

Example

Scanned invoices: a scanner saves to /Scans; the trigger, with names *.pdf, runs Nextcloud Files Download a file with {{ file }}, an AI step that reads the invoice, a row in a Data Table, then Move / rename to /Scans/Done/.

pages.title: Jira issue
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when Jira issues are created, or created or updated (checked on a schedule).
pages.html:
The Jira issue trigger starts the workflow when issues are created (or, if you choose, created or updated) that a JQL filter finds, such as project = OPS AND priority in (High, Highest). It searches on its schedule, every 2 minutes by default, as the credential's user. Nothing has to be set up in Jira, and no Jira administrator is needed.

The first check only notes the time. From then on, each issue created (or changed) since starts a run, the oldest first.

Settings

SettingDescription
Jira credentialIts user must see the issues. Required.
JQL filterWhich issues, e.g. project = OPS AND priority in (High, Highest); empty: all the user sees. Its ORDER BY is not used.
Start onChoices: Issues created; Issues created or updated. Default: Issues created. Required.
RunsChoices: One run per issue; One run per check with issues. Default: One run per issue. Required.
Issue variablee.g. {{ issue.key }}, {{ issue.summary }}, {{ issue.priority }}, {{ issue.url }}. Default: issue. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 2.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per issue, the variable is the issue, as Jira Issues gives it: {{ issue.key }}, {{ issue.summary }}, {{ issue.status }}, {{ issue.priority }}, {{ issue.assignee.displayName }}, {{ issue.url }}, {{ issue.description }}, {{ issue.fields }}, plus {{ issue.event }}: created or updated.

With One run per check with issues, it is { issues, count }. Use a Loop over {{ issue.issues }}.

One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check. With Issues created or updated, an issue changed several times between two checks starts one run. A change made by the workflow itself (a comment, a status) is a change too: filter those out in the JQL (such as AND updatedBy != currentUser() where your Jira has it) or with an If, so the workflow does not start itself again.

Example

Urgent issues to the on-call channel: the filter project = OPS AND priority = Highest, then a message with {{ issue.key }}: {{ issue.summary }} and {{ issue.url }} through Microsoft Teams or Nextcloud Talk.

pages.title: HubSpot record
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when HubSpot records are created, or created or updated (checked on a schedule).
pages.html:
The HubSpot record trigger starts the workflow when records of one type (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, a custom object) are created, or, if you choose, created or updated, that its filters find, such as lifecyclestage = lead. It searches on its schedule, every 5 minutes by default, with the credential's token. Nothing has to be set up in HubSpot.

The first check only notes the time. From then on, each record created (or changed) since starts a run, the oldest first.

Settings

SettingDescription
HubSpot credentialRequired.
RecordsChoices: Contacts; Companies; Deals; Tickets; A custom object. Default: Contacts. Required.
Custom objectIts type ID (2-1234567) or name.
FiltersWhich records, one per line (at most 5), as HubSpot Records' search: e.g. lifecyclestage = lead; empty: all.
Start onChoices: Records created; Records created or updated. Default: Records created. Required.
RunsChoices: One run per record; One run per check with records. Default: One run per record. Required.
Record variablee.g. {{ record.email }}, {{ record.dealname }}, {{ record.url }}. Default: record. Required.
RunChoices: At a regular interval; Every day; Every week; Every month; Advanced (cron expression). Default: At a regular interval. Required.
EveryDefault: 5.
UnitsChoices: Minutes; Hours; Days. Default: Minutes.
OnChoices: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday. Default: Monday.
AtHH:MM; several times separated by commas, e.g. 09:00, 18:00. Default: 09:00.
On dayMonths without this day are skipped. Default: 1.
Cron expressionminute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, e.g. "30 8 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 08:30.

The variable

With One run per record, the variable is the record, as HubSpot Records gives it: {{ record.id }}, {{ record.url }}, its properties ({{ record.email }}, {{ record.dealname }}, …), plus {{ record.event }}: created or updated. The usual properties of the type are read; for others, use Get a record with {{ record }}.

With One run per check with records, it is { records, count }. Use a Loop over {{ record.records }}.

One check starts at most 200 runs; the rest wait for the next check. With Records created or updated, a record changed several times between two checks starts one run, and a change the workflow itself makes is a change too: filter those out with an If so the workflow does not start itself again.

Example

New deals to the sales channel: deals, the filter amount >= 10000, then a message with {{ record.dealname }}, {{ record.amount }} and {{ record.url }} through Microsoft Teams.

pages.title: Salesforce record
pages.summary: Starts the workflow when Salesforce records are created, or created or updated (checked on a schedule).
pages.html:
The Salesforce record trigger starts the workflow when records of one object are created, or, if you choose, created or updated, that a SOQL condition finds, such as LeadSource = 'Web'. It queries on its schedule, every 2 minutes by default, as the app's run-as user. Nothing has to be set up in Salesforce beyond the app.

The first check only notes the time. From then on, each record created (or changed) since starts a run, the oldest first. Created uses CreatedDate; created or updated uses SystemModstamp, which changes with every change, made by people, flows or the API.

Settings

SettingDescription
Salesforce credentialIts run-as user must see the records. Required.
ObjectChoices: Accounts; Contacts; Leads; Opportunities; Cases; Another object. Default: Leads. Required.
API namee.g. Invoice__c.
WhereA SOQL condition: which records, e.g. LeadSource = 'Web'; empty: all.
FieldsMore fields to read, separated by commas (the object's usual ones are read).
Start onChoices: Records created; Records created or updated. Default: Records created. Required.
