Trusted variables names variables whose text is your own, such as a prompt built in a Set step. Without it, a prompt that is only {{ my_prompt }} is treated as data, and the model has no instructions to follow.

Warning: the marks make an attack harder, not impossible: a model may still follow what it reads. What actually limits the damage is what the agent is allowed to do: offer few write tools, ask for approval, and use the lockdown below.

Lockdown after untrusted input

With this switch on, once the agent has read untrusted content in a run, every tool that changes something asks for approval, whatever the step's Ask for approval says. Untrusted content means a tool that ran, a file sent with the prompt, or a marked value in the prompts: in that last case, from the first call. It is off by default.

Masking personal data

On the Claude, OpenAI and Gemini steps, Mask personal data (off by default) replaces email addresses, phone numbers and IBANs with placeholders such as [EMAIL_ab12_1] before anything leaves for the provider: in the prompts, the text of files and tool results. The real values are put back in the model's answer and in the arguments of the tools it calls, so tools, approvers, the variable and the logs see the real values. Ollama, Lemonade and LM Studio are never masked, as they run on your servers.

  • It works by pattern, so it can miss things. A phone number is recognized with a +, a leading 0, or written like 212-555-0100; a bare 40721234567 is not. Names and other personal data are not touched.
  • While masking, a PDF is always sent as its text, never as the document itself.
  • Images cannot be masked. They are sent as they are, and the run's log says so.
  • The model only ever sees the placeholder, so it cannot work with the value itself, such as telling which company an address belongs to from its domain.

Variables

VariableTypeDescription
aiobjectThe answer: { text, html, json, model, stop_reason, rounds, tool_calls, usage, cost, trace_id }; on error { error, trace_id }; a limit reached: { error, trace_id, limit, rounds, tool_calls, usage, cost }
ai.textstringThe answer
ai.htmlstringThe answer as safe HTML (its Markdown converted); in an email {{ ai.html }} shows it formatted
ai.jsonanyThe answer as JSON (answer: JSON)
ai.modelstring
ai.stop_reasonstring
ai.roundsnumber
ai.tool_callsarray
ai.usageobject
ai.errorstringOn error only
ai.costobjectEstimated from the tokens (usd), or the System AI credits used (credits)
ai.limitstringThe limit that stopped the agent: tool_calls, write_calls, cost, budget
ai.trace_idstringThe id of this visit's agent trace. A later step can link to it: /workflow/trace?id={{ ai.trace_id }} after your installation's address

Claude: effort and fallback

Effort sets how much the model thinks before answering: higher for harder tasks, lower for speed and cost. When a request is declined, Fallback on refusal (on by default) lets Anthropic retry it on the model they recommend, for models that support it.

Example: classify incoming mail

  1. Email (inbound) trigger, variable mail.
  2. Claude: system prompt "You sort customer emails.", prompt Subject: {{ mail.subject }} and {{ mail.text }}, Answer: JSON, with the schema above.
  3. Switch on {{ ai.json.category }}: one branch per team, each forwarding the mail.

pages.title: Testing AI steps
pages.summary: Test cases for AI steps and agent workflows: recorded tool results, checks, test runs and tests before publishing.
pages.html:
A change to a prompt, a model or a tool can quietly change what an agent does. Test cases let you check an AI step or an agent workflow before you publish: each case gives the draft some inputs and says what must happen. No test sends an email or changes anything outside the run. The models are really called, so a test run spends tokens.

Test cases

Open the Tests panel with the clipboard icon in the designer's toolbar. A workflow can have up to 50 test cases. There are two ways to make one:

  • Save as test case: in the Executions panel, select a finished run and click the clipboard icon with the plus. The case gets the run's inputs, the tool results from its trace, and what its other steps gave. It then opens for you to add its checks.
  • By hand: click + in the Tests panel and write the inputs as JSON, for example {"message": "My printer is down"}. These are the run's first variables, the ones a trigger would set.

Note: A test case keeps its copy of the inputs and results for as long as it exists, whatever the retention of the run it came from. Values under names that look like secrets, such as password or api_token, are replaced with [removed] when a case is saved from a run.

Tool calls in a test

Each test case chooses how the agent's tool calls are answered:

ChoiceTools that only readTools that change something
Recorded resultsAnswered from the recording: no tool runs.Answered from the recording: no tool runs.
Real read toolsRun for real, unless they ask for an approval.Answered from the recording, or refused: the model is told the tool did not run.

A tool counts as changing something unless it is known to be read-only: the integrations' write operations, workflows run as tools, Remember, and any project or MCP tool not marked read-only. Nothing asks for an approval during a test, and a tool that would have to ask doesn't run.

A recorded result is matched by the tool's name, then by the same arguments and the same step. A call with no recording gets a tool error, and the case's notes say so. Recorded results come from the trace, so they are cut as the trace cuts them (8,000 characters) and images are not kept. If the trace is no longer kept, nothing is recorded.

What runs in a test

Only the trigger, the AI steps, Set, Code, If, Switch, Merge and Loop run. Every other step does not: Send email, HTTP Request, Data table, the integrations, Wait, Human task, Reply to chat, Run a workflow. Instead, what it gave in the saved run stands in for it: its variables, and the output it took. With nothing recorded, it takes its first output and sets no variables, and the case's notes say so.

Note: A case saved from a conversation sends its message as the chat does, but the earlier turns are not replayed: the agent answers as if it were the first turn. Continue the conversation has no conversation in a test.

Checks

CheckPasses when
JSON answer fieldA field of the JSON answer, such as category or items.0.id, equals or does not equal a value, contains a text, matches a pattern, exists or is absent. The step's Answer must be JSON.
Tool was calledA call of that tool was made (* stands for any part of the name), with optional checks on its arguments.
Tool was not calledNo such call was made.
No write tool was calledThe agent did not call any tool that changes something. A call counts even though it did not run in the test.
Answer contains, Answer does not containThe text is in the answer, or is not. Case is ignored unless you tick Exact case.
Judged by a modelA model reads the answer and says whether it meets a short rubric.

With several AI steps, a check can name one; otherwise answer checks read the last AI step that ran, and tool checks look at all of them. A case with no checks only has to finish.

Judged by a model

The judge is the provider and model chosen in Assistant settings. It is paid like the Assistant, from its monthly budget or from System AI credits, and its tokens count in the test's totals. With no provider chosen, the check fails and says why.

The judge receives the rubric, the answer and the names of the tools called, not their arguments. The answer goes between marks with a random name, as data to grade, and personal data is masked if the step masks it. Only a clear pass passes: if the judge's reply can't be read, the check fails. This setting is separate from what the Assistant may read (May read): the answers of your tests go to this provider whichever you chose there.

Running the tests

Run tests saves your changes and runs every case on the draft, one after the other, in the background. You need to be allowed to edit the workflow. One run per workflow goes at a time, and Stop ends it.

The table shows each case's result, how many checks passed, its tokens and estimated cost, and the difference from the last run: fixed or broken, the change in tokens and cost, and whether the answer changed. Click a case for each check, the answer and a link to its execution with its agent trace. The latest 20 runs are kept, in the list above the table; older ones go with their executions.

Test runs are not listed with the workflow's executions and don't count on the Overview. Their tokens do count in the account's monthly AI budget, and a real read counts as an agent action in the audit log. A recorded or refused call does not.

Tests before publishing

Turn on Tests must pass to publish in the Tests panel (you need to be allowed to publish) to require a passing run. See Publishing and versions.

From Claude Code or Claude Desktop

The MCP server has run_tests and get_test_run, so an assistant can change a draft, run its tests and read the result.

pages.title: Integrations
pages.summary: Steps for Google, Microsoft 365, LDAP directories and SQL databases.
pages.html:
Besides the general steps, Rail22 has steps for these services:

  • Google: Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Google Docs.
  • Microsoft 365: Outlook Mail, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive / SharePoint, Excel, Microsoft Teams.
  • Microsoft Intune: devices (filters, remote actions, retire, wipe), compliance policies and configuration profiles, apps and their assignments, Windows Autopilot, any Graph request, and a device trigger.
  • Nextcloud: files (list, search, download, upload, move), shares and public links, users and groups, Talk messages, any OCS request, and a file trigger.
  • LDAP: directory entries, groups and passwords.
  • Bitdefender GravityZone: endpoints, incidents, the blocklist, quarantine, investigation, reports, any API method, and an event trigger.
  • Checkmk: current problems and states, acknowledgements and downtimes, hosts and service discovery, any API request, and a problem trigger.
  • Zabbix: current problems, acknowledgements and maintenances, hosts and their latest values, any API method, and a problem trigger.
  • VMware vCenter: VMs, power and guest shutdown, clones, snapshots, hosts, datastores, maintenance mode, alarms, any API request, and an alarm trigger.
  • Proxmox VE: VMs and containers, power, clones and migration, snapshots, backups to a storage or Proxmox Backup Server, nodes and storage, any API request, and a task trigger.
  • Hyper-V: VMs, power and guest shutdown, checkpoints, the host's volumes, switches, replication and events, any PowerShell script, and a VM state trigger.
  • Namecheap: domains and those expiring soon, renewals, registrar lock, DNS records, name servers and email forwarding, the balance and prices, any API command.
  • Shopify: orders (paid, fulfilled with tracking, cancelled), products and prices, stock by location, customers, webhooks, any GraphQL query, and an event trigger.
  • Jira (Cloud and Data Center): issues (JQL search, create, update, status, assignee, comments, labels, links, attachments), projects, fields and users, any REST request, and an issue trigger.
  • GLPI: tickets (search, create, update, status, actors, follow-ups, tasks, solutions, attachments), assets of any type, users, groups and categories, any API request, and a ticket trigger.
  • HubSpot: contacts, companies, deals, tickets and custom objects (search, create, update, create or update by email, associations, notes), properties, pipelines and owners, any API request, and a record trigger.
  • Salesforce: records of any object (SOQL, SOSL, create, update, upsert by external ID, delete, activities), objects, fields and limits, any REST request, and a record trigger.
  • FortiGate: blocking IPs (address groups, bans), policies, users and VPN, the firewall's state and configuration backups, any API request, and an event trigger.
  • Sophos Firewall: blocking IPs (host groups) and domains (URL groups), firewall rules, users and VPN, the firewall's interfaces and zones, any XML API request.
  • Wazuh: alerts and vulnerabilities, agents and their groups, active response (blocking IPs), scans, inventory, the manager and its rules, any API request, and an alert trigger.
  • Veeam Backup & Replication (12 and 13): jobs, sessions, backups and restore points, the infrastructure, Instant Recovery, any API request, and an event trigger.
  • Databases: one step per SQL database: MySQL / MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Firebird, ODBC.

An AI step can use the operations of these steps as tools, with a credential of the project: the model decides what to look up and, when you allow it, what to change. See Building an agent.

The services of a country come with its regional plugin: Romania (RegionalRO) has ANAF (companies, e-Factura, e-Transport), the BNR exchange rates, SmartBill, FGO, Sameday, FAN Courier and Cargus.

SAP comes with the SAP plugin: SAP Cloud Integration (call iFlows, monitor messages and artifacts, deploy, a trigger for failed messages).

For any other service with a web API, use HTTP Request with an API key or OAuth credential. For services with an MCP server, an AI step can use its tools.

pages.title: Google
pages.summary: Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Calendar and Google Docs steps.
pages.html:
The Google steps work with a Google account through OAuth credentials. Create the credential under Credentials and connect it to the Google account. Setting up the OAuth app, below, explains how to register it and get its client ID and secret. The steps act with that account's rights. They are part of Rail22 itself, on every plan, Free included.

StepCredentialOperations
GmailGoogle Mail (OAuth)Send a message; create a draft; search / read messages; get a message; mark / archive / label a message; move a message to the trash; list the labels
Google DriveGoogle Drive (OAuth)List / search files; get file information; download a file (into the project Files); upload a file; create a folder; move a file; share a file; delete a file
Google SheetsGoogle Sheets or Google Drive (OAuth)Read rows; append rows; update cells; clear cells; get spreadsheet information; create a spreadsheet; add a sheet
Google CalendarGoogle Calendar (OAuth)List events; get an event; create an event; update an event; delete an event; quick add (from a sentence); find busy times; list the calendars
Google DocsGoogle Docs or Google Drive (OAuth)Read a document; create a document; append content; replace texts (fill a template); copy a document (a template)

Useful details

  • Gmail search uses Gmail's own syntax: from:ana@example.com has:attachment newer_than:2d. Attachments can be saved as project files.
  • Gmail send sends from the connected mailbox, so replies come back to it. In reply to keeps a message in its thread.
  • Drive download exports Google files: Docs, Sheets and Slides as Office files, PDF, CSV and more.
  • Sheets read can treat the first row as the header. Each row then becomes an object: {{ sheet.rows[0].Email }}.
  • Docs templates: copy a template document, then Replace texts with an object of placeholders. Each {{key}} in the document gets its value.
  • Calendar create can add a Google Meet link and invite guests.

Every step has On error, a timeout and a result variable. The designer suggests the result's fields as you type.

Setting up the OAuth app

The credentials connect through your own OAuth app at Google: you register it once, then paste its client ID and client secret into the credentials. One app can serve all your Google credentials.

What each credential needs

CredentialEnable this APIScope requestedUsed by
Google Mail (OAuth)Gmail APIhttps://mail.google.com/Gmail step, Read emails (IMAP)
Google Drive (OAuth)Google Drive API (+ Sheets / Docs API for those steps)https://www.googleapis.com/auth/driveGoogle Drive step; also Sheets and Docs steps; HTTP Request
Google Sheets (OAuth)Google Sheets APIhttps://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheetsGoogle Sheets step; HTTP Request
Google Calendar (OAuth)Google Calendar APIhttps://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendarGoogle Calendar step; HTTP Request
Google Docs (OAuth)Google Docs API (+ Drive API to copy templates)https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documentsGoogle Docs step; HTTP Request

Every credential also asks for openid and email, to show which Google account it is connected to. It asks for offline access, so Rail22 can renew its access by itself.

1. Create a Google Cloud project

  1. Open the Google Cloud Console and sign in with the Google account that will own the app, ideally an administrator of your Google Workspace.
  2. In the project picker at the top, click New project, name it (e.g. Rail22) and create it. Make sure it is selected.

2. Enable the APIs

  1. Go to APIs & Services → Library.
  2. Search for each API you need (table above), such as Gmail API or Google Drive API, open it and click Enable.

Note: a credential that connects but fails in its step with a message like "API has not been used in project … or it is disabled" is missing its API. Enable it and try again after a minute.

3. Configure the consent screen

Go to Google Auth Platform (called OAuth consent screen in older consoles).

  1. Branding: the app name people see when they connect (e.g. Rail22), a support email, and optionally your logo and domain.
  2. Audience:
    • Internal: only users of your Google Workspace organization can connect. No verification by Google is needed. This is the simplest choice for a company.
    • External: any Google account. While the app is in Testing, only the test users you add here can connect, and their connections expire after 7 days. Publish the app (In production) for lasting connections. Google may then require verification, because Gmail and Drive scopes are sensitive or restricted.
  3. Data access: click Add or remove scopes and add the scopes of the credentials you will use (table above).

4. Create the OAuth client

  1. Go to Clients (or APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID).
  2. Application type: Web application. Give it a name.
  3. Under Authorized redirect URIs, click Add URI and paste Rail22's redirect URI. It is shown in every OAuth credential's form, and has the form: 
    https://<your Rail22 address>/credential/oauth_callback
    It must match exactly: https, the host, and no trailing slash.
  4. Click Create.

5. Copy the client ID and secret

Google shows the Client ID (ending in .apps.googleusercontent.com) and the Client secret. Copy both, or download the JSON file.

Warning: new Google consoles show the client secret only when it is created. If you lose it, open the client, add a new secret, update the credentials in Rail22, then delete the old secret. Treat the secret like a password.

To find the client again later: Google Auth Platform → Clients (or APIs & Services → Credentials), then click its name. The Client ID is always shown there.

6. Create and connect the credential in Rail22

  1. In the project, open Credentials & variables and add a credential of the kind you need, such as Google Drive (OAuth).
  2. Paste the Client ID and Client secret, then save.
  3. Click Connect. Google asks you to sign in and to allow the access. You come back to Rail22, and Account shows the connected address.
  4. Click Test to check it.

The credential acts as the Google account that connected it: workflows see what that account sees. Connect with a dedicated account (e.g. automation@yourcompany.com) rather than a person's when workflows are shared.

Troubleshooting

MessageFix
redirect_uri_mismatchThe redirect URI in the Google client doesn't match Rail22's exactly. Copy it again from the credential's form.
access_denied, app not verified, blockedExternal app in Testing: add the account as a test user. Or use an Internal app.
The connection stops working after a weekExternal app in Testing: publish it to production.
API has not been used in project… or it is disabledEnable that API (step 2).
invalid_clientWrong client ID or secret, or the secret was deleted. Paste the current ones.
Insufficient permission / scopeThe scope wasn't granted: add it under Data access, then click Connect again.

pages.title: Microsoft 365
pages.summary: Outlook Mail, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive / SharePoint, Excel and Microsoft Teams steps.
pages.html:
The Microsoft 365 steps use Microsoft Graph through OAuth credentials. Create the credential under Credentials and connect it to a Microsoft account (work, school or personal). Setting up the Entra app, below, explains how to register it and get its client ID and secret. The steps are part of Rail22 itself, on every plan, Free included.

StepCredentialOperations
Outlook MailOutlook Mail (Microsoft Graph)Send a message; create a draft; search / read messages; get a message; mark / move / categorize a message; delete a message; list the folders
Outlook CalendarOutlook Calendar (Microsoft Graph)List events; get an event; create an event; update an event; delete an event; find busy times; list the calendars
OneDrive / SharePointOneDrive & SharePoint (Microsoft Graph)List / search files; get file information; download a file (into the project Files); upload a file; create a folder; move / rename a file; share a file; delete a file
ExcelOneDrive & SharePoint (Microsoft Graph)Read rows; append rows; update cells; clear cells; get workbook information; add a worksheet
Microsoft TeamsMicrosoft Teams (Microsoft Graph)Send a channel message; reply to a channel message; send a chat message; list my teams; list the channels of a team; list my chats

Useful details

To talk to an agent in Teams, see the Teams message trigger.

  • Folders in OneDrive / SharePoint can be given by id, by path (/Reports) or by a sharing link.
  • Excel works on workbooks stored in OneDrive or SharePoint. With a header row, each row becomes an object, as with Google Sheets.
  • Outlook Mail folders: inbox, archive, sentitems… or a folder id.
  • To read a Microsoft 365 mailbox over IMAP instead, use a Microsoft 365 Mail (OAuth) credential with Read emails (IMAP).

Setting up the Entra app

The credentials connect through your own app registration in Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD). You register it once, then paste its client ID and client secret into the credentials. One app can serve all your Microsoft credentials.

What each credential needs

All are delegated permissions: the credential acts as the person who connects it.

CredentialAPIDelegated permissionsUsed by
Outlook Mail (Microsoft Graph)Microsoft GraphUser.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.SendOutlook Mail step; HTTP Request
Outlook Calendar (Microsoft Graph)Microsoft GraphUser.Read, Calendars.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read.SharedOutlook Calendar step; HTTP Request
OneDrive & SharePoint (Microsoft Graph)Microsoft GraphUser.Read, Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.ReadWrite.AllOneDrive / SharePoint and Excel steps; HTTP Request
Microsoft Teams (Microsoft Graph)Microsoft GraphUser.Read, Team.ReadBasic.All, Channel.ReadBasic.All, ChannelMessage.Send, ChatMessage.Send, Chat.ReadBasicTeams step; HTTP Request
Microsoft 365 Mail (OAuth)Office 365 Exchange OnlineIMAP.AccessAsUser.AllRead emails (IMAP)

Every credential also asks for offline_access, openid, email and profile, so Rail22 can renew its access and show the connected account. You don't need to add these: Microsoft grants them with sign-in.

1. Register the app

  1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center and sign in with an account allowed to register apps. In many organizations that means an administrator.
  2. Go to Entra ID → App registrations (or Identity → Applications → App registrations) and click New registration.
  3. Name: what people see when they connect, e.g. Rail22.
  4. Supported account types:
    • Accounts in this organizational directory only (single tenant): only your organization. The usual choice.
    • Accounts in any organizational directory (multitenant): work and school accounts of any organization.
    • … and personal Microsoft accounts: also Outlook.com and other personal accounts.
  5. Redirect URI: platform Web, and Rail22's redirect URI. It is shown in every OAuth credential's form, and has the form: 
    https://<your Rail22 address>/credential/oauth_callback
    It must match exactly: https, the host, and no trailing slash.
  6. Click Register.

2. Copy the client ID (and tenant ID)

The app's Overview page shows:

  • Application (client) ID: the Client ID for Rail22.
  • Directory (tenant) ID: needed for a single-tenant app (see step 5).

To find them again later: App registrations → All applications, then click the app.

3. Create the client secret

  1. In the app, go to Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret.
  2. Give it a description (e.g. Rail22) and an expiry. The longest offered is 24 months.
  3. Click Add, then copy the secret's Value at once.

Warning: copy the Value column, not the Secret ID. The value is shown only right after it is created: once you leave the page, it can't be read again. If you lose it, create a new secret.

Note: secrets expire. Note the date. Before it, create a new secret, paste it into your Microsoft credentials (the connections stay), then delete the old one.

4. Add the permissions

  1. In the app, go to API permissions → Add a permission.
  2. For the Graph credentials: choose Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions, tick the permissions from the table above, and click Add permissions.
  3. For Microsoft 365 Mail (IMAP): Add a permission → APIs my organization uses, search for Office 365 Exchange Online, choose Delegated permissions, tick IMAP.AccessAsUser.All, and add it.
  4. If your organization requires it, or for permissions marked Admin consent required (some Teams and SharePoint permissions), click Grant admin consent for <organization>. An administrator must do this.

5. Create and connect the credential in Rail22

  1. In the project, open Credentials & variables and add a credential of the kind you need, such as Outlook Mail (Microsoft Graph).
  2. Paste the Client ID and the secret's value as Client secret.
  3. Set Tenant to match the account types you chose:
    Supported account typesTenant
    This organizational directory onlyThe Directory (tenant) ID, or your domain (e.g. example.com)
    Any organizational directoryorganizations
    Any organizational directory and personal accountscommon (default)
  4. Save, then click Connect. Microsoft asks you to sign in and accept the permissions. You come back to Rail22, and Account shows the connected address.
  5. Click Test to check it.

The credential acts as the account that connected it. Connect with a dedicated account (e.g. a shared automation mailbox) rather than a person's when workflows are shared.

Notes

  • Teams works with work and school accounts only.
  • Microsoft 365 Mail (IMAP): IMAP must be allowed for the mailbox in Exchange (Microsoft 365 admin center → the user → Mail → Email apps).
  • Graph credentials also work with HTTP Request, for other Microsoft Graph calls within their permissions.

Troubleshooting

MessageFix
AADSTS50011 (redirect URI mismatch)Add Rail22's redirect URI exactly, under the Web platform (Authentication page).
AADSTS7000215 (invalid client secret)You pasted the Secret ID, or the secret expired or was deleted. Paste a current secret's Value.
AADSTS50194 / AADSTS90072 (account not in tenant)The Tenant doesn't match the app's account types, or the account isn't in your organization. Use the tenant ID for single-tenant apps.
AADSTS65001 / Need admin approvalAn administrator must grant consent (API permissions → Grant admin consent).
IMAP: authentication failedCheck IMAP.AccessAsUser.All (Office 365 Exchange Online), and that IMAP is enabled for the mailbox.

pages.title: Nextcloud
pages.summary: Files, shares, users and groups, and Talk messages of a Nextcloud server, any OCS request, and a file trigger.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to a Nextcloud server (your own or a hosted one) as one of its users. Its steps are in the Nextcloud group of the step list:

  • Nextcloud Files: lists and searches files, downloads them into the project Files, uploads, creates folders, moves, copies and deletes.
  • Nextcloud Shares: shares files and folders by public link, with users, groups or email addresses, and changes or removes shares.
  • Nextcloud Users: creates, changes, disables and deletes users, and their groups (for administrators).
  • Nextcloud Talk: sends messages to conversations, and reads them.
  • Nextcloud API: any request of Nextcloud's OCS API.

The Nextcloud file trigger starts a workflow when files appear or change in a folder.

The credential

In Nextcloud, sign in as the user the workflows act as, open Personal settings > Security, and under Devices & sessions create an app password (named, for example, Rail22). Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Nextcloud credential, in the Files & collaboration group:

SettingDescription
ServerThe address you open Nextcloud at, such as https://cloud.example.com, with its path when it has one (https://example.com/nextcloud).
UserThe user's login name.
App passwordThe app password. It is stored encrypted, and can be revoked in Nextcloud at any time without changing the user's own password.
Trust the server's certificateOnly for a server with a self-signed certificate.

Test shows the Nextcloud version, the user and its quota. The steps can do what the user can: the users and groups need an administrator, or a group admin for the users of their groups. A server on a private address (inside your network) needs the account's Integrations may connect to private network addresses.

What the steps share

  • Paths are in the user's files, as Nextcloud shows them: /Documents/Invoices/2026-11.pdf. An item of a list works as well, so {{ item }} in a loop over List a folder, or {{ file }} of the file trigger, names that file.
  • Items are { name, path, folder, isFolder, size, modified, contentType, etag, fileId, permissions, favorite }. modified is ISO 8601; size is in bytes (a folder's: its whole content).
  • Lists give { items, count, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Errors: Nextcloud's message, such as User does not exist or HTTP status 409: Parent node does not exist. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

Note: deleting files, sharing them by public link and deleting users act at once. For an AI step they are write operations: not offered by default, and they ask for approval when approvals are on.

pages.title: Nextcloud Files
pages.summary: Lists and searches files, downloads, uploads, creates folders, moves, copies and deletes.
pages.html:
The Nextcloud Files step works with the user's files, through WebDAV.

The credential, the results and the errors are the same for every Nextcloud step: see Nextcloud.

Operations

OperationWebDAVResult
List a folderPROPFIND{ items, count, truncated }: the folder's files and folders, its subfolders' too to Subfolders levels; files, folders or both; names matching Names (patterns such as *.pdf, invoice-*).
Search files by nameSEARCH{ items, count, truncated }: the files under the folder and all its subfolders whose name contains the text, in any case, the newest first.
Get an itemPROPFINDThe item.
Download a file (into the project Files)GET{ id, filename, size, contentType, isImage, …, item }: the file saved in the project Files, as Download File does (the allowed types, at most Largest size).
Upload a filePUTThe new item. A project file (such as {{ file.id }}) or a text, into the folder. When the name exists: keep both (the new one named report (2).pdf), replace, or fail.
Create a folderMKCOLThe folder. Its parents are created too; a folder that exists already is fine.
Move / rename, CopyMOVE / COPYThe item at its new place. To is a folder ending in / (the name is kept) or the new path. An item already there is replaced only with Overwrite.
DeleteDELETE{ path, deleted }. With the Deleted files app, the item goes to the trash bin.

Settings

SettingDescription
Nextcloud credentialA Nextcloud credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List a folder; Search files by name; Get an item; Download a file (into the project Files); Upload a file; Create a folder; Move / rename; Copy; Delete. Default: List a folder. Required.
FolderA path in the files, e.g. /Documents/Invoices; empty: the top. (For: List a folder, Search files by name, Upload a file.)
Pathe.g. /Documents/report.pdf, or an item of a list ({{ item }}). (Required for: Get an item, Download a file (into the project Files), Move / rename, Copy, Delete, Create a folder.)
ItemsChoices: Files and folders; Files; Folders. Default: Files and folders. (For: List a folder.)
SubfoldersLevels below the folder (0: only it). Default: 0. (For: List a folder.)
NamesPatterns, e.g. *.pdf, invoice-*; empty: all. (For: List a folder.)
Name containsAny case. (Required for: Search files by name.)
Save asThe name in the project Files; empty: the file's. (For: Download a file (into the project Files).)
UploadChoices: A project file; A text. Default: A project file. (Required for: Upload a file.)
NameEmpty: the project file's name (a text needs one). (For: Upload a file.)
When the name existsChoices: Keep both (the new one renamed); Replace the existing file; Fail. Default: Keep both (the new one renamed). (Required for: Upload a file.)
Project fileThe id of a file of the project, e.g. {{ file.id }} (Download File) or {{ mail.attachment_files[0] }}.
Text{{ ... }} for expressions (a list / object is written as JSON).
ToA folder ending in / (the name kept), or the new path, e.g. /Archive/2026/ or /Archive/report-old.pdf. (Required for: Move / rename, Copy.)
OverwriteReplace an item already there. Default: off. (For: Move / rename, Copy.)
Largest size (MB)Default: 25. (Required for: Download a file (into the project Files), Upload a file.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 500. Required. (For: List a folder, Search files by name.)
Timeout (s)Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: files. Required.
On errorNextcloud's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, invoices from email: an Email inbound trigger, then Upload a file with {{ mail.attachment_files[0] }} into /Accounting/Inbox.

pages.title: Nextcloud Shares
pages.summary: Shares files and folders by link, with users, groups or emails; changes and removes shares.
pages.html:
The Nextcloud Shares step shares the user's files and folders, through the OCS sharing API.

The credential, the results and the errors are the same for every Nextcloud step: see Nextcloud.

Operations

OperationNextcloud APIResult
List sharesGET …/shares{ items, count, truncated }: the user's shares, those of a path, or those shared with the user.
Share a file or folderPOST …/sharesThe share, as Nextcloud gives it: id, share_type, path, permissions, url and token (a link), share_with, expiration.
Update a sharePUT …/shares/<id>The share. The access, password, expiry date, note and label that are not empty are changed.
Delete a shareDELETE …/shares/<id>{ id, deleted }.

Access: Can view; Can edit (a file: change it; a folder: also add and delete in it); File drop, for a folder's public link: visitors can upload, but not see what is there. Nextcloud's own rules apply, such as a password or an expiry date required for links when the administrator enforces them.

Settings

SettingDescription
Nextcloud credentialA Nextcloud credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List shares; Share a file or folder; Update a share; Delete a share. Default: Share a file or folder. Required.
SharesChoices: Mine; Of a path; Shared with me. Default: Mine. (For: List shares.)
PathA file or folder, e.g. /Documents/report.pdf, or an item of a list. List: for "Of a path". (Required for: Share a file or folder.)
Share withChoices: A public link; A user; A group; An email address. Default: A public link. (Required for: Share a file or folder.)
User, group or emailThe user's or group's ID, or the email address.
ShareIts ID, or a share of a list or of Share. (Required for: Update a share, Delete a share.)
AccessChoices: Unchanged (share: can view); Can view; Can edit; File drop (a folder's link: upload only). (For: Share a file or folder, Update a share.)
PasswordFor a link or an email share; empty: none / unchanged. (For: Share a file or folder, Update a share.)
ExpiresA date (2026-12-31) or relative (+30 days); empty: none / unchanged. (For: Share a file or folder, Update a share.)
NoteShown to the recipient. (For: Share a file or folder, Update a share.)
LabelOf a link, to tell links apart. (For: Share a file or folder, Update a share.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 500. Required. (For: List shares.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: share. Required.
On errorNextcloud's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, a customer's upload folder: Nextcloud Files Create a folder /Customers/{{ form.company }}, then Share a file or folder as a file-drop link that expires in 30 days (+30 days), then Send email with {{ share.url }}.

pages.title: Nextcloud Users
pages.summary: Creates, changes, disables and deletes users, and their groups.
pages.html:
The Nextcloud Users step manages the server's users and groups, through the OCS provisioning API. The credential's user must be an administrator, or a group admin (for the users of their groups).

The credential, the results and the errors are the same for every Nextcloud step: see Nextcloud.

Operations

OperationNextcloud APIResult
List usersGET cloud/users/details{ items, count, truncated }: the users a search finds (in IDs, names and emails), each with its details.
Get a userGET cloud/users/<id>The user: id, displayname, email, enabled, groups, quota (used, total, relative), lastLogin, language.
Create a userPOST cloud/usersThe user. Without a password, Nextcloud emails the user a link to set one: the email is then required.
Update a userPUT cloud/users/<id>The user. The name, email and quota that are not empty are changed (such as 5 GB, none for unlimited, default).
Enable a user, Disable a userPUT …/enable, …/disable{ id, enabled }. A disabled user cannot sign in; their files are kept.
Add to groups, Remove from groupsPOST / DELETE …/groups{ id, groups }.
Delete a userDELETE cloud/users/<id>{ id, deleted }. The user's files are deleted too.
List groupsGET cloud/groups{ items, count, truncated }: each group as { id }.

Settings

SettingDescription
Nextcloud credentialA Nextcloud credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List users; Get a user; Create a user; Update a user; Enable a user; Disable a user; Add to groups; Remove from groups; Delete a user; List groups. Default: List users. Required.
SearchIn IDs, names and emails; empty: all. (For: List users, List groups.)
UserIts ID (login name), or a user of a list. (Required for: Get a user, Update a user, Enable a user, Disable a user, Add to groups, Remove from groups, Delete a user.)
User IDThe login name: letters, digits, spaces and _.@-'. (Required for: Create a user.)
Name(For: Create a user, Update a user.)
EmailCreate without a password: required, Nextcloud sends the welcome email. (For: Create a user, Update a user.)
PasswordEmpty: the user sets one from the welcome email. (For: Create a user.)
GroupsGroup IDs, separated by commas, or a list. (For: Create a user, Add to groups, Remove from groups.)
Quotae.g. 5 GB, none (unlimited), default. (For: Create a user, Update a user.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 500. Required. (For: List users, List groups.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: users. Required.
On errorNextcloud's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, onboarding from a Form: Create a user with the new colleague's email and the group of their department, then a welcome message with Nextcloud Talk. Offboarding: Disable a user first, and delete later.

pages.title: Nextcloud Talk
pages.summary: Sends messages to Talk conversations, and reads them.
pages.html:
The Nextcloud Talk step posts to the user's Talk conversations, as the credential's user. The Talk app must be installed, and the user a participant of the conversation.

The credential, the results and the errors are the same for every Nextcloud step: see Nextcloud.

Operations

OperationNextcloud APIResult
Send a messagePOST apps/spreed/api/v1/chat/<token>The message: id, token, message, timestamp. Markdown is shown as Talk shows it. Silent: no notification for the participants.
List conversationsGET apps/spreed/api/v4/room{ items, count, truncated }: each with token, name, displayName, type, unreadMessages, lastActivity.
Read messagesGET apps/spreed/api/v1/chat/<token>{ items, count, truncated }: the newest messages, the newest first (at most 200).

The conversation is given by its token (in its address: …/call/<token>) or its name. A user made for Rail22 (such as rail22-bot), added to the conversations, makes the messages easy to tell apart.

Settings

SettingDescription
Nextcloud credentialA Nextcloud credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Send a message; List conversations; Read messages. Default: Send a message. Required.
ConversationIts token (in its address: /call/<token>) or its name. (Required for: Send a message, Read messages.)
MessageMarkdown; {{ ... }} for expressions. (Required for: Send a message.)
SilentNo notification for the participants. Default: off. (For: Send a message.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 500. Required. (For: List conversations, Read messages.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: talk. Required.
On errorNextcloud's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Nextcloud API
pages.summary: Any request of Nextcloud's OCS API.
pages.html:
The Nextcloud API step sends any request of Nextcloud's OCS API, as the credential's user: what the other Nextcloud steps don't have, such as user status, notifications or an app's own OCS endpoints. It is an advanced step.

The path is below /ocs/v2.php, such as /cloud/user or /apps/notifications/api/v2/notifications. Parameters is a JSON object, sent in the query of a GET or DELETE and as a form for a POST or PUT; a list is sent as name[]. The result is the answer's ocs.data.

Settings

SettingDescription
Nextcloud credentialA Nextcloud credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: An OCS request. Default: An OCS request. Required.
MethodChoices: GET; POST; PUT; DELETE. Default: GET. (Required for: An OCS request.)
PathBelow /ocs/v2.php, e.g. /cloud/user or /apps/notifications/api/v2/notifications. (Required for: An OCS request.)
ParametersA JSON object (empty: none), e.g. {"search": "ana"}; lists are sent as name[].
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: nextcloud. Required.
On errorNextcloud's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: LDAP
pages.summary: Searches and manages entries of an LDAP directory (Active Directory, OpenLDAP...).
pages.html:
The LDAP step works with a directory such as Active Directory or OpenLDAP, through an LDAP server credential of the project. It acts with the rights of the credential's bind DN. Every account has it, whatever its plan.

Operations

OperationResult
Search entries{ entries, count, truncated }. Each entry has its dn and attributes.
Get an entryThe entry.
Add / modify / rename or move / delete an entry{ dn }
Add / remove a member of a group{ dn }
Check a password{ valid, dn }
Set a password{ dn }

Use it to provision accounts from an HR form, add people to groups after an approval, or check who someone's manager is before assigning a task.

Note: signing in to Rail22 with your directory is a separate feature, which depends on your plan. The step doesn't need it. See LDAP sign-in.

pages.title: Databases
pages.summary: The SQL database steps (MySQL / MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Firebird, ODBC): what they share.
pages.html:
Rail22 has one step per kind of SQL database: MySQL / MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Firebird, ODBC. They are in the Databases group of the step list. Each reads and changes a database through a credential of its own kind, of the project: the MySQL / MariaDB step lists only the MySQL / MariaDB credentials, and so on. Every account has them. Which ones you can use depends on what the installation provides: see What the installation needs below.

This page is what the steps share. The page of each step has its credential, what is particular to that database, and an example.

Operations

OperationResult
Query rows{ rows, count, columns, truncated }: the rows of a SELECT, each an object keyed by column. At most At most (rows); truncated says there were more.
Execute a statement{ affected, lastInsertId }: an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, a procedure call or a change of the tables. lastInsertId is the new row's id where the database gives one (MySQL, SQL Server), else null.
Insert rows{ affected }: the rows of a list of objects keyed by column, such as {{ response.body.items }}, inserted into Table in one transaction: all of them, or none when one fails.

Each step runs one statement on its own connection. Statements of different steps are not in one transaction.

Values in the SQL

A {{ }} in the SQL is sent to the database as a parameter of the statement, never as SQL text. A value can't change the statement, whatever it holds:

SELECT id, name, email FROM customers
WHERE country = {{ form.country }} AND created_at >= {{ since }}
  • Quotes around a {{ }} are not needed. '{{ name }}' is the same parameter.
  • Build a pattern in the expression: name LIKE {{ '%' + name + '%' }}. A {{ }} inside a quoted text, as in '%{{ name }}%', is an error.
  • Table and column names can't be parameters. Write them in the SQL.
  • Numbers and texts are sent as they are, and an empty value as NULL. True / false are booleans for PostgreSQL, 1 / 0 for the others. Lists and objects are sent as JSON text.

Settings

SettingDescription
Kind credentialA credential of the step's kind, of the project (menu: Credentials), for example MySQL / MariaDB credential. Required.
OperationChoices: Query rows; Execute a statement; Insert rows. Default: Query rows. Required.
SQLOne statement. A {{ }} is sent as a parameter: WHERE id = {{ order.id }} (not for table or column names). (Shown for some values of Operation.)
TableA table, or schema.table. (Shown for some values of Operation.)
RowsAn expression giving a list of objects keyed by column, e.g. {{ response.body.items }}. (Shown for some values of Operation.)
At most (rows)More are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (Shown for some values of Operation.)
Timeout (s)To connect, and of the statement where the database has a limit. Default: 60. Required.
Result variable{ rows, count, ... } or { affected }. Default: db. Required.
On errorDatabase errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Variables

VariableTypeDescription
dbobjectThe step's result
db.rowsarrayQuery rows only
db.countnumberQuery rows only
db.columnsarrayThe column names. Query rows only
db.truncatedbooleanMore rows than At most. Query rows only
db.affectednumberThe rows changed. Execute a statement and Insert rows only
db.lastInsertIdstringThe id of the row inserted, null where the database has none. Execute a statement only
db.errorstringOn error only

Each row has its columns by name: {{ db.rows[0].email }}. Names are as the database gives them: Oracle and Firebird give unquoted names in capitals ({{ db.rows[0].EMAIL }}). Long texts and binary columns are read whole. Binary values are base64 text.

The credentials

Create one under Credentials & variables, in the Database group, of the step's kind, and use Test to check that it connects.

CredentialSettings
MySQL / MariaDBServer, port (3306), database (optional), username, password. TLS: none, encrypted, or encrypted with the server's certificate checked.
PostgreSQLServer, port (5432), database, username, password. TLS: none, when the server offers it, encrypted, or encrypted with the certificate and name checked.
Microsoft SQL ServerServer, or a named instance such as sql.example.com\SQLEXPRESS, port (1433), database (optional), username, password, Encrypt the connection, and Trust the server's certificate for a self-signed one.
OracleServer, port (1521), Service name (such as ORCLPDB1), username, password.
FirebirdServer, port (3050), the database's path or alias on the server, username, password.
ODBC data sourceThe name of a data source set up on the Rail22 server by its administrator, and a username and password when the data source doesn't hold them.

Note: the step works with the rights of the credential's user. Give that user only what the workflows need, for example read access to the tables they query.

The Timeout applies to connecting. MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQL Server (with Microsoft's driver) also stop a statement that runs longer. For Oracle, Firebird and ODBC, the database's own limits apply.

What the installation needs

Each kind of database needs its PHP extension (a PDO driver). A kind whose extension is missing is not offered for new credentials, and its step isn't in the step list.

DatabasePHP extension
MySQL / MariaDBpdo_mysql
PostgreSQLpdo_pgsql
Microsoft SQL Serverpdo_sqlsrv (Microsoft's driver), or pdo_dblib (FreeTDS; encryption as set in freetds.conf)
Oraclepdo_oci, with Oracle's client libraries
Firebirdpdo_firebird
ODBCpdo_odbc, with unixODBC and the database's ODBC driver

Install the extension for both the web server's PHP (PHP-FPM) and the command-line PHP, which runs the daemon. Then restart PHP-FPM and the daemon. The setup wizard's Prerequisites list each kind, and say when the command-line PHP lacks an extension the web one has. A workflow that runs in the daemon without the extension fails with a message naming the missing extension.

ODBC credentials name a data source set up on the server, in odbc.ini. They can't hold a connection string, which could point a driver at files on the Rail22 server.

pages.title: MySQL / MariaDB
pages.summary: Queries and changes a MySQL or MariaDB database: rows, statements, bulk inserts.
pages.html:
The MySQL / MariaDB step runs SQL on a MySQL or MariaDB server through a MySQL / MariaDB credential of the project: it reads rows, runs a statement, or inserts a list of rows in one transaction.

The operations, the values in the SQL, every setting and the result variable are the same for every database step: see Databases.

The credential

Server, port (3306), database (optional: without one, name the tables as database.table), username, password. TLS: none, encrypted, or encrypted with the server's certificate checked against the system's certificate authorities.

LOAD DATA LOCAL is off: a statement can't read files of the Rail22 server.

Good to know

  • Execute a statement gives lastInsertId: the id of an AUTO_INCREMENT row inserted.
  • The Timeout also stops a long statement: max_execution_time on MySQL (for SELECT only), max_statement_time on MariaDB.
  • True / false are sent as 1 / 0.

Example

SELECT id, email, total FROM orders
WHERE status = {{ form.status }} AND created_at >= {{ since }}
ORDER BY created_at DESC

What the installation needs

The PHP extension pdo_mysql, in both the web server's PHP and the command-line PHP (the daemon). Without it, the step isn't in the step list and its credential isn't offered. See Databases.

pages.title: PostgreSQL
pages.summary: Queries and changes a PostgreSQL database: rows, statements, bulk inserts.
pages.html:
The PostgreSQL step runs SQL on a PostgreSQL server through a PostgreSQL credential of the project: it reads rows, runs a statement, or inserts a list of rows in one transaction.

The operations, the values in the SQL, every setting and the result variable are the same for every database step: see Databases.

The credential

Server, port (5432), database, username, password. TLS: none, encrypted when the server offers it, encrypted, or encrypted with the certificate and the server's name checked.

Good to know

  • True / false are sent as booleans.
  • The Timeout also stops a long statement (statement_timeout).
  • lastInsertId is usually null: use INSERT … RETURNING id with Query rows to get the new rows' ids.

Example

INSERT INTO tickets (subject, requester, priority)
VALUES ({{ mail.subject }}, {{ mail.from }}, {{ priority }})
RETURNING id

With Query rows, the new ticket's id is {{ db.rows[0].id }}.

What the installation needs

The PHP extension pdo_pgsql, in both the web server's PHP and the command-line PHP (the daemon). Without it, the step isn't in the step list and its credential isn't offered. See Databases.

pages.title: SQL Server
pages.summary: Queries and changes a Microsoft SQL Server database: rows, statements, bulk inserts.
pages.html:
The SQL Server step runs SQL on Microsoft SQL Server (or Azure SQL) through a Microsoft SQL Server credential of the project: it reads rows, runs a statement or a stored procedure, or inserts a list of rows in one transaction.

The operations, the values in the SQL, every setting and the result variable are the same for every database step: see Databases.

The credential

Server, or a named instance such as sql.example.com\SQLEXPRESS, port (1433), database (optional), username, password, Encrypt the connection, and Trust the server's certificate for a self-signed one.

Good to know

  • Execute a statement gives lastInsertId: the id of an IDENTITY row inserted.
  • With Microsoft's driver (pdo_sqlsrv), the Timeout also stops a long statement.
  • True / false are sent as 1 / 0.

Example

SELECT TOP 50 CustomerID, Name, Email FROM dbo.Customers
WHERE Country = {{ form.country }}

What the installation needs

The PHP extension pdo_sqlsrv (Microsoft's driver), or pdo_dblib (FreeTDS; encryption as set in freetds.conf), in both the web server's PHP and the command-line PHP (the daemon). Without one, the step isn't in the step list and its credential isn't offered. See Databases.

pages.title: Oracle
pages.summary: Queries and changes an Oracle database: rows, statements, bulk inserts.
pages.html:
The Oracle step runs SQL on an Oracle database through an Oracle credential of the project: it reads rows, runs a statement or a PL/SQL block, or inserts a list of rows in one transaction.

The operations, the values in the SQL, every setting and the result variable are the same for every database step: see Databases.

The credential

Server, port (1521), Service name (such as ORCLPDB1), username, password.

Good to know

  • Unquoted column names come back in capitals: {{ db.rows[0].EMAIL }}.
  • lastInsertId is null.
  • The Timeout applies to connecting; the database's own limits apply to statements.
  • True / false are sent as 1 / 0.

Example

SELECT employee_id, email FROM hr.employees
WHERE department_id = {{ dept }}
FETCH FIRST 100 ROWS ONLY

What the installation needs

The PHP extension pdo_oci, with Oracle's client libraries (Instant Client),, in both the web server's PHP and the command-line PHP (the daemon). Without it, the step isn't in the step list and its credential isn't offered. See Databases.

pages.title: Firebird
pages.summary: Queries and changes a Firebird database: rows, statements, bulk inserts.
pages.html:
The Firebird step runs SQL on a Firebird server through a Firebird credential of the project: it reads rows, runs a statement, or inserts a list of rows in one transaction.

The operations, the values in the SQL, every setting and the result variable are the same for every database step: see Databases.

The credential

Server, port (3050), the database's path or alias on the server (such as /data/sales.fdb), username, password.

Good to know

  • Unquoted column names come back in capitals: {{ db.rows[0].EMAIL }}.
  • lastInsertId is null: use INSERT … RETURNING with Query rows.
  • The Timeout applies to connecting; the database's own limits apply to statements.

Example

SELECT FIRST 20 ID, NAME, STOCK FROM PRODUCTS
WHERE STOCK < {{ threshold }}

What the installation needs

The PHP extension pdo_firebird, in both the web server's PHP and the command-line PHP (the daemon). Without it, the step isn't in the step list and its credential isn't offered. See Databases.

pages.title: ODBC
pages.summary: Queries and changes any database with an ODBC driver, through a data source set up on the server.
pages.html:
The ODBC step runs SQL on any database that has an ODBC driver (for example DB2, Informix, SAP HANA, Snowflake, Access) through an ODBC data source credential of the project: it reads rows, runs a statement, or inserts a list of rows in one transaction.

The operations, the values in the SQL, every setting and the result variable are the same for every database step: see Databases.

The credential

The name of a data source set up on the Rail22 server by its administrator, in odbc.ini, and a username and password when the data source doesn't hold them. A credential can't hold a connection string, which could point a driver at files on the Rail22 server.

The credential's Test only checks that it connects.

Good to know

  • The SQL is the database's own dialect.
  • The Timeout applies to connecting; the database's own limits apply to statements.
  • lastInsertId depends on the driver, and is often null.

Example

SELECT ITEM_NO, DESCRIPTION FROM ITEMS WHERE CHANGED_AT > {{ since }}

What the installation needs

The PHP extension pdo_odbc, with unixODBC and the database's ODBC driver,, in both the web server's PHP and the command-line PHP (the daemon). Without it, the step isn't in the step list and its credential isn't offered. See Databases.

pages.title: Bitdefender GravityZone
pages.summary: Endpoints, incidents, blocklist, quarantine, investigation and reports of a GravityZone console, cloud or on-premises.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Bitdefender GravityZone, in the cloud or on your own premises, through its Public API. Its steps are in the Security group of the step list:

  • GravityZone Endpoints: lists endpoints, groups and policies, scans endpoints, moves them, labels them and assigns policies.
  • GravityZone Incidents: lists and reads EDR / XDR incidents, changes their status, priority, assignee and note, and isolates endpoints.
  • GravityZone Blocklist: blocks file hashes on every endpoint, lists the blocklist and removes items from it.
  • GravityZone Quarantine: lists quarantined files, restores or deletes them, empties the quarantine and quarantines a file.
  • GravityZone Investigation: live response on an endpoint: runs a command, collects an investigation package, retrieves a file, kills a process.
  • GravityZone Reports: creates and lists reports, gets their download links, and saves a report's files in Files.
  • GravityZone API: calls any method of the GravityZone Public API: licensing, accounts, packages, patch management and the others.

The GravityZone event trigger starts a workflow when GravityZone sends events: a malware detection, a new incident, a finished task.

The credential

In GravityZone, create an API key under My Account (or a service API key) and enable the APIs the workflows need: Network, Incidents, Quarantine, Reports, Policies, Investigation, Push (for the trigger). Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Bitdefender GravityZone credential, in the Security group:

SettingDescription
API access URLAs shown in GravityZone under My Account > Control Center API, such as https://cloud.gravityzone.bitdefender.com/api. An on-premises console: https://<console>/api.
KeyA personal API key (sent as HTTP Basic) or a service API key (sent in the X-API-Key header).
API keyThe key. It is stored encrypted.
Trust the console's certificateOnly for an on-premises console with a self-signed certificate.

Test checks the key and lists the APIs enabled for it.

Note: GravityZone's keys have no read-only scope: a key with an API enabled can both read and change in it. Give each workflow's credential a key with only the APIs it needs.

On-premises consoles

Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more. For a console in your own network, turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach. Turn on Trust the console's certificate when the console has a self-signed certificate.

What the steps share

  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }: Rail22 reads the pages (100 items each) up to At most (items), and truncated says there were more.
  • Ids (endpoints, groups, items) are GravityZone's. Where a setting takes several, give a list, text separated by commas, or a list of objects: their id is used. So {{ endpoints.items }} from a list works as targets.
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the call's parameters, over the step's own: filters, options and everything a step has no setting for. See Bitdefender's API reference for each method's parameters.
  • Errors: GravityZone's message, with its details, such as Invalid params: The endpointId is not valid. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.
  • Rate limit: GravityZone allows about 10 requests per second per key. When it asks to wait (HTTP 429), the step waits up to 10 seconds and tries once more.

pages.title: GravityZone Endpoints
pages.summary: Lists endpoints, groups and policies, scans endpoints, moves them, labels them and assigns policies.
pages.html:
The GravityZone Endpoints step works with the endpoints of the console's network inventory (the Network and Policies APIs).

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every GravityZone step: see Bitdefender GravityZone.

Operations

OperationGravityZone methodResult
List endpointsnetwork.getEndpointsList{ items, count, total, truncated }. Of a group (empty: the company's), managed or not, with the subgroups' endpoints.
Get endpoint detailsnetwork.getManagedEndpointDetailsThe endpoint: its name, OS, agent, modules, policy, state.
List network inventorynetwork.getNetworkInventoryItems{ items, count, total, truncated }: groups and endpoints.
List custom groupsnetwork.getCustomGroupsListThe groups under a group.
Scan endpointsnetwork.createScanTaskA quick, full, memory or custom scan task on endpoints or groups: GravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
List scan tasksnetwork.getScanTasksList{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Get task statusnetwork.getTaskStatusThe task's status.
Move endpoints to a groupnetwork.moveEndpointsGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
Set endpoint labelnetwork.setEndpointLabelGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true). An empty label removes it.
List policiespolicies.getPoliciesList{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Assign a policynetwork.assignPolicyGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialA Bitdefender GravityZone credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List endpoints; Get endpoint details; List network inventory; List custom groups; Scan endpoints; List scan tasks; Get task status; Move endpoints to a group; Set endpoint label; List policies; Assign a policy. Default: List endpoints. Required.
GroupA group's id; empty: the company's root. (For: List endpoints; List network inventory; List custom groups.)
EndpointsChoices: All; Managed only; Unmanaged only. Default: All. (For: List endpoints.)
With subgroupsDefault: on. (For: List endpoints; List network inventory.)
EndpointAn endpoint's id. (Required for: Get endpoint details; Set endpoint label.)
TargetsEndpoint (or group, to scan and assign) ids: a list, or separated by commas. (Required for: Scan endpoints; Move endpoints to a group; Assign a policy.)
ScanChoices: Quick scan; Full scan; Memory scan; Custom scan. Default: Quick scan. (For: Scan endpoints.)
Task nameEmpty: GravityZone's. (For: Scan endpoints.)
TaskA task's id (e.g. of Scan endpoints). (Required for: Get task status.)
Into groupThe group's id. (Required for: Move endpoints to a group.)
LabelEmpty: removes the label. (For: Set endpoint label.)
PolicyThe policy's id (List policies). (Required for: Assign a policy.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the call's parameters (over the step's own), e.g. {"filters": {...}}: see the GravityZone API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List endpoints; List network inventory; List scan tasks; List policies.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else GravityZone's result. Default: endpoints. Required.
On errorGravityZone's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A nightly full scan of a group's endpoints, then a check of the task: Scan endpoints with Targets {{ vars.servers_group }} and Scan Full scan, a Wait, then Get task status with Task {{ endpoints }}.

Targets accept a list of objects too: {{ endpoints.items }} from List endpoints scans every endpoint listed.

pages.title: GravityZone Incidents
pages.summary: Lists and reads EDR / XDR incidents, changes their status, priority, assignee and note, and isolates endpoints.
pages.html:
The GravityZone Incidents step works with the incidents of GravityZone's EDR and XDR (the Incidents API), and isolates endpoints from the network.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every GravityZone step: see Bitdefender GravityZone.

Operations

OperationGravityZone methodResult
List incidentsincidents.getIncidentsList{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Get an incidentincidents.getIncidentThe incident.
Change statusincidents.changeIncidentStatusOpen, Investigating, False positive or Closed.
Change priorityincidents.changeIncidentPriorityLow, Medium, High or Critical.
Assignincidents.assignIncidentTo a user of the console, by id.
Set the noteincidents.updateIncidentNoteReplaces the incident's note.
Isolate an endpointincidents.createIsolateEndpointTaskGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
Restore an endpoint from isolationincidents.createRestoreEndpointFromIsolationTaskGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialA Bitdefender GravityZone credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List incidents; Get an incident; Change status; Change priority; Assign; Set the note; Isolate an endpoint; Restore an endpoint from isolation. Default: List incidents. Required.
KindChoices: Incidents; Extended incidents (XDR). Default: Incidents. (For: List incidents; Get an incident; Change status; Change priority; Assign; Set the note.)
IncidentThe incident's id. (Required for: Get an incident; Change status; Change priority; Assign; Set the note.)
StatusChoices: Open; Investigating; False positive; Closed. Default: Investigating. (For: Change status.)
PriorityChoices: Low; Medium; High; Critical. Default: Medium. (For: Change priority.)
AssigneeThe id of a user of the console. (Required for: Assign.)
NoteReplaces the incident's note. (For: Set the note.)
EndpointThe endpoint's id. (Required for: Isolate an endpoint; Restore an endpoint from isolation.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the call's parameters (over the step's own), e.g. {"filters": {...}}: see the GravityZone API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List incidents.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else GravityZone's result. Default: incidents. Required.
On errorGravityZone's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Kind chooses between incidents (endpoint) and extended incidents (XDR).

Example

With the GravityZone event trigger on New incident: an If on the incident's severity, a Human task asking the security team whether to isolate the endpoint, then Isolate an endpoint and Set the note with the team's answer.

pages.title: GravityZone Blocklist
pages.summary: Blocks file hashes on every endpoint, lists the blocklist and removes items from it.
pages.html:
The GravityZone Blocklist step manages the file hashes GravityZone blocks on every endpoint (the Incidents API).

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every GravityZone step: see Bitdefender GravityZone.

Operations

OperationGravityZone methodResult
List blocked hashesincidents.getBlocklistItems{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Block hashesincidents.addToBlocklistSHA-256 or MD5 hashes, with a note (shown in GravityZone).
Unblock an itemincidents.removeFromBlocklistBy the item's id, from the list.

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialA Bitdefender GravityZone credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List blocked hashes; Block hashes; Unblock an item. Default: Block hashes. Required.
HashChoices: SHA-256; MD5. Default: SHA-256. (For: Block hashes.)
HashesA list, or one per line / separated by commas. (Required for: Block hashes.)
NoteWhy they are blocked (shown in GravityZone). (For: Block hashes.)
ItemThe blocklist item's id (List blocked hashes). (Required for: Unblock an item.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the call's parameters (over the step's own), e.g. {"filters": {...}}: see the GravityZone API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List blocked hashes.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else GravityZone's result. Default: blocklist. Required.
On errorGravityZone's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Hashes are a list, or one per line or separated by commas, up to 1,000 per step. Each is checked before anything is sent: a hash of the wrong kind or length is an error, and nothing is blocked.

Example

A threat intelligence feed read by HTTP Request on a schedule, then Block hashes with Hashes {{ response.body.sha256 }} and the note Feed {{ schedule_time }}.

pages.title: GravityZone Quarantine
pages.summary: Lists quarantined files, restores or deletes them, empties the quarantine and quarantines a file.
pages.html:
The GravityZone Quarantine step works with the files GravityZone quarantined on endpoints (the Quarantine API, computers).

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every GravityZone step: see Bitdefender GravityZone.

Operations

OperationGravityZone methodResult
List quarantined itemsquarantine/computers.getQuarantineItemsList{ items, count, total, truncated } Of one endpoint, or of all.
Restore itemsquarantine/computers.createRestoreQuarantineItemTaskTo where they were, or to a folder; optionally with an exclusion added to the policy.
Delete itemsquarantine/computers.createRemoveQuarantineItemTaskGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
Empty the quarantinequarantine/computers.createEmptyQuarantineTaskGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
Quarantine a filequarantine/computers.createAddFileToQuarantineTaskA file, by its path, on endpoints.

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialA Bitdefender GravityZone credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List quarantined items; Restore items; Delete items; Empty the quarantine; Quarantine a file. Default: List quarantined items. Required.
EndpointEmpty: the items of every endpoint. (For: List quarantined items.)
ItemsQuarantined item ids: a list, or separated by commas. (Required for: Restore items; Delete items.)
Restore toA folder of the endpoint; empty: where the file was. (For: Restore items.)
Add an exclusion to the policyDefault: off. (For: Restore items.)
EndpointsEndpoint ids: a list, or separated by commas. (Required for: Quarantine a file.)
FileThe file's path on the endpoints. (Required for: Quarantine a file.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the call's parameters (over the step's own), e.g. {"filters": {...}}: see the GravityZone API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List quarantined items.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else GravityZone's result. Default: quarantine. Required.
On errorGravityZone's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A false positive confirmed by a person: a Human task shows the quarantined item, then Restore items with Add an exclusion to the policy on, so the file is not caught again.

pages.title: GravityZone Investigation
pages.summary: Live response on an endpoint: runs a command, collects an investigation package, retrieves a file, kills a process.
pages.html:
The GravityZone Investigation step acts on an endpoint through GravityZone's agent (the Investigation API). It is an advanced step.

Warning: these operations run on your endpoints with the agent's rights. Let only the people who may do so edit the workflows that use this step, and enable the Investigation API only on the keys that need it.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every GravityZone step: see Bitdefender GravityZone.

Operations

OperationGravityZone methodResult
Run a commandstartCommandExecutionOnEndpointGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
Collect an investigation packagecollectInvestigationPackageGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
Retrieve a filestartRetrieveInvestigationFileFromEndpointGravityZone's answer (usually the task's id, or true).
Get a retrieved file's addressgetInvestigationFileUrlThe address of the file or package, once the task is done.
Kill a processkillProcessBy its process id.

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialA Bitdefender GravityZone credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Run a command; Collect an investigation package; Retrieve a file; Get a retrieved file's address; Kill a process. Default: Run a command. Required.
EndpointThe endpoint's id. (Required for: Run a command; Collect an investigation package; Retrieve a file; Kill a process.)
CommandRun by GravityZone's agent on the endpoint. (Required for: Run a command.)
FileThe file's path on the endpoint. (Required for: Retrieve a file.)
TaskThe id of the retrieve / collect task. (Required for: Get a retrieved file's address.)
ProcessThe process id (PID). (Required for: Kill a process.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the call's parameters (over the step's own), e.g. {"filters": {...}}: see the GravityZone API reference. (Under Advanced….)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else GravityZone's result. Default: investigation. Required.
On errorGravityZone's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

After a New incident event: Collect an investigation package from the incident's endpoint, a Wait, then Get a retrieved file's address, and an email to the security team with the link.

pages.title: GravityZone Reports
pages.summary: Creates and lists reports, gets their download links, and saves a report's files in Files.
pages.html:
The GravityZone Reports step works with the console's reports (the Reports API).

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every GravityZone step: see Bitdefender GravityZone.

Operations

OperationGravityZone methodResult
Create a reportreports.createReportGravityZone's answer (the report's id). The schedule and options go in Other parameters.
List reportsreports.getReportsList{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Get download linksreports.getDownloadLinks{ readyForDownload, lastInstanceUrl, allInstancesUrl }
Download into Filesreports.getDownloadLinks + the file{ files, count }: each { id, filename, size, contentType }.
Delete a reportreports.deleteReportGravityZone's answer.

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialA Bitdefender GravityZone credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Create a report; List reports; Get download links; Download into Files; Delete a report. Default: Download into Files. Required.
Name(Required for: Create a report.)
TypeGravityZone's report type number (see its API reference). Default: 1. (Required for: Create a report.)
TargetsEndpoint or group ids: a list, or separated by commas. (Required for: Create a report.)
ReportThe report's id. (Required for: Get download links; Download into Files; Delete a report.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the call's parameters (over the step's own), e.g. {"filters": {...}}: see the GravityZone API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List reports.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else GravityZone's result. Default: report. Required.
On errorGravityZone's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Download into Files takes the report's last instance. GravityZone gives it as a ZIP: the step unpacks it and saves the files inside (CSV, PDF, …) in the project's Files, up to 20, of the types Files accept.

Example

A weekly report sent by email: a Schedule Trigger on Mondays, Download into Files, then Send email with {{ report.files }} attached.

pages.title: GravityZone API
pages.summary: Calls any method of the GravityZone Public API: licensing, accounts, packages, patch management and the others.
pages.html:
The GravityZone API step calls any method of the GravityZone Public API, for what the other GravityZone steps don't cover: licensing, accounts, companies, packages, patch management, maintenance windows, integrations. It is an advanced step.

Give the API (the part of the address after jsonrpc/, such as licensing or quarantine/computers), the Method and its Parameters as a JSON object, as in Bitdefender's API reference. {{ }} work in the parameters. The result is GravityZone's result, as it is.

API: licensing
