Method: getMonthlyUsage
Parameters: {"targetMonth": "{{ month }}"}

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every GravityZone step: see Bitdefender GravityZone.

Settings

SettingDescription
GravityZone credentialA Bitdefender GravityZone credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Call a method. Default: Call a method. Required.
APIe.g. network, licensing, quarantine/computers. Default: network. (Required for: Call a method.)
Methode.g. getLicenseInfo. (Required for: Call a method.)
VersionDefault: 1.0. (For: Call a method.)
ParametersA JSON object (empty: none), or an expression giving one.
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else GravityZone's result. Default: gz. Required.
On errorGravityZone's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Veeam Backup & Replication
pages.summary: Jobs, sessions, backups, infrastructure and Instant Recovery of a Veeam Backup & Replication 12 or 13 server.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Veeam Backup & Replication 12 (12.0 to 12.3) and 13 through its REST API. Its steps are in the Backup group of the step list:

  • Veeam Jobs: lists jobs and their states, starts, stops and retries jobs, enables and disables them.
  • Veeam Sessions: lists job sessions (runs) and their results, reads their tasks and log, stops them, and waits for them to finish.
  • Veeam Backups: lists backups and restore points, and checks that a machine has a recent restore point.
  • Veeam Infrastructure: repositories and their free space, proxies, managed servers, the license and the backup server.
  • Veeam Restore: instant Recovery of VMware vSphere machines from a restore point: start, list, stop.
  • Veeam API: sends any request of the Veeam Backup & Replication REST API.

The Veeam event trigger starts a workflow when job sessions end with the results you choose, such as Failed or Warning.

The credential

Under Credentials & variables, create a Veeam Backup & Replication credential, in the Backup group:

SettingDescription
ServerThe backup server's REST API, such as https://vbr.example.local:9419.
Username, PasswordA Veeam user with a built-in role: Veeam's custom roles can't use the REST API. DOMAIN\user for a domain user. The password is stored encrypted.
Veeam versionThe backup server's release: 13, 12.3.1 (or a later 12.3), 12.3, 12.2, 12.1 or 12.0. Its REST API version is sent with every request (1.3-rev1 for 13 down to 1.1-rev0 for 12.0).
Trust the server's certificateFor the backup server's own self-signed certificate.

Test signs in and shows the server's name and version. When the Veeam version chosen doesn't match the server, it says which one to choose.

Note: give the credential's user the smallest role that does the job: Backup Viewer to read, Backup Operator to start and stop jobs, Restore Operator for restores.

Servers in your network

A backup server is usually on your own network. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach. Turn on Trust the server's certificate for the server's own certificate.

What the steps share

  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }: Rail22 reads the pages (200 items each) up to At most (items), and truncated says there were more.
  • Ids are Veeam's (such as 8f6c…). Where a step takes a session, restore point or mount, an object with an id works too: {{ jobs }} after Start a job is the session started.
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the query of a list (filters such as typeFilter) or to the body of an action. See Veeam's REST API reference.
  • Errors: Veeam's message, such as The job was not found (NotFound). With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.
  • Older releases: the steps' requests are those of Veeam's REST API, which grew with each release. A request that the server's release doesn't have fails with a message that says so. Use the newest release you can.
  • Sign-in: Rail22 signs in once and keeps the token while it is valid, renews it, and signs in again when the server refuses it.

pages.title: Veeam Jobs
pages.summary: Lists jobs and their states, starts, stops and retries jobs, enables and disables them.
pages.html:
The Veeam Jobs step works with the backup server's jobs: backup, replication, backup copy and the others.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every Veeam step: see Veeam Backup & Replication.

Operations

OperationVeeam requestResult
List jobsGET /api/v1/jobs{ items, count, total, truncated } Name: a pattern, with * at the start and / or end.
List job statesGET /api/v1/jobs/states{ items, count, total, truncated }: each job's status, last result, last and next run.
Get a jobGET /api/v1/jobs/{id}The job and its settings.
Start a jobPOST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/startThe session started: its id is what Veeam Sessions waits for. Optionally an active full backup.
Stop a jobPOST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/stopGracefully (the machines being processed finish), or at once.
Retry a jobPOST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/retryThe machines that failed in its last run; the session started.
Enable a jobPOST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/enable—
Disable a jobPOST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/disable—

Settings

SettingDescription

pages.title: FortiGate
pages.summary: Block IPs, manage addresses, policies, users and VPN, read the state and back up the configuration of FortiGate firewalls.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to FortiGate firewalls (FortiOS 7.x) through the FortiOS REST API. Its steps are in the Security group of the step list:

  • FortiGate Addresses: blocks and unblocks IPs through an address group, and manages address objects and groups.
  • FortiGate Banned IPs: bans IPs for a time (the firewall's quarantine), lists and lifts bans.
  • FortiGate Policies: lists firewall policies and their hit counts, enables and disables policies.
  • FortiGate Users & VPN: local users (enable, disable), signed-in users (sign out), SSL VPN sessions and IPsec tunnels.
  • FortiGate System: status, resource usage, interfaces, HA, licenses, and the configuration backed up into Files.
  • FortiGate API: sends any request of the FortiOS REST API.

The FortiGate event trigger starts a workflow from a FortiGate automation stitch: a log event, an IOC, an HA failover, a configuration change.

The credential

On the FortiGate, create a REST API administrator (System > Administrators > Create New > REST API Admin) with a profile that allows what the workflows do, and add Rail22's address to its Trusted Hosts. Copy the API key it shows: it is shown only once. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a FortiGate credential, in the Security group:

SettingDescription
FirewallIts HTTPS administration address, with the port when it is not 443, such as https://fw.example.local:8443.
API tokenThe REST API administrator's key, sent as Authorization: Bearer. It is stored encrypted.
VDOMWith VDOMs: the one the steps work in. Empty: the administrator's.
Trust the firewall's certificateFor FortiGate's own self-signed certificate.

Test shows the firewall's hostname, model, FortiOS version and serial number.

Note: give the REST API administrator only the permissions the workflows need: read-only for reports, Firewall read-write to block addresses, System for backups.

Firewalls in your network

A firewall's administration address is usually private. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • IP addresses are a list, text separated by commas or lines, or a list of objects: their ip or srcip is used. Each is checked before anything is sent.
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the query of a read (such as {"filter": "name=@web"}) or to the body of a change. See Fortinet's REST API reference.
  • Errors: FortiOS's error numbers are named, such as an object of that name already exists (-5) or the object does not exist (-3). With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

IPv6 addresses go to the IPv6 tables (address6, addrgrp6): create an IPv6 group of the same name for them.

Setting up blocking

  1. On the FortiGate, create an address group, such as Rail22 blocked (and an IPv6 one of the same name when you block IPv6 too).
  2. Create a deny policy with that group as its source (or destination), above the policies that would allow the traffic.
  3. In the step, choose Block IPs with that group.

Example

With the GravityZone event or FortiGate event trigger: Block IPs with IP addresses {{ fgt.srcip }}, then a Wait of 24 hours and Unblock IPs. For a time-limited block without objects, see FortiGate Banned IPs.

pages.title: Sophos Firewall
pages.summary: Block IPs and domains, manage hosts, groups, rules, users and VPN, and read the interfaces and zones of Sophos Firewalls.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Sophos Firewall (SFOS 18 and later) through its XML API. Its steps are in the Security group of the step list:

  • Sophos Firewall Hosts: blocks and unblocks IPs through an IP host group, and manages IP hosts, FQDN hosts and host groups.
  • Sophos Firewall Rules: lists firewall rules, enables and disables them.
  • Sophos Firewall Users & VPN: users (enable, disable), IPsec connections and SSL VPN policies.
  • Sophos Firewall Web: blocks and unblocks domains through a web filter URL group.
  • Sophos Firewall System: the hostname and API version, interfaces, zones and gateways.
  • Sophos Firewall API: sends any request of the XML API.

Sophos Firewall has no webhooks, so there is no Sophos trigger. To start a workflow from a firewall event, run it on a Schedule, or from another product's trigger, such as the GravityZone event.

The credential

On the firewall, under Backup & firmware > API, turn on the API configuration and add Rail22's address to Allowed IP address. Create an administrator whose profile allows what the workflows do. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Sophos Firewall credential, in the Security group:

SettingDescription
FirewallIts HTTPS administration address, with the port (4444 unless changed), such as https://fw.example.local:4444.
User nameThe administrator the steps sign in as.
PasswordIts password. It is stored encrypted, and sent with each request, as the XML API asks.
Trust the firewall's certificateFor the firewall's own self-signed certificate.

Test shows the firewall's hostname and its API version.

Note: use an administrator just for Rail22, with a profile that gives only what the workflows need: read-only for reports, read-write on Objects to block addresses, on Firewall to turn rules on and off.

Firewalls in your network

A firewall's administration address is usually private. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items). The XML API sends the whole list: total is how many it sent.
  • IP addresses are a list, text separated by commas or lines, or a list of objects: their ip or srcip is used. Each is checked before anything is sent.
  • Changes read the entity, change it and send it back whole, as the XML API replaces an entity on update: the other members of a group, the other fields of a rule are kept.
  • Other fields, under Advanced…, is a JSON object of more fields of the entity a change sends, such as {"Description": "From Rail22"}. See Sophos's XML API reference.
  • Errors are the firewall's own messages with their status code, such as status 502: Operation failed. Entity having same name already exists. A refused sign-in, the API turned off (532) or an address not allowed (534) say what to do. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

pages.title: Sophos Firewall Hosts
pages.summary: Blocks and unblocks IPs through an IP host group, and manages IP hosts, FQDN hosts and host groups.
pages.html:
The Sophos Firewall Hosts step manages the firewall's IP hosts, FQDN hosts and IP host groups, and blocks IPs the usual way: an IP host per IP, in a host group that a drop rule uses.

The credential, Other fields, the list results and the errors are the same for every Sophos Firewall step: see Sophos Firewall.

Operations

OperationXML API requestResult
Block IPs (host + group)Set add IPHost, Set update IPHostGroupEach IP made an IP host named Name prefix + the IP, and put in Group (IPv6 ones in IPv6 group): { group, group6, hosts, count }. A host or membership that exists already is fine: blocking again changes nothing.
Unblock IPsSet update IPHostGroup, Remove IPHostEach taken out of its group, and its host deleted when chosen. One not blocked is fine.
List IP hostsGet IPHost{ items, count, total, truncated } Name contains: a filter; IPv4 or IPv6.
Get a hostGet IPHost (or FQDNHost)The host.
Create a hostSet add IPHost (or FQDNHost)An IP, a network (a CIDR such as 10.1.2.0/24, ip mask, or an IPv6 prefix), an IP range, or an FQDN: { name, message }.
Delete a hostRemove IPHost (or FQDNHost){ name, message }
List IP host groupsGet IPHostGroup{ items, count, total, truncated } IPv4 or IPv6.
Add a host to a groupSet update IPHostGroupThe group's other hosts kept: { name, group, message }.
Remove a host from a groupSet update IPHostGroup{ name, group, message }

Settings

SettingDescription
Sophos Firewall credentialA Sophos Firewall credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Block IPs (host + group); Unblock IPs; List IP hosts; Get a host; Create a host; Delete a host; List IP host groups; Add a host to a group; Remove a host from a group. Default: Block IPs (host + group). Required.
IP addressesA list, or separated by commas / lines (IPv4 or IPv6), e.g. {{ fgt.srcip }}. (Required for: Block IPs (host + group); Unblock IPs.)
GroupThe IP host group (used by a drop rule, to block). (Required for: Block IPs (host + group); Unblock IPs; Add a host to a group; Remove a host from a group.)
IPv6 groupThe IPv6 host group, for IPv6 addresses (empty: IPv6 addresses refused). (For: Block IPs (host + group); Unblock IPs.)
Name prefixThe hosts are named <prefix><ip> (an IPv6 address's colons as dashes). Default: r22-block-. (For: Block IPs (host + group); Unblock IPs.)
Delete the hosts tooDefault: on. (For: Unblock IPs.)
Name containsEmpty: all. (For: List IP hosts; List IP host groups.)
IPv6Default: off. (For: List IP hosts; List IP host groups.)
HostThe host's name. (Required for: Get a host; Create a host; Delete a host; Add a host to a group; Remove a host from a group.)
TypeChoices: IP / network; IP range; FQDN. Default: IP / network. (For: Get a host; Create a host; Delete a host.)
ValueIP / network: 10.1.2.3, 10.1.2.0/24, "10.1.2.0 255.255.255.0" or 2001:db8::/64; range: 10.1.2.10-10.1.2.20; FQDN: host.example.com. (Required for: Create a host.)
DescriptionShown on the firewall. (For: Create a host; Block IPs (host + group).)
Other fieldsA JSON object of more fields of the entity a change sends (e.g. {"Description": "From Rail22"}): see the Sophos Firewall API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List IP hosts; List IP host groups.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else the entity, or what was changed. Default: hosts. Required.
On errorThe firewall's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

A host group holds hosts of one IP family, and a name is unique among all the hosts and groups: IPv6 addresses need their own group, with another name (such as Rail22 blocked v6). An IPv6 host's name has dashes for the colons: r22-block-2001-db8--66.

Setting up blocking

  1. On the firewall, under Hosts and services > IP host group, create a group, such as Rail22 blocked (and an IPv6 one when you block IPv6 too).
  2. Create a firewall rule that drops traffic from that group (as source, or as destination for outgoing traffic), above the rules that would allow it.
  3. In the step, choose Block IPs with that group.

Example

With the GravityZone event trigger: Block IPs with IP addresses {{ gz.srcip }}, then a Wait of 24 hours and Unblock IPs.

A rule that allows a partner's access, made in advance and kept off: a workflow with a Form trigger and an approval enables it, and a Wait disables it again at the end of the day.

pages.title: Sophos Firewall Users & VPN
pages.summary: Users (enable, disable), IPsec connections and SSL VPN policies.
pages.html:
The Sophos Firewall Users & VPN step works with the firewall's users and VPN connections. A user made inactive can no longer sign in: remote access VPN, the captive portal, the user portal.

The credential, Other fields, the list results and the errors are the same for every Sophos Firewall step: see Sophos Firewall.

OperationXML API requestResult
List usersGet User{ items, count, total, truncated } User name contains: a filter.
Get a userGet UserThe user, by user name.
Enable a userSet update UserThe user read, its Status set to Active, sent back: { user, status, message }. Its password is kept.
Disable a userSet update UserThe same, with Inactive. One inactive already is fine.

OperationChoices: List users; Get a user; Enable a user; Disable a user; List IPsec connections; List SSL VPN policies. Default: Disable a user. Required.

UserThe user name. (Required for: Get a user; Enable a user; Disable a user.)
Other fieldsA JSON object of more fields of the entity a change sends (e.g. {"Description": "From Rail22"}): see the Sophos Firewall API reference. (Under Advanced….)

When a person leaves, the offboarding workflow disables their account in the directory with LDAP, and their firewall user with Disable a user.

pages.title: Sophos Firewall Web
pages.summary: Blocks and unblocks domains through a web filter URL group.
pages.html:
The Sophos Firewall Web step puts domains in, or takes them out of, a URL group of the web filter. A web policy that blocks the group blocks the domains.

The credential, Other fields, the list results and the errors are the same for every Sophos Firewall step: see Sophos Firewall.

Operations

OperationXML API requestResult
Block domains (URL group)Set update WebFilterURLGroupThe domains added to the group's list (the others kept): { group, domains, count, message }. One there already is fine.
Unblock domainsSet update WebFilterURLGroupThe domains taken out. One not there is fine.
List URL groupsGet WebFilterURLGroup{ items, count, total, truncated } Name contains: a filter.
Get a URL groupGet WebFilterURLGroupThe group and its URLlist.

Settings

SettingDescription
Sophos Firewall credentialA Sophos Firewall credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Block domains (URL group); Unblock domains; List URL groups; Get a URL group. Default: Block domains (URL group). Required.
DomainsA list, or separated by commas / lines, e.g. bad.example.com. (Required for: Block domains (URL group); Unblock domains.)
URL groupThe URL group (blocked by a web policy). (Required for: Block domains (URL group); Unblock domains; Get a URL group.)
Name containsEmpty: all. (For: List URL groups.)
Other fieldsA JSON object of more fields of the entity a change sends (e.g. {"Description": "From Rail22"}): see the Sophos Firewall API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List URL groups.)

Domains are a list, or text separated by commas or lines. They are made lower case, and a URL is taken as its host: https://www.example.com/page blocks www.example.com.

Setting up blocking

  1. On the firewall, under Web > URL groups, create a group, such as Rail22 blocked.
  2. In the web policies your firewall rules use, add a rule that blocks that group.
  3. In the step, choose Block domains with that group.

pages.title: Sophos Firewall API
pages.summary: Sends any request of the Sophos Firewall XML API.
pages.html:
The Sophos Firewall API step sends any request of the XML API, for what the other Sophos Firewall steps don't cover: services, NAT rules, web policies, IPS, DHCP. It is an advanced step.

Write the Request as in Sophos's XML API reference: what follows <Login> inside <Request>, such as <Get>, <Set operation="add"> or <Remove>. Rail22 adds the login. {{ }} work in it, but values aren't escaped: a value with & or < must be written as XML. The result is the firewall's answer as JSON: { APIVersion, <entity>: its fields, … }. A repeated element is a list.

<Get>
  <Services>
    <Filter><key name="Name" criteria="like">web</key></Filter>
  </Services>
</Get>

The credential, Other fields, the list results and the errors are the same for every Sophos Firewall step: see Sophos Firewall.

Settings

SettingDescription
Sophos Firewall credentialA Sophos Firewall credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Send a request. Default: Send a request. Required.
RequestWhat follows <Login> in <Request>, e.g. <Get><Services/></Get> (the login is added). (Required for: Send a request.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else the entity, or what was changed. Default: sfos. Required.
On errorThe firewall's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Wazuh
pages.summary: Alerts, vulnerabilities, agents, active response, scans and inventory of a Wazuh installation.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Wazuh (4.8 and later) through its two APIs: the Server API, for the agents and everything the manager does, and the Wazuh indexer, which holds the alerts and the vulnerabilities. Its steps are in the Security group of the step list:

  • Wazuh Alerts: searches and counts alerts by level, agent, rule, group and MITRE technique, and their most frequent values.
  • Wazuh Vulnerabilities: what the vulnerability detector found, per agent, severity, CVE and package.
  • Wazuh Agents: lists, creates, restarts and deletes agents, their keys and their groups.
  • Wazuh Active Response: blocks an IP on agents, or runs a command on them.
  • Wazuh Scans: security configuration assessment, file integrity and rootcheck: results, and starting scans.
  • Wazuh Inventory: an agent's operating system, hardware, packages, processes, open ports, addresses and hotfixes.
  • Wazuh Manager: the daemons, the cluster, the log, the rules and decoders, and restarting the manager.
  • Wazuh API: any request to the Server API or the indexer.

The Wazuh alert trigger starts a workflow on new alerts.

The credential

In Wazuh, create an API user (Server management > Security in the dashboard) with the roles the workflows need, and an indexer user that may read wazuh-alerts-* and wazuh-states-vulnerabilities-*. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Wazuh credential, in the Security group:

SettingDescription
Server APIThe manager's address with its port, such as https://wazuh.example.local:55000.
API user, API passwordSigns in for a token, which is renewed when it expires. The password is stored encrypted.
IndexerIts address with its port, such as https://wazuh.example.local:9200. Without it, Wazuh Alerts, Wazuh Vulnerabilities and the Wazuh alert trigger cannot run; the other steps can.
Indexer user, Indexer passwordSent as HTTP Basic. The password is stored encrypted.
Trust the servers' certificatesFor a default installation's self-signed certificates.

Test shows the Wazuh version and host, and how many alerts the indexer user can read.

Servers in your network

A Wazuh server is usually on your internal network. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • Agents are given by id: 1 and 001 are the same agent. An agent or an alert works as well, so {{ alert }} names the agent of an alert. Several are separated by commas, or given as a list.
  • Every agent must be asked for with all. An empty Agents is an error, never every agent, even though it means that to Wazuh's own API. Wazuh Agents does not delete with all.
  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Changes give { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Wazuh handles each agent on its own: when some fail, the step succeeds and failed says which and why; when all fail, it is an error.
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the query of the Server API, such as {"q": "os.platform=ubuntu"}; to the body of what Wazuh Agents creates; or to the search of the indexer, such as {"_source": ["rule", "agent"]}.
  • Errors: Wazuh's message and its code, such as An agent with the same name already exists (error 1708). With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

pages.title: Wazuh Alerts
pages.summary: Searches and counts the alerts in the Wazuh indexer, and finds their most frequent values.
pages.html:
The Wazuh Alerts step reads the alerts from the Wazuh indexer (wazuh-alerts-*), so the credential needs the indexer.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Wazuh step: see Wazuh.

Operations

OperationWazuh requestResult
Search alertsPOST /wazuh-alerts-*/_search{ items, count, total, truncated }: the alerts that match, newest first, each as Wazuh wrote it, with _id and _index: {{ a.rule.level }}, {{ a.rule.description }}, {{ a.agent.name }}, {{ a.data.srcip }}, {{ a.full_log }}. The indexer gives at most 10,000 in one search.
Get an alertPOST /wazuh-alerts-*/_searchThe alert with that _id.
Count alertsPOST /wazuh-alerts-*/_search{ count }.
Most frequent valuesPOST /wazuh-alerts-*/_search{ field, items: [ { value, count } ], total }: for example the rules that fired most in the last 24 hours.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialA Wazuh credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Search alerts; Get an alert; Count alerts; Most frequent values. Default: Search alerts. Required.
Level and worseOf the rule, 0 to 16; empty: every level. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
AgentsTheir ids or names, separated by commas; empty: every agent. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
RulesTheir ids, separated by commas; empty: every rule. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
Rule groupsSeparated by commas, any of them, e.g. authentication_failed; empty: every group. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
MITRE techniquesTheir ids, separated by commas, e.g. T1110; empty: all. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
QueryIn Lucene syntax, e.g. data.srcip:"10.0.0.5" AND NOT agent.name:web*. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
FromA date / time, or e.g. -1 hour, yesterday; empty: the last 24 hours. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
ToEmpty: now. (For: Search alerts, Count alerts, Most frequent values.)
AlertIts _id (Search alerts, or the Wazuh alert trigger). (Required for: Get an alert.)
OfChoices: Rule; Rule description; Rule group; MITRE technique; Agent; Source IP; Target user. Default: Rule. (Required for: Most frequent values.)
How manyDefault: 10. (For: Most frequent values.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of the Server API (e.g. {"q": "os.platform=ubuntu"}), to the body of what it creates, or to the search of the indexer (e.g. {"_source": ["rule", "agent"]}).
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: Search alerts.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; a change: { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Default: alerts. Required.
On errorWazuh's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

An alert's content comes from the logs of the monitored machines, so an attacker can influence it. Check values such as {{ alert.data.srcip }} before a workflow acts on them.

pages.title: Wazuh Agents
pages.summary: Lists, creates, restarts and deletes Wazuh agents, their keys and their groups.
pages.html:
The Wazuh Agents step manages the agents and their groups.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Wazuh step: see Wazuh.

Operations

OperationWazuh requestResult
List agentsGET /agents{ items, count, total, truncated }: of the statuses and group given.
Get an agentGET /agentsThe agent: id, name, ip, status, group, os, version, lastKeepAlive.

Get an agent's keyGET /agents/<id>/key{ id, key }.
Restart agentsPUT /agents/restart{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }.

List groupsGET /groups{ items, count, total, truncated }.
List a group's agentsGET /groups/<group>/agents{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Add agents to a groupPUT /agents/group{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }.
Remove agents from a groupDELETE /agents/group{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }.
Create a groupPOST /groups{ group, message }.
Delete a groupDELETE /groups{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialA Wazuh credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List agents; Get an agent; Count per status; List outdated agents; Create an agent; Get an agent's key; Restart agents; Delete agents; List groups; List a group's agents; Add agents to a group; Remove agents from a group; Create a group; Delete a group. Default: List agents. Required.
StatusEmpty: every status. Choices: Active; Disconnected; Pending; Never connected. (For: List agents, List a group's agents.)
GroupIts name (List agents: empty: every group). (For: List agents, List a group's agents, Add agents to a group, Remove agents from a group, Create a group, Delete a group.) (Required for: List a group's agents, Add agents to a group, Remove agents from a group, Create a group, Delete a group.)
ContainingA text in any field; empty: all. (For: List agents, List outdated agents, List groups, List a group's agents.)
AgentIts id; an agent or an alert works too. (Required for: Get an agent, Get an agent's key.)
AgentsTheir ids, separated by commas, or a list of agents or alerts. Or all, for every agent (not to delete). (Required for: Restart agents, Delete agents, Add agents to a group, Remove agents from a group.)
NameThe new agent's name: letters, digits, _ - . (Required for: Create an agent.)
IP addressThe address it connects from, a network or any; empty: found by Wazuh. (For: Create an agent.)
Remove from the key storeElse its key is only marked removed. Default: off. (For: Delete agents.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of the Server API (e.g. {"q": "os.platform=ubuntu"}), to the body of what it creates, or to the search of the indexer (e.g. {"_source": ["rule", "agent"]}).
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List agents, List outdated agents, List groups, List a group's agents.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; a change: { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Default: agents. Required.
On errorWazuh's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Note: an agent's key lets whoever holds it enroll as that agent. It is in the run's variables, so limit who can read the run. For an AI step, Get an agent's key and Create an agent count as write operations: they are not offered by default, and ask for approval when approvals are on.

pages.title: Wazuh Active Response
pages.summary: Blocks an IP on Wazuh agents, or runs a command on them.
pages.html:
The Wazuh Active Response step sends a response to agents (PUT /active-response).

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Wazuh step: see Wazuh.

Operations

OperationWazuh requestResult
Block an IPPUT /active-response{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }: the script chosen, run with the address as the alert's data.srcip.
Run a commandPUT /active-response{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }: a command defined in the manager's ossec.conf, or !script for a script in the agent's active-response/bin.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialA Wazuh credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Block an IP; Run a command. Default: Block an IP. Required.
AgentsTheir ids, separated by commas, or a list of agents or alerts. Or all, for every agent. (Required for: Block an IP, Run a command.)
IP addressTo block on those agents. (Required for: Block an IP.)
ScriptChoices: firewall-drop (Linux, iptables); host-deny (Linux, /etc/hosts.deny); route-null (Linux); netsh (Windows); route-null (Windows). Default: firewall-drop (Linux, iptables). (Required for: Block an IP.)
CommandA command of the manager's ossec.conf, or !script for a script on the agent. (Required for: Run a command.)
ArgumentsOne per line, or a list. (For: Run a command.)
Alert dataA JSON object the script reads as the alert's data, e.g. {"srcip": "203.0.113.5"}. (For: Run a command.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of the Server API (e.g. {"q": "os.platform=ubuntu"}), to the body of what it creates, or to the search of the indexer (e.g. {"_source": ["rule", "agent"]}).
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; a change: { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Default: response. Required.
On errorWazuh's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Note: Wazuh answers when the command has been sent, not when it has run: an agent that is disconnected, or does not have the script, is not reported as failing here. Check the result on the agent, for example with the agent's active-responses.log.

Wazuh's API has no request that undoes a block: to lift one, remove it on the host, or run a script of your own that does.

Choose the script for the agents' system. firewall-drop needs iptables on the agent.

Example

With the Wazuh alert trigger on brute-force rules: Agents {{ alert }}, IP address {{ alert.data.srcip }}. Add an If first that leaves out your own networks: the address comes from a log line.

pages.title: Wazuh Scans
pages.summary: Security configuration assessment, file integrity and rootcheck of a Wazuh agent: results, and starting scans.
pages.html:
The Wazuh Scans step reads what an agent's scans found, and starts scans.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Wazuh step: see Wazuh.

Operations

OperationWazuh requestResult
SCA: list policiesGET /sca/<id>{ items, count, total, truncated }: each policy with policy_id, pass, fail and score.
SCA: list a policy's checksGET /sca/<id>/checks/<policy>{ items, count, total, truncated }: each check with title, result, remediation.
FIM: list filesGET /syscheck/<id>{ items, count, total, truncated }: the files file integrity monitoring knows, with their hashes.
FIM: last scanGET /syscheck/<id>/last_scan{ start, end }.
FIM: run a scanPUT /syscheck{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }.
Rootcheck: list findingsGET /rootcheck/<id>{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Rootcheck: run a scanPUT /rootcheck{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialA Wazuh credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: SCA: list policies; SCA: list a policy's checks; FIM: list files; FIM: last scan; FIM: run a scan; Rootcheck: list findings; Rootcheck: run a scan. Default: SCA: list policies. Required.
AgentIts id; an agent or an alert works too. (Required for: SCA: list policies, SCA: list a policy's checks, FIM: list files, FIM: last scan, Rootcheck: list findings.)
AgentsTheir ids, separated by commas, or a list of agents or alerts. Or all, for every agent. (Required for: FIM: run a scan, Rootcheck: run a scan.)
PolicyIts policy_id (SCA: list policies). (Required for: SCA: list a policy's checks.)
ResultChoices: Any; Failed; Passed; Not applicable. (For: SCA: list a policy's checks.)
FileIts full path; empty: every file. (For: FIM: list files.)
HashMD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 of the file; empty: any. (For: FIM: list files.)
ContainingA text in any field; empty: all. (For: SCA: list policies, SCA: list a policy's checks, FIM: list files, Rootcheck: list findings.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of the Server API (e.g. {"q": "os.platform=ubuntu"}), to the body of what it creates, or to the search of the indexer (e.g. {"_source": ["rule", "agent"]}).
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: SCA: list policies, SCA: list a policy's checks, FIM: list files, Rootcheck: list findings.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; a change: { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Default: scan. Required.
On errorWazuh's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Wazuh Inventory
pages.summary: An agent's operating system, hardware, packages, processes, open ports, addresses and hotfixes.
pages.html:
The Wazuh Inventory step reads what Wazuh's syscollector knows of an agent (GET /syscollector/<id>/<operation>). Operating system and Hardware give one item; the others give { items, count, total, truncated }.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Wazuh step: see Wazuh.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialA Wazuh credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Operating system; Hardware; Packages; Processes; Open ports; Network addresses; Windows hotfixes. Default: Packages. Required.
AgentIts id; an agent or an alert works too. (Required for: Operating system, Hardware, Packages, Processes, Open ports, Network addresses, Windows hotfixes.)
ContainingA text in any field; empty: all. (For: Packages, Processes, Open ports, Network addresses, Windows hotfixes.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of the Server API (e.g. {"q": "os.platform=ubuntu"}), to the body of what it creates, or to the search of the indexer (e.g. {"_source": ["rule", "agent"]}).
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: Packages, Processes, Open ports, Network addresses, Windows hotfixes.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; a change: { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Default: inventory. Required.
On errorWazuh's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Wazuh Manager
pages.summary: The Wazuh manager's daemons, cluster, log, rules and decoders, and restarting it.
pages.html:
The Wazuh Manager step reads the state and the ruleset of the manager.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Wazuh step: see Wazuh.

Operations

OperationWazuh requestResult
Daemons' statusGET /manager/statusEach daemon and its state, such as { "wazuh-analysisd": "running" }. The log names any daemon that is neither running nor stopped.
InformationGET /manager/infoversion, type, path and more.
Cluster statusGET /cluster/status{ enabled, running }.
Read the logGET /manager/logs{ items, count, total, truncated }: lines of the level and daemon given.
List rulesGET /rules{ items, count, total, truncated }.
List decodersGET /decoders{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Restart the managerPUT /manager/restart{ affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. The manager stops processing events while it restarts.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialA Wazuh credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Daemons' status; Information; Cluster status; Read the log; List rules; List decoders; Restart the manager. Default: Daemons' status. Required.
LevelChoices: Any; Critical; Error; Warning; Info; Debug. (For: Read the log.)
Daemone.g. wazuh-analysisd; empty: every daemon. (For: Read the log.)
RulesTheir ids, separated by commas; empty: every rule. (For: List rules.)
LevelOne (10) or a range (7-10); empty: every level. (For: List rules.)
Groupe.g. authentication_failed; empty: every group. (For: List rules.)
ContainingA text in any field; empty: all. (For: Read the log, List rules, List decoders.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of the Server API (e.g. {"q": "os.platform=ubuntu"}), to the body of what it creates, or to the search of the indexer (e.g. {"_source": ["rule", "agent"]}).
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: Read the log, List rules, List decoders.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; a change: { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Default: manager. Required.
On errorWazuh's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Wazuh API
pages.summary: Any request to the Wazuh Server API or indexer.
pages.html:
The Wazuh API step sends any request: what the other Wazuh steps do not have, such as MITRE, CDB lists, the ruleset's files, agent upgrades or other indices. It is an advanced step.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Wazuh step: see Wazuh.

Settings

SettingDescription
Wazuh credentialA Wazuh credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Server API request; Indexer request. Default: Server API request. Required.
MethodChoices: GET; POST; PUT; DELETE. Default: GET. (Required for: Server API request, Indexer request.)
Pathe.g. /mitre/techniques, or to the indexer /wazuh-alerts-*/_search ({{ }} allowed). (Required for: Server API request, Indexer request.)
QueryA JSON object (empty: none), e.g. {"limit": 10}. (For: Server API request, Indexer request.)
BodyA JSON object (empty: none). (For: Server API request, Indexer request.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; a change: { affected, failed, count, failedCount, message }. Default: wazuh. Required.
On errorWazuh's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

The result is the answer as it is. For example, the techniques of a tactic: Server API request, GET, path /mitre/techniques, query {"search": "credential-access", "limit": 10}.

pages.title: Checkmk
pages.summary: Problems, states, acknowledgements, downtimes and hosts of a Checkmk monitoring site.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Checkmk sites (2.2 and later) through the Checkmk REST API. Its steps are in the Monitoring group of the step list:

  • Checkmk Status: current problems, a host's state and its services, and any Livestatus query.
  • Checkmk Acknowledge & Downtime: acknowledges host and service problems, schedules and removes downtimes.
  • Checkmk Hosts: lists, creates and deletes monitored hosts, discovers their services and activates changes.
  • Checkmk API: sends any request of the Checkmk REST API.

The Checkmk problem trigger starts a workflow when a new problem appears, and optionally when it clears.

The credential

In Checkmk, create an automation user (Setup > Users > Add user, with an Automation secret for machine accounts) with the roles the workflows need. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Checkmk credential, in the Monitoring group:

SettingDescription
ServerThe Checkmk server's address, without the site, such as https://monitoring.example.local.
SiteThe site's name, as in its address https://<server>/<site>/.
Automation user, Automation secretSent as Authorization: Bearer <user> <secret>. The secret is stored encrypted.
Trust the server's certificateOnly for a self-signed certificate.

Test shows the site, its Checkmk version and edition.

Servers in your network

A monitoring server is usually on your internal network. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the body of a change (such as {"sticky": false}) or to the query of a read (such as more columns). See the REST API documentation of your Checkmk.
  • Errors: Checkmk's message, with the fields it refused, such as host_name: Host "web01" already exists. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

pages.title: Checkmk Status
pages.summary: Current problems, a host's state and its services, and any Livestatus query.
pages.html:
The Checkmk Status step reads what Checkmk monitors, now, through Livestatus.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every Checkmk step: see Checkmk.

Operations

OperationCheckmk requestResult
List current problemsGET domain-types/host|service/collections/all{ items, count, total, truncated }: hosts DOWN or UNREACH and services WARN or worse (or CRIT and worse), of a host or all, each { kind, host_name, service, state, stateText, output, since, acknowledged, inDowntime }. Acknowledged problems and those in a downtime are left out unless chosen.
Get a host's stateGET domain-types/host|service/collections/all{ host, services }: the host's state and every service of it.
List servicesGET domain-types/service/collections/all{ items, count, total, truncated }: the services of a host (or all), of a state.
Livestatus queryGET domain-types/host|service/collections/all{ items, count, total, truncated }: the rows of the table, with a filter (JSON) and the columns you give.

Settings

SettingDescription
Checkmk credentialA Checkmk credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List current problems; Get a host's state; List services; Livestatus query. Default: List current problems. Required.
HostIts name; empty: every host (not for a host's state). (Required for: List current problems; Get a host's state; List services.)
ServicesChoices: WARN and worse; CRIT and worse. Default: WARN and worse. (For: List current problems.)
With acknowledged problemsDefault: off. (For: List current problems.)
With problems in a downtimeDefault: off. (For: List current problems.)
StateChoices: All; Not OK; OK; WARN; CRIT; UNKNOWN. Default: All. (For: List services.)
TableChoices: Services; Hosts. Default: Services. (For: Livestatus query.)
ColumnsSeparated by commas, e.g. host_name, description, state, plugin_output. (For: Livestatus query.)
FilterA Livestatus filter as JSON (empty: all), e.g. {"op": ">", "left": "state", "right": 0}. (For: Livestatus query.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the body of a change (e.g. {"sticky": true}) or to the query of a read: see the Checkmk REST API documentation. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List current problems; List services; Livestatus query.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else Checkmk's answer. Default: status. Required.
On errorCheckmk's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

stateText is OK, WARN, CRIT or UNKNOWN for a service, UP, DOWN or UNREACH for a host.

Example

A morning summary: a Schedule Trigger at 07:30, List current problems, then Send email with a Loop over {{ status.items }}, or nothing when {{ status.count }} is 0.

pages.title: Checkmk Acknowledge & Downtime
pages.summary: Acknowledges host and service problems, schedules and removes downtimes.
pages.html:
The Checkmk Acknowledge & Downtime step acknowledges problems, so Checkmk stops notifying about them, and schedules downtimes for maintenance.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every Checkmk step: see Checkmk.

Operations

OperationCheckmk requestResult
Acknowledge a host problemPOST domain-types/acknowledge/collections/host—
Acknowledge service problemsPOST domain-types/acknowledge/collections/serviceOne acknowledgement per service.
Schedule a host downtimePOST domain-types/downtime/collections/hostFrom Start (empty: now) for Minutes.
Schedule a service downtimePOST domain-types/downtime/collections/service—
List downtimesGET domain-types/downtime/collections/all{ items, count, total, truncated }.
Remove a downtimePOST domain-types/downtime/actions/delete/invokeBy its id, on the credential's site.

Settings

SettingDescription
Checkmk credentialA Checkmk credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Acknowledge a host problem; Acknowledge service problems; Schedule a host downtime; Schedule a service downtime; List downtimes; Remove a downtime. Default: Acknowledge service problems. Required.
HostIts name (List downtimes: empty: all). (Required for: Acknowledge a host problem; Acknowledge service problems; Schedule a host downtime; Schedule a service downtime; List downtimes.)
ServicesTheir names, one per line, or a list. (Required for: Acknowledge service problems; Schedule a service downtime.)
CommentShown in Checkmk. (Required for: Acknowledge a host problem; Acknowledge service problems; Schedule a host downtime; Schedule a service downtime.)
StickyKept until the state is OK again (else removed at any state change). Default: on. (For: Acknowledge a host problem; Acknowledge service problems.)
NotifySend the acknowledgement notification. Default: off. (For: Acknowledge a host problem; Acknowledge service problems.)
Persistent commentDefault: off. (For: Acknowledge a host problem; Acknowledge service problems.)
StartA date / time, or e.g. +1 hour, tomorrow 22:00; empty: now. (For: Schedule a host downtime; Schedule a service downtime.)
MinutesDefault: 60. (Required for: Schedule a host downtime; Schedule a service downtime.)
DowntimeIts id (List downtimes). (Required for: Remove a downtime.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the body of a change (e.g. {"sticky": true}) or to the query of a read: see the Checkmk REST API documentation. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List downtimes.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else Checkmk's answer. Default: ack. Required.
On errorCheckmk's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Services are given one per line (a service's name may hold commas), or as a list. Start takes a date and time, or words such as +1 hour or tomorrow 22:00.

Example

With the Checkmk problem trigger: a ticket in a Data Table, then Acknowledge service problems with Host {{ cmk.host_name }}, Services {{ cmk.service }} and the comment Ticket {{ ticket.row.id }}.

pages.title: Checkmk Hosts
pages.summary: Lists, creates and deletes monitored hosts, discovers their services and activates changes.
pages.html:
The Checkmk Hosts step changes what Checkmk monitors: its hosts and their services.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every Checkmk step: see Checkmk.

Operations

OperationCheckmk requestResult
List hostsGET domain-types/host_config/collections/all{ items, count, total, truncated }: each with its folder and attributes.
Get a hostGET objects/host_config/{host}Its configuration.
Create a hostPOST domain-types/host_config/collections/allIn a folder, with an IP address and an alias; other attributes, such as tags, in Other parameters ({"attributes": {...}}).
Delete a hostDELETE objects/host_config/{host}—
Discover servicesPOST domain-types/service_discovery_run/actions/start/invokeAccept all, add new services only, refresh, or start over.
Activate pending changesPOST domain-types/activation_run/actions/activate-changes/invokeNone pending is fine.
List pending changesGET domain-types/activation_run/collections/pending_changes{ items, count, total, truncated }.

Settings

SettingDescription
Checkmk credentialA Checkmk credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List hosts; Get a host; Create a host; Delete a host; Discover services; Activate pending changes; List pending changes. Default: List hosts. Required.
HostIts name in Checkmk. (Required for: Get a host; Create a host; Delete a host; Discover services.)
Foldere.g. / or /servers/linux. Default: /. (For: Create a host.)
IP addressEmpty: Checkmk resolves the host name. (For: Create a host.)
Alias(For: Create a host.)
DiscoveryChoices: Accept all (new and vanished services, labels); Add new services only; Refresh (search again); Start over (remove all, then add). Default: Accept all (new and vanished services, labels). (For: Discover services.)
Activate changesAfterwards; off: they wait in Checkmk. Default: on. (For: Create a host; Delete a host; Discover services.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the body of a change (e.g. {"sticky": true}) or to the query of a read: see the Checkmk REST API documentation. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List hosts; List pending changes.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else Checkmk's answer. Default: hosts. Required.
On errorCheckmk's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Checkmk applies configuration changes only once they are activated. With Activate changes on (the default), creating, deleting a host or discovering its services activates them right after. Off, they wait for someone to activate them in Checkmk, or for Activate pending changes.

Example

A new server from a provisioning Webhook: Create a host with its name and address, then Discover services: it is monitored a few minutes later.

pages.title: Checkmk API
pages.summary: Sends any request of the Checkmk REST API.
pages.html:
The Checkmk API step sends any request of the Checkmk REST API, for what the other Checkmk steps don't cover: folders, rules, users, contact groups, BI, the agent bakery. It is an advanced step.

Give the Method, the Path after /check_mk/api/1.0, and the Query and Body as JSON objects, as in the REST API documentation of your Checkmk (Help > Developer resources). Changing an existing object needs its ETag in If-Match, or *. {{ }} work in all of them.

Method: GET
Path: /domain-types/folder_config/collections/all
Query: {"parent": "~", "recursive": true}

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every Checkmk step: see Checkmk.

Settings

SettingDescription
Checkmk credentialA Checkmk credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Send a request. Default: Send a request. Required.
MethodChoices: GET; POST; PUT; DELETE. Default: GET. (Required for: Send a request.)
PathAfter /check_mk/api/1.0, e.g. /domain-types/folder_config/collections/all ({{ }} allowed). (Required for: Send a request.)
QueryA JSON object (empty: none), e.g. {"parent": "~"}. (For: Send a request.)
BodyA JSON object (empty: none). (For: Send a request.)
If-MatchThe object's ETag, for changes Checkmk guards (empty: none; * for any). (For: Send a request.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; else Checkmk's answer. Default: cmk. Required.
On errorCheckmk's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Zabbix
pages.summary: Problems, acknowledgements, maintenances, hosts and latest values of a Zabbix server.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Zabbix servers (6.0 LTS and later) through the Zabbix API. Its steps are in the Monitoring group of the step list:

  • Zabbix Problems: current problems by severity, host, host group and tags, and one event with its acknowledgements.
  • Zabbix Acknowledge & Maintenance: acknowledges problems, adds messages, closes them or changes their severity; creates, lists and removes maintenances.
  • Zabbix Hosts: lists, reads, creates, enables, disables and deletes hosts, their latest values, and the host groups.
  • Zabbix API: calls any method of the Zabbix API.

The Zabbix problem trigger starts a workflow when a new problem appears, and optionally when it is resolved.

The credential

In Zabbix, create an API token (Users > API tokens > Create API token) for a user whose role may use the API and sees the hosts the workflows need; for changes (acknowledgements, maintenances, hosts), the user needs the matching permissions. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Zabbix credential, in the Monitoring group:

SettingDescription
ServerThe Zabbix frontend's address, with its path when it has one, such as https://monitor.example.local/zabbix. A pasted page address (…/zabbix.php?action=…) works too.
API tokenSent as Authorization: Bearer <token> to Zabbix 6.4 and later, in the request's auth member to 6.0 and 6.2. It is stored encrypted.
Trust the server's certificateOnly for a self-signed certificate.

Test shows the Zabbix version and how many hosts the token sees.

Servers in your network

A monitoring server is usually on your internal network. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • Hosts are given by their technical name (Host name in Zabbix), host groups and templates by their name: the steps look up their ids. Several are separated by commas, or given as a list.
  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object merged into the parameters of the step's API call, such as {"selectTags": "extend"}. See the API documentation of your Zabbix version.
  • Errors: Zabbix's message and its details, such as Invalid params.: Host with the same name "web01" already exists. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

pages.title: Zabbix Problems
pages.summary: Current problems by severity, host, host group and tags, and one event with its acknowledgements.
pages.html:
The Zabbix Problems step reads what Zabbix reports now.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every Zabbix step: see Zabbix.

Operations

OperationZabbix methodResult
List current problemsproblem.get, event.get{ items, count, total, truncated }: the unresolved problems of the severity and worse, of the hosts, host groups and tags given, newest first, each { eventid, name, severity, severityText, host, hostName, hosts, since, acknowledged, suppressed, opdata, tags, triggerid }. Acknowledged and suppressed problems are left out unless chosen.
Get an eventevent.getThe event, with value (problem or ok) and acknowledges: [ { clock, message, action, user } ].

Settings

SettingDescription
Zabbix credentialA Zabbix credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List current problems; Get an event. Default: List current problems. Required.
SeverityChoices: All severities; Information and worse; Warning and worse; Average and worse; High and worse; Disaster. Default: Warning and worse. (For: List current problems.)

severityText is Not classified, Information, Warning, Average, High or Disaster (severity 0 to 5). host is the first host's technical name, hostName its visible name, tags an object such as { "service": "nginx" }.

Example

A morning summary: a Schedule Trigger at 07:30, List current problems of High and worse, then Send email with a Loop over {{ problems.items }}, or nothing when {{ problems.count }} is 0.

pages.title: Zabbix Acknowledge & Maintenance
pages.summary: Acknowledges problems, adds messages, closes them or changes their severity; creates, lists and removes maintenances.
pages.html:
The Zabbix Acknowledge & Maintenance step updates problems and plans maintenance periods.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every Zabbix step: see Zabbix.

Operations

OperationZabbix methodResult

Unacknowledge problemsevent.acknowledge{ eventids, action }.
Add a message to problemsevent.acknowledge{ eventids, action }.
Create a maintenancemaintenance.create{ maintenanceids, name, start, end }: from now (or Start) for Minutes, for the hosts and host groups given, with or without data collection.
List maintenancesmaintenance.get{ items, count, total, truncated }: each maintenance with its hosts, groups, timeperiods, start and end.
Remove maintenancesmaintenance.delete{ maintenanceids }.

Settings

SettingDescription
Zabbix credentialA Zabbix credential of the project. Required.

Events takes ids separated by commas, or a list: of ids, or of objects with an eventid, such as {{ problems.items }} of Zabbix Problems or the Zabbix problem trigger's variable.

Example

Before a patch window: Create a maintenance of the host group Linux servers from tomorrow 22:00 for 120 minutes, with data collection, so no problem notifications are sent while the servers restart.

pages.title: Zabbix Hosts

A new server, from a form: a Form with its name and address, then Create a host in Linux servers with the template Linux by Zabbix agent, then Send email to the team.

pages.title: Zabbix API

pages.html:
The Zabbix API step calls any method of the Zabbix API: what the other Zabbix steps do not have, such as triggers, templates, history, users or services. It is an advanced step.

The credential and the errors are the same as for every Zabbix step: see Zabbix. The token is sent as the other steps send it.

Settings

SettingDescription
Zabbix credentialA Zabbix credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Call a method. Default: Call a method. Required.
Methode.g. trigger.get, history.get, template.get ({{ }} allowed). (Required for: Call a method.)
ParametersA JSON object or list (empty: none), e.g. {"output": ["description"], "only_true": true}. (For: Call a method.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.

The result is Zabbix's result. For example, the triggers in problem state of a host: method trigger.get, parameters {"output": ["description", "priority"], "host": "web01", "only_true": true}.

pages.title: VMware vCenter
pages.summary: Virtual machines, power, snapshots, inventory, maintenance mode and alarms of a VMware vCenter Server.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to VMware vCenter Server (vSphere 8) through its vSphere Automation REST API and its VI/JSON API. Its steps are in the Virtualization group of the step list:

  • VMware VMs: lists VMs, powers them on and off, shuts down and restarts guests, reads guest information, clones and deletes VMs.
  • VMware Snapshots: lists, creates, reverts to and removes snapshots, and removes old ones.
  • VMware Inventory: hosts, clusters, datacenters, datastores with their free space, networks, folders, resource pools; puts hosts in and out of maintenance mode.
  • VMware Alarms: lists the triggered alarms and acknowledges them.
  • VMware API: sends any request of the REST API or of VI/JSON.

The VMware alarm trigger starts a workflow when a vCenter alarm turns red (or yellow), and optionally when it clears.

Versions

The REST API steps (VMs, Inventory lists, API) need vCenter Server 7.0 Update 2 or later. Snapshots, alarms, maintenance mode and the alarm trigger use VI/JSON, which needs vCenter Server 8.0 Update 1 or later. An ESXi host on its own has neither API: connect to its vCenter.

The credential

In vCenter, create a user (such as automation@vsphere.local) and give it a role with the privileges the workflows need, on the objects they work on: for example Virtual machine > Interaction for power, Virtual machine > Snapshot management for snapshots, Host > Configuration > Maintenance for maintenance mode, Alarms > Acknowledge alarm. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a VMware vCenter credential, in the Virtualization group:

SettingDescription
vCenter ServerIts address, as for the vSphere Client, such as https://vcenter.example.local.
Username, PasswordThe vCenter user. The password is stored encrypted.
Trust the server's certificateOnly for vCenter's own self-signed certificate (VMCA).

Test signs in to both APIs and shows vCenter's product and version, the number of datacenters, and whether snapshots, alarms and maintenance mode are available.

Rail22 keeps one vCenter session per API while it works and signs out when it is done.

Servers in your network

A vCenter Server is usually on your internal network. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • Objects by name or id: a VM, host, cluster, folder or datacenter can be given by its name (exactly, as in the vSphere Client) or by its vCenter id, such as vm-42, host-10 or domain-c8. A name that several objects share is refused: give the id.
  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Tasks: snapshots and maintenance mode run as vCenter tasks. The step waits until the task ends, within its Timeout, unless Wait for the task is off. A task that fails is an error with vCenter's message.
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the query of a list (such as {"datacenters": "datacenter-3"}) or to the body of an action. See the vSphere API reference.
  • Errors: vCenter's message and its type, such as The operation is not allowed in the current state. (NOT_ALLOWED_IN_CURRENT_STATE). With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

pages.title: VMware VMs
pages.summary: Lists VMs, powers them on and off, shuts down and restarts guests, clones and deletes VMs.
pages.html:
The VMware VMs step works with the virtual machines of a vCenter Server.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every VMware step: see VMware vCenter.

Operations

OperationvCenter requestResult
List VMsGET /api/vcenter/vm{ items, count, total, truncated }: each { vm, name, power_state, cpu_count, memory_size_MiB }, sorted by name. Names (one per line; * for any text), a power state, a host, cluster, folder or datacenter narrow it.
Get a VMGET /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}The VM, as vCenter gives it (hardware, disks, network adapters…), with its id as vm.
Get its power stateGET /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/power{ vm, state }: POWERED_ON, POWERED_OFF or SUSPENDED.
Power on, Power off, Suspend, ResetPOST /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/power{ vm, action, state, already }. A VM that is so already is fine: already is true.
Shut down the guest OSPOST /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/guest/powerA clean shutdown through VMware Tools, waited for until the VM is off (within the Timeout). With Then power off, a VM still on near the timeout is powered off (forced: true). Off already is fine.
Restart the guest OSPOST /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/guest/powerA restart through VMware Tools.
Get guest informationGET /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/guest/...{ identity, interfaces }: the guest OS, host name and IP address, and its network interfaces. VMware Tools must be running.
Clone a VMPOST /api/vcenter/vm?action=clone{ vm, name }: the new VM, in a folder (or the source's), powered on or not. Other placement (host, datastore, resource pool) goes in Other parameters, such as {"placement": {"datastore": "datastore-20"}}.
Delete a VMDELETE /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}The VM and its disks deleted. It must be powered off.

Settings

SettingDescription
VMware credentialA VMware vCenter credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List VMs; Get a VM; Get its power state; Power on; Shut down the guest OS; Restart the guest OS; Power off; Suspend; Reset; Get guest information; Clone a VM; Delete a VM. Default: List VMs. Required.
NamesOne per line or comma separated; * any text (web*); empty: every VM. (For: List VMs.)
Power stateChoices: Any; Powered on; Powered off; Suspended. Default: Any. (For: List VMs.)
HostName or id; empty: any. (For: List VMs.)
ClusterName or id; empty: any. (For: List VMs.)
FolderName or id; empty: any. (For: List VMs.)
DatacenterName or id; empty: any. (For: List VMs.)
VMIts name (exactly) or its id (vm-42); clone: the source. (Required for: Get a VM; Get its power state; Power on; Power off; Suspend; Reset; Shut down the guest OS; Restart the guest OS; Get guest information; Delete a VM; Clone a VM.)
New name(Required for: Clone a VM.)
FolderName or id; empty: the source's. (For: Clone a VM.)
Power onDefault: off. (For: Clone a VM.)
Wait until powered offWithin the step's Timeout. Default: on. (For: Shut down the guest OS.)
Then power offWhen still on near the timeout. Default: off. (For: Shut down the guest OS.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of a list (e.g. {"datacenters": "datacenter-3"}) or to the body of an action: see the vSphere API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List VMs.)
Timeout (s)Waiting for a task or a power state included. Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: vms. Required.
On errorvCenter's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A patch night: List VMs with the names web* and the state Powered on, then a Loop over {{ vms.items }} with VMware Snapshots (Create a snapshot) and Restart the guest OS for {{ item.vm }}.

pages.title: VMware Snapshots
pages.summary: Lists, creates, reverts to and removes VM snapshots, and removes old ones.
pages.html:
The VMware Snapshots step works with the snapshots of one VM. It uses VI/JSON: vCenter Server 8.0 Update 1 or later.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every VMware step: see VMware vCenter.

Operations

OperationvCenter requestResult
List snapshotsGET VirtualMachine/{vm}/snapshot{ items, count, total, truncated }: the snapshot tree as a list, parents before their children, each { id, name, description, createTime, state, quiesced, current, parent, depth }.
Create a snapshotPOST VirtualMachine/{vm}/CreateSnapshot_Task{ vm, task, snapshot, name }: snapshot is the new snapshot's id (when waited for). With the memory, reverting resumes the running VM. Quiescing needs VMware Tools.
Revert to a snapshotPOST VirtualMachineSnapshot/{id}/RevertToSnapshot_TaskThe VM back to the snapshot (by name or id), or to the current snapshot when none is given.
Remove a snapshotPOST VirtualMachineSnapshot/{id}/RemoveSnapshot_TaskThe snapshot removed and its disks consolidated; its children too when chosen.
Remove all snapshotsPOST VirtualMachine/{vm}/RemoveAllSnapshots_TaskEvery snapshot of the VM removed, consolidated.
Remove old snapshotsPOST VirtualMachineSnapshot/{id}/RemoveSnapshot_Task{ removed, count }: the snapshots older than the days (and named like the pattern, such as Before*), removed oldest first, one after the other.

Settings

SettingDescription
VMware credentialA VMware vCenter credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List snapshots; Create a snapshot; Revert to a snapshot; Remove a snapshot; Remove all snapshots; Remove old snapshots. Default: List snapshots. Required.
VMIts name (exactly) or its id (vm-42). (Required for: List snapshots; Create a snapshot; Revert to a snapshot; Remove a snapshot; Remove all snapshots; Remove old snapshots.)
NameDefault: Before the workflow. (Required for: Create a snapshot.)
Description(For: Create a snapshot.)
Include the memoryOf a running VM: reverting resumes it. Default: off. (For: Create a snapshot.)
Quiesce the guest file systemsNeeds VMware Tools. Default: off. (For: Create a snapshot.)
SnapshotIts name (exactly) or id; revert, empty: the current one. (For: Revert to a snapshot; Remove a snapshot.)
Its children tooDefault: off. (For: Remove a snapshot.)
Older than (days)Default: 7. (Required for: Remove old snapshots.)
Named* any text (e.g. Before*); empty: any name. (For: Remove old snapshots.)
Wait for the taskWithin the step's Timeout. Default: on. (For: Create a snapshot; Revert to a snapshot; Remove a snapshot; Remove all snapshots.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of a list (e.g. {"datacenters": "datacenter-3"}) or to the body of an action: see the vSphere API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List snapshots.)
Timeout (s)Waiting for a task or a power state included. Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: snapshots. Required.
On errorvCenter's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

Snapshot housekeeping: a Schedule Trigger every night, VMware VMs List VMs, then a Loop with Remove old snapshots older than 7 days named Before*, so the snapshots workflows take before a change do not pile up.

pages.title: VMware Inventory
pages.summary: Hosts, clusters, datastores and more; hosts in and out of maintenance mode.
pages.html:
The VMware Inventory step reads the infrastructure of a vCenter Server and puts hosts in and out of maintenance mode.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every VMware step: see VMware vCenter.

Operations

OperationvCenter requestResult
List hostsGET /api/vcenter/host{ items, count, total, truncated }: each { host, name, connection_state, power_state }, of a datacenter or a cluster.
List clustersGET /api/vcenter/cluster{ items, count, total, truncated }: each { cluster, name, ha_enabled, drs_enabled }.
List datacentersGET /api/vcenter/datacenter{ items, count, total, truncated }: each { datacenter, name }.
List datastoresGET /api/vcenter/datastore{ items, count, total, truncated }: each { datastore, name, type, capacity, free_space, freePercent, lowOnSpace }: lowOnSpace is true under the percent chosen.
List networks, folders, resource poolsGET /api/vcenter/network|folder|resource-pool{ items, count, total, truncated }, of a datacenter; folders of a type.
Enter maintenance mode (host)POST HostSystem/{host}/EnterMaintenanceMode_Task{ host, inMaintenance, already, task }. With DRS, the host's running VMs move to other hosts first. In it already is fine. Needs vCenter 8.0 Update 1 or later.

Get vCenter's versionGET /api/appliance/system/version{ product, version, build, … }. The user needs to be allowed to read the appliance's settings.

DatacenterName or id; empty: every one. (For: List hosts; List clusters; List datastores; List networks; List folders; List resource pools.)
ClusterName or id; empty: every one. (For: List hosts; List resource pools.)
Low on space under (%)Default: 10. (For: List datastores.)
TypeChoices: Any; VMs and templates; Hosts and clusters; Datastores; Networks; Datacenters. Default: Any. (For: List folders.)
HostIts name (exactly) or its id (host-10). (Required for: Enter maintenance mode (host); Exit maintenance mode (host).)
Wait for the taskWithin the step's Timeout. Default: on. (For: Enter maintenance mode (host); Exit maintenance mode (host).)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the query of a list (e.g. {"datacenters": "datacenter-3"}) or to the body of an action: see the vSphere API reference. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List hosts; List clusters; List datacenters; List datastores; List networks; List folders; List resource pools.)
Timeout (s)Waiting for a task or a power state included. Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: inventory. Required.

A daily capacity check: List datastores, a Loop over {{ inventory.items }} and an If on {{ item.lowOnSpace }}, then Send email with {{ item.name }} and {{ item.freePercent }}% free.

pages.title: VMware Alarms
pages.summary: Lists the alarms triggered in vCenter and acknowledges them.
pages.html:
The VMware Alarms step reads the alarms triggered now in a vCenter Server, on any object, and acknowledges them. It uses VI/JSON: vCenter Server 8.0 Update 1 or later.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every VMware step: see VMware vCenter.

Operations

OperationvCenter requestResult
List triggered alarmsGET Folder/{root}/triggeredAlarmState{ items, count, total, truncated }: red first, then newest first, each { key, alarm: { id, name }, entity: { type, id, name }, status, time, acknowledged, acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedTime }. Acknowledged alarms are left out unless chosen.
Acknowledge an alarmPOST AlarmManager/AlarmManager/AcknowledgeAlarm{ alarm, entity, acknowledged }. The alarm is one of the list, or of the VMware alarm trigger (such as {{ alarm }}), or its key alarm-7|vm-42.

SettingDescription
VMware credentialA VMware vCenter credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List triggered alarms; Acknowledge an alarm. Default: List triggered alarms. Required.

OfChoices: Any object; VMs; Hosts; Datastores; Clusters; Datacenters; Networks. Default: Any object. (For: List triggered alarms.)
Also acknowledged onesDefault: off. (For: List triggered alarms.)
Alarme.g. {{ alarm }} from the VMware alarm trigger, or its key (alarm-7|vm-42). (Required for: Acknowledge an alarm.)
