entity.type is the kind of object, such as VirtualMachine, HostSystem, Datastore or ClusterComputeResource.

pages.title: VMware API
pages.summary: Sends any request of the vCenter REST API or of VI/JSON.
pages.html:
The VMware API step sends any request to vCenter, for what the other VMware steps do not do: VM hardware, content library deployments, tags, vMotion and more. It is an advanced step.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results and the errors are the same for every VMware step: see VMware vCenter.

Operations

  • REST API request: the method, a path under /api/ (such as /api/vcenter/vm/vm-42/hardware), the query and the body as JSON objects.
  • VI/JSON request (vCenter 8.0 Update 1 or later): a path <type>/<id>/<property or method>, such as VirtualMachine/vm-42/runtime. GET reads a property; POST calls a method with its parameters as the body. Objects are given as {"_typeName": "ManagedObjectReference", "type": "HostSystem", "value": "host-10"}. With Wait for the task it returns, a …_Task method's task is followed until it ends and its result is the task's information.

The result is vCenter's answer as it is.

Settings

SettingDescription
VMware credentialA VMware vCenter credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: REST API request; VI/JSON request. Default: REST API request. Required.
MethodVI/JSON: GET a property, POST a method. Choices: GET; POST; PUT; PATCH; DELETE. Default: GET. (Required for: REST API request; VI/JSON request.)
Pathe.g. /api/vcenter/vm/vm-42/hardware ({{ }} allowed). (Required for: REST API request.)
Path<type>/<id>/<property or method>, e.g. VirtualMachine/vm-42/runtime. (Required for: VI/JSON request.)
QueryA JSON object (empty: none), e.g. {"power_states": "POWERED_ON"}. (For: REST API request.)
BodyA JSON object (empty: none).
Wait for the task it returnsA *_Task method: its info when it ends. Default: off. (For: VI/JSON request.)
Timeout (s)Waiting for a task or a power state included. Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: vmware. Required.
On errorvCenter's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Proxmox VE
pages.summary: VMs and containers, power, snapshots, backups, nodes, storage and tasks of a Proxmox VE cluster.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Proxmox VE clusters and servers (7 and 8) through the Proxmox VE API. Its steps are in the Virtualization group of the step list:

  • Proxmox Guests: lists VMs and containers, starts, shuts down, reboots and stops them, reads their status, configuration and IP addresses, clones, migrates and deletes them.
  • Proxmox Snapshots: lists, creates, rolls back to and deletes snapshots, and deletes old ones.
  • Proxmox Backups: backs up a guest now (vzdump, to a Proxmox Backup Server too), lists backups, checks a guest's latest backup, lists backup jobs, deletes a backup.
  • Proxmox Cluster: nodes, storage with free space, the cluster's status, recent tasks, HA, pools and version.
  • Proxmox API: sends any request of the Proxmox VE API.

The Proxmox task trigger starts a workflow when a task ends, such as a failed backup.

The credential

In Proxmox, create an API token under Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens, for a user with a role that has the privileges the workflows need (for example PVEVMAdmin on the guests, PVEDatastoreUser on the backup storage, PVEAuditor to read). With Privilege Separation on, give the token its own permissions too. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Proxmox VE credential, in the Virtualization group:

SettingDescription
ServerA node's address, as for the web interface, such as https://pve1.example.local:8006. Any node of a cluster answers for the whole cluster.
Token IDThe token's full ID, user@realm!token, such as automation@pve!rail22.
SecretThe token's secret, shown once when it is made. It is stored encrypted.
Trust the server's certificateOnly for Proxmox's own self-signed certificate.

Test shows the Proxmox VE version, the cluster's name and its nodes, with those offline marked.

Servers in your network

Proxmox is usually on your internal network. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • Guests by VMID or name: a VM or container is given by its VMID (such as 100) or its name (exactly). The step finds its node and type itself. A name that several guests share is refused: give the VMID.
  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Tasks: actions run as Proxmox tasks. The step waits until the task ends, within its Timeout (5 minutes by default), unless Wait for the task is off. A task that fails is an error with its exit status and the last lines of its log. The task's ID (UPID) is in the result as task.
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the request's parameters (such as {"bwlimit": 50000}). See the API viewer of your Proxmox (https://<node>:8006/pve-docs/api-viewer/).
  • Errors: Proxmox's message, such as HTTP status 500: VM 100 is running - destroy failed, with the parameters it refused. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

pages.title: Proxmox Guests
pages.summary: Lists VMs and containers, starts, shuts down and stops them, clones, migrates and deletes them.
pages.html:
The Proxmox Guests step works with the VMs (QEMU) and containers (LXC) of a Proxmox VE cluster.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results, tasks and the errors are the same for every Proxmox step: see Proxmox VE.

Operations

OperationProxmox requestResult
List VMs and containersGET /cluster/resources?type=vm{ items, count, total, truncated }: each { vmid, name, node, type, status, cpu, maxcpu, mem, maxmem, disk, maxdisk, uptime, tags, template }, by VMID. Names (one per line; * for any text), a status, a type, a node and a tag narrow it. Templates are left out unless chosen.
Get its statusGET …/status/currentIts status, as Proxmox gives it (status, qmpstatus, uptime, cpu, mem…), with vmid, node and type.
Get its configurationGET …/configIts configuration: memory, cores, disks, network…
Start, Shut down, Reboot, Stop, Suspend, Resume, ResetPOST …/status/{action}{ vmid, node, type, action, status, already, task }. Starting a running guest, or stopping or shutting down a stopped one, is fine: already is true. Shut down asks the guest OS (ACPI or the guest agent) and waits for its timeout; with Then stop it, a guest still running is stopped. Reset is for VMs only.
Get its network interfaces…/agent/network-get-interfacesIts interfaces and IP addresses: a VM's through the QEMU guest agent (it must be installed and enabled), a container's from Proxmox.
ClonePOST …/clone{ vmid, node, name, task }: the new guest, with the VMID given or the next free one, full or linked (from a template), on another node or storage.
Migrate to another nodePOST …/migrateThe guest moved. A running VM moves online (live) when chosen; a running container is restarted on the target.
DeleteDELETE …The guest and its disks deleted, and removed from backup and replication jobs. It must be stopped.

Settings

SettingDescription
Proxmox credentialA Proxmox VE credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List VMs and containers; Get its status; Get its configuration; Start; Shut down; Reboot; Stop (power off); Suspend; Resume; Reset (VMs); Get its network interfaces; Clone; Migrate to another node; Delete. Default: List VMs and containers. Required.
NamesOne per line or comma separated; * any text (web*); empty: all. (For: List VMs and containers.)
StatusChoices: Any; Running; Stopped; Paused. Default: Any. (For: List VMs and containers.)
TypeChoices: VMs and containers; VMs; Containers. Default: VMs and containers. (For: List VMs and containers.)
NodeEmpty: every node. (For: List VMs and containers.)
TagEmpty: any. (For: List VMs and containers.)
Templates tooDefault: off. (For: List VMs and containers.)
VM or containerIts VMID or its name (exactly); clone: the source. (Required for: Get its status; Get its configuration; Start; Shut down; Reboot; Stop (power off); Suspend; Resume; Reset (VMs); Get its network interfaces; Clone; Migrate to another node; Delete.)
Shutdown timeout (s)Then it fails, or is stopped. Default: 120. (For: Shut down.)
Then stop itWhen still running after the shutdown timeout. Default: off. (For: Shut down.)
New nameEmpty: Proxmox's own. (For: Clone.)
New VMIDEmpty: the next free one. (For: Clone.)
Full cloneOff: linked (from a template). Default: on. (For: Clone.)
Target nodeMigrate: required; clone, empty: the source's. (For: Clone; Migrate to another node.)
StorageOf a full clone; empty: the source's. (For: Clone.)
Online (live)A running container is restarted instead. Default: on. (For: Migrate to another node.)
Wait for the taskWithin the step's Timeout. Default: on. (For: Start; Shut down; Reboot; Stop (power off); Suspend; Resume; Reset (VMs); Clone; Migrate to another node; Delete.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the request's parameters (e.g. {"bwlimit": 50000}): see the Proxmox VE API viewer. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List VMs and containers.)
Timeout (s)Waiting for its task included. Default: 300. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: guests. Required.
On errorProxmox's errors, a failed task, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A test environment on demand: Clone the template tpl-debian, Start {{ guests.vmid }}, then Get its network interfaces and Send email with its IP address.

pages.title: Proxmox Snapshots
pages.summary: Lists, creates, rolls back to and deletes snapshots of VMs and containers, and deletes old ones.
pages.html:
The Proxmox Snapshots step works with the snapshots of one VM or container.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results, tasks and the errors are the same for every Proxmox step: see Proxmox VE.

Operations

OperationProxmox requestResult
List snapshotsGET …/snapshot{ items, count, total, truncated }: oldest first, each { name, description, snaptime, time, vmstate, parent, current }; current marks the snapshot the guest runs from.
Create a snapshotPOST …/snapshotA snapshot named with letters, digits, _ and -, starting with a letter (2 to 40). With the RAM, rolling back resumes the running VM.
Roll back to a snapshotPOST …/snapshot/{name}/rollbackThe guest back to the snapshot.
Delete a snapshotDELETE …/snapshot/{name}The snapshot deleted.
Delete old snapshotsDELETE …/snapshot/{name}{ removed, count }: the snapshots older than the days (and named like the pattern, such as before*), deleted oldest first, one after the other.

Settings

SettingDescription
Proxmox credentialA Proxmox VE credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List snapshots; Create a snapshot; Roll back to a snapshot; Delete a snapshot; Delete old snapshots. Default: List snapshots. Required.
VM or containerIts VMID or its name (exactly). (Required for: List snapshots; Create a snapshot; Roll back to a snapshot; Delete a snapshot; Delete old snapshots.)
NameLetters, digits, _ -; starts with a letter. Default: before_workflow. (Required for: Create a snapshot.)
Description(For: Create a snapshot.)
Include the RAM (VMs)A running VM: rolling back resumes it. Default: off. (For: Create a snapshot.)
SnapshotIts name. (Required for: Roll back to a snapshot; Delete a snapshot.)
Older than (days)Default: 7. (Required for: Delete old snapshots.)
Named* any text (e.g. before*); empty: any name. (For: Delete old snapshots.)
Wait for the taskWithin the step's Timeout. Default: on. (For: Create a snapshot; Roll back to a snapshot; Delete a snapshot.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the request's parameters (e.g. {"bwlimit": 50000}): see the Proxmox VE API viewer. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List snapshots.)
Timeout (s)Waiting for its task included. Default: 300. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: snapshots. Required.
On errorProxmox's errors, a failed task, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

Safe updates: Create a snapshot named before_update, then the update (such as a HTTP Request to your configuration tool); on its error output, Roll back to a snapshot. A nightly workflow deletes the before* snapshots older than 7 days.

pages.title: Proxmox Backups
pages.summary: Backs up a guest now, lists backups, checks a guest's latest backup, lists backup jobs.
pages.html:
The Proxmox Backups step backs up guests with vzdump and reads the backups on a storage, a Proxmox Backup Server storage included.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results, tasks and the errors are the same for every Proxmox step: see Proxmox VE.

Operations

OperationProxmox requestResult
Back up a guest nowPOST /nodes/{node}/vzdump{ vmid, node, storage, task, backup }: the backup to the storage (or the node's default), in snapshot, suspend or stop mode, with notes. backup is the backup made (volid, size, time…) when the task was waited for and a storage given.
List backups on a storageGET /nodes/{node}/storage/{storage}/content{ items, count, total, truncated }: newest first, each { volid, vmid, ctime, time, size, format, notes, protected, verification }, of a guest or all. The node is the guest's, or the one given.
Get a guest's latest backupGET /nodes/{node}/storage/{storage}/content{ vmid, backup, ageHours }: its newest backup on the storage and how many hours old it is; backup is null when there is none.
List backup jobsGET /cluster/backup{ items, count, total, truncated }: the cluster's scheduled backup jobs.
Delete a backupDELETE /nodes/{node}/storage/{storage}/content/{volid}A backup deleted, by its volume ID (such as pbs:backup/vm/100/2026-10-31T01:00:00Z).

Settings

SettingDescription
Proxmox credentialA Proxmox VE credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Back up a guest now; List backups on a storage; Get a guest's latest backup; List backup jobs; Delete a backup. Default: Back up a guest now. Required.
VM or containerIts VMID or its name (exactly); list, empty: every guest's. (For: Back up a guest now; List backups on a storage; Get a guest's latest backup.)
StorageIts ID, e.g. pbs; back up, empty: the node's default. (For: Back up a guest now; List backups on a storage; Get a guest's latest backup; Delete a backup.)
NodeThe storage's; empty: the guest's. (For: List backups on a storage; Delete a backup.)
ModeChoices: Snapshot (no downtime); Suspend; Stop. Default: Snapshot (no downtime). (For: Back up a guest now.)
CompressionNot for Proxmox Backup Server. Choices: ZSTD; LZO; GZIP; None. Default: ZSTD. (For: Back up a guest now.)
NotesShown with the backup, e.g. Before the upgrade. (For: Back up a guest now.)
BackupIts volume ID, e.g. {{ backup.backup.volid }}. (Required for: Delete a backup.)
Wait for the taskWithin the step's Timeout. Default: on. (For: Back up a guest now; Delete a backup.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the request's parameters (e.g. {"bwlimit": 50000}): see the Proxmox VE API viewer. (Under Advanced….)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List backups on a storage; List backup jobs.)
Timeout (s)Waiting for its task included. Default: 300. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: backup. Required.
On errorProxmox's errors, a failed task, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A backup check every morning: a Loop over the important guests with Get a guest's latest backup, and an If on {{ backup.ageHours }} greater than 26 (or {{ backup.backup }} empty) that sends an email.

pages.title: Proxmox Cluster

pages.title: Proxmox API
pages.summary: Sends any request of the Proxmox VE API.
pages.html:
The Proxmox API step sends any request of the Proxmox VE API, for what the other Proxmox steps do not do: changing a guest's configuration, firewall rules, replication, Ceph and more. It is an advanced step.

The credential, Other parameters, the list results, tasks and the errors are the same for every Proxmox step: see Proxmox VE.

Give the method, a path under /api2/json (such as /nodes/pve1/qemu/100/config) and the parameters as a JSON object (such as {"memory": 4096}). With Wait for the task it starts, an answer that is a task (a UPID) is followed until the task ends, and the result is its status. Otherwise the result is Proxmox's data as it is.

Settings

SettingDescription
Proxmox credentialA Proxmox VE credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Send a request. Default: Send a request. Required.
MethodChoices: GET; POST; PUT; DELETE. Default: GET. (Required for: Send a request.)
PathUnder /api2/json, e.g. /nodes/pve1/qemu/100/config ({{ }} allowed). (Required for: Send a request.)
ParametersA JSON object (empty: none), e.g. {"memory": 4096}.
Wait for the task it startsAn answer that is a task (UPID): its status when it stops. Default: off.
Timeout (s)Waiting for its task included. Default: 300. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: proxmox. Required.
On errorProxmox's errors, a failed task, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: Hyper-V
pages.summary: VMs, power, checkpoints, the host, replication and events of a Hyper-V host, through PowerShell over WinRM.
pages.html:
Rail22 manages Hyper-V hosts (Windows Server 2016 and later) the way an administrator does: it runs PowerShell with the Hyper-V module on the host, through Windows Remote Management (WinRM) over HTTPS. Its steps are in the Virtualization group of the step list:

  • Hyper-V VMs: lists VMs, starts them, shuts down and restarts their guest OS, turns them off, saves, pauses, resumes and resets them, reads their network adapters, deletes them.
  • Hyper-V Checkpoints: lists, creates, restores and removes checkpoints, and removes old ones.
  • Hyper-V Host: the host's memory and VMs, its volumes with free space, virtual switches, VM replication, and the Hyper-V errors and warnings of its event logs.
  • Hyper-V PowerShell: runs any PowerShell script on the host.

The Hyper-V VM state trigger starts a workflow when a VM stops running, or when its replication health turns Warning or Critical.

Each step works on one host. In a failover cluster, use the host that owns the VM.

Preparing the host

On the Hyper-V host, in an administrator's PowerShell, turn on a WinRM HTTPS listener (here with a self-signed certificate; a certificate of your own CA works the same) and allow it through the firewall:

$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -DnsName hv01.example.local -CertStoreLocation Cert:\LocalMachine\My
New-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Listener -Transport HTTPS -Address * -CertificateThumbPrint $cert.Thumbprint -Force
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "WinRM HTTPS" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5986 -Action Allow

Use a dedicated account, member of the host's Hyper-V Administrators and Remote Management Users groups (an administrator works too):

Add-LocalGroupMember -Group "Hyper-V Administrators" -Member "EXAMPLE\svc-rail22"
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group "Remote Management Users" -Member "EXAMPLE\svc-rail22"

NTLM works with domain and local accounts. Basic works only with local accounts, and only after Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Service\Auth\Basic $true. Both are sent over HTTPS only.

The credential

Under Credentials & variables, create a Hyper-V credential, in the Virtualization group:

SettingDescription
HostIts WinRM HTTPS address, such as https://hv01.example.local:5986.
Username, PasswordDOMAIN\user, user@domain or a local user. The password is stored encrypted.
AuthenticationNTLM (domain or local accounts) or Basic (local accounts).
Trust the host's certificateFor the listener's self-signed certificate.

Test runs PowerShell on the host and shows its name, its Windows version and how many VMs it has. It says so when the Hyper-V PowerShell module is missing.

Servers in your network

A Hyper-V host is on your internal network. Rail22 connects only to public internet addresses unless the account allows more: turn on Integrations may connect to private network addresses in Account settings. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses stay out of reach.

What the steps share

  • VMs by name or ID: a VM is given by its name (exactly) or its ID (a GUID). A name that several VMs share is refused: give the ID.
  • Values stay data: the steps' settings reach PowerShell as data ($P), never as part of the script, so a value such as a VM name cannot run commands on the host.
  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Timeout (2 minutes by default) covers the whole script, waits included, such as a guest shutdown.
  • Errors: PowerShell's or WinRM's message, such as VM 'web01' is Running: turn it off first. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

pages.title: Hyper-V VMs
pages.summary: Lists VMs, starts them, shuts down their guest OS, turns them off, saves, pauses and deletes them.
pages.html:
The Hyper-V VMs step works with the virtual machines of a Hyper-V host.

The credential, the list results and the errors are the same for every Hyper-V step: see Hyper-V.

Operations

OperationPowerShellResult
List VMsGet-VM{ items, count, total, truncated }: by name, each { name, id, state, status, cpuUsage, processorCount, memoryAssigned, uptimeSeconds, heartbeat, replicationHealth, checkpoint, ... }. Names (one per line; * for any text) and a state narrow it.
Get a VMGet-VMThe VM, with the same fields.
Start, Turn off, Save, Pause, ResumeStart-VM, Stop-VM -TurnOff, Save-VM, Suspend-VM, Resume-VM{ name, id, action, state, already, forced }. A VM that is so already is fine: already is true. Turn off is like pulling the plug.
Shut down the guest OSStop-VMA clean shutdown through the integration services, waited for up to the seconds given. With Then turn it off, a VM still running is turned off (forced: true); otherwise that is an error. Off already is fine.
Restart the guest OS, ResetRestart-VMA restart through the integration services, or a hard reset.
Get its network adaptersGet-VMNetworkAdapterIts adapters: { name, macAddress, switchName, ipAddresses, status }. The guest's IP addresses come through the integration services.
DeleteRemove-VMThe VM removed. It must be off. Its virtual disks are kept, unless Delete its virtual disks too is on (not for a VM with checkpoints).

Settings

SettingDescription
Hyper-V credentialA Hyper-V host of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List VMs; Get a VM; Start; Shut down the guest OS; Restart the guest OS; Turn off; Save; Pause; Resume; Reset; Get its network adapters; Delete. Default: List VMs. Required.
NamesOne per line or comma separated; * any text (web*); empty: every VM. (For: List VMs.)
StateChoices: Any; Running; Off; Saved; Paused. Default: Any. (For: List VMs.)
VMIts name (exactly) or its ID. (Required for: Get a VM; Start; Shut down the guest OS; Restart the guest OS; Turn off; Save; Pause; Resume; Reset; Get its network adapters; Delete.)
Wait for the shutdown (s)Within the step's Timeout. Default: 90. (For: Shut down the guest OS.)
Then turn it offWhen still running after the wait. Default: off. (For: Shut down the guest OS.)
Delete its virtual disks tooNot for a VM with checkpoints. Default: off. (For: Delete.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List VMs.)
Timeout (s)The PowerShell script's, waiting included. Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: vms. Required.
On errorPowerShell's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A maintenance window: List VMs with the names app* and the state Running, then a Loop with Hyper-V Checkpoints (Create a checkpoint) and Restart the guest OS for {{ item.id }}.

pages.title: Hyper-V Checkpoints
pages.summary: Lists, creates, restores and removes checkpoints of a VM, and removes old ones.
pages.html:
The Hyper-V Checkpoints step works with the checkpoints of one VM. A checkpoint is Production or Standard as the VM is set in Hyper-V.

The credential, the list results and the errors are the same for every Hyper-V step: see Hyper-V.

Its children tooDefault: off. (For: Remove a checkpoint.)
Older than (days)Default: 7. (Required for: Remove old checkpoints.)
Named* any text (e.g. Before*); empty: any name. (For: Remove old checkpoints.)

pages.title: Hyper-V Host
pages.summary: The host's memory and VMs, volumes with free space, virtual switches, replication and Hyper-V events.
pages.html:
The Hyper-V Host step reads the state of the Hyper-V host itself.

The credential, the list results and the errors are the same for every Hyper-V step: see Hyper-V.

At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List volumes; List virtual switches; List VM replication; List Hyper-V errors and warnings.)
Timeout (s)The PowerShell script's, waiting included. Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: host. Required.
On errorPowerShell's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A morning report: a Schedule Trigger, List volumes, List VM replication and List Hyper-V errors and warnings of the last 24 hours, then Send email with what needs attention.

pages.title: Hyper-V PowerShell
pages.summary: Runs any PowerShell script on the Hyper-V host.
pages.html:
The Hyper-V PowerShell step runs a PowerShell script on the host (Windows PowerShell 5.1, with the Hyper-V module), for what the other Hyper-V steps do not do: new VMs, exports, VM settings, failover clusters and more. It is an advanced step.

The credential, the list results and the errors are the same for every Hyper-V step: see Hyper-V.

The script's value is the result, converted to JSON (to a depth of 8): end it with the value you want, such as Get-VM | Select-Object Name, MemoryAssigned. Enums are best turned into text ("$($_.State)"), dates into text too ($_.CreationTime.ToString('o')). An error stops the script and is the step's error.

Give values of the workflow in Parameters, a JSON object such as {"name": "{{ vm.name }}"}, and read them in the script as $P.name. Never write {{ }} into the script itself: the parameters stay data, so a value cannot run commands. The helpers r22find (a VM by name or ID) and r22vm (a VM's fields) are there too.

A script can be about 10,000 characters long.

Settings

SettingDescription
Hyper-V credentialA Hyper-V host of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Run a script. Default: Run a script. Required.
ScriptIts value is the result; the parameters are $P (e.g. $P.name). Default: Get-VM | Select-Object Name, @{ n = 'State'; e = { "$($_.State)" } }. (Required for: Run a script.)
ParametersA JSON object (empty: none), e.g. {"name": "{{ vm.name }}"}.
Timeout (s)The PowerShell script's, waiting included. Default: 120. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }. Default: result. Required.
On errorPowerShell's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

Example

A VM's memory raised: Parameters {"vm": "{{ vm }}", "gb": 8} and the script $v = r22find $P.vm; Set-VMMemory -VM $v -StartupBytes ($P.gb * 1GB); r22vm (Get-VM -Id $v.Id) (the VM off).

pages.title: Namecheap
pages.summary: Domains, DNS records, name servers, email forwarding, renewals and the balance of a Namecheap account.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Namecheap through the Namecheap API. Its steps are in the Domains & DNS group of the step list:

  • Namecheap Domains: lists the domains and those expiring soon, checks availability, locks, unlocks and renews domains.
  • Namecheap DNS: lists, adds, sets and removes DNS records, and changes name servers and email forwarding.
  • Namecheap Account: the balance, the prices of a TLD and the SSL certificates.
  • Namecheap API: any command of the Namecheap API, such as registering a domain.

The credential

In Namecheap, open Profile > Tools > Business & Dev Tools > Namecheap API Access, turn API access on and copy the API key. On the same page, add the public IPv4 address of the Rail22 server to the whitelisted IPs. Namecheap answers no other address. Namecheap only gives API access to accounts that meet its conditions, such as a minimum balance or number of domains. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a Namecheap credential, in the Domains & DNS group:

SettingDescription
API userYour Namecheap user name.
API keyThe key from API Access. It is stored encrypted.
Acts for userThe user whose domains the steps manage. Leave it empty for your own; resellers can name one of their customers.
Client IPThe public IPv4 address that Rail22's requests come from, as whitelisted in API Access.
SandboxUses api.sandbox.namecheap.com, with a sandbox account and its own key: for trying workflows without real domains or charges.

Test shows the user and the available balance. A wrong key or an address that is not whitelisted is reported with what to fix.

What the steps share

  • Domains are given by name, such as example.com or example.co.uk. A domain from a list works as well, so {{ item }} in a loop over List domains names that domain.
  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items). The items have the fields Namecheap gives, with its names, such as Name, Expires, IsLocked and AutoRenew. true and false are booleans.
  • Other parameters, under Advanced…, is a JSON object added to the command's parameters, as Namecheap names them, such as {"SortBy": "NAME_DESC"}.
  • Errors: Namecheap's message and its number, such as Domain not found (error 2019166). With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.
  • Limits: Namecheap takes at most 20 commands a minute, 700 an hour and 8,000 a day per user. A loop over many domains can reach them. Over a limit, the step fails with Namecheap's error.

Note: Renew a domain charges your Namecheap balance. For an AI step, it counts as a write operation, like the DNS changes and the lock: write operations are not offered by default, and ask for approval when approvals are on.

pages.title: Namecheap Domains
pages.summary: Lists the domains and those expiring soon, checks availability, locks, unlocks and renews domains.
pages.html:
The Namecheap Domains step works with the domains of the account.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Namecheap step: see Namecheap.

Operations

OperationNamecheap commandResult
List domainsnamecheap.domains.getList{ items, count, total, truncated }: all, expiring or expired, containing a text, sorted.
List domains expiring soonnamecheap.domains.getList{ items, count, total, truncated }: the domains that expire within Within (days), the soonest first, each with daysLeft (0 on the day it expires, negative after).
Get a domainnamecheap.domains.getInfoThe domain: Status, DomainName, DomainDetails (CreatedDate, ExpiredDate), Whoisguard, DnsDetails.
Check availabilitynamecheap.domains.check{ items, available, count }: each name with Available and IsPremiumName; available lists the free names. At most 50 names.
Get a domain's contactsnamecheap.domains.getContactsRegistrant, Tech, Admin and AuxBilling.
Get the registrar locknamecheap.domains.getRegistrarLock{ domain, locked }.
Lock a domain, Unlock a domainnamecheap.domains.setRegistrarLock{ domain, locked }.
Renew a domainnamecheap.domains.renewDomainName, Renew, ChargedAmount, OrderID, TransactionID. Charged to the balance.
List TLDsnamecheap.domains.getTldList{ items, count, total, truncated }: each TLD with Name, MinRegisterYears, MaxRegisterYears, IsApiRegisterable, IsApiRenewable.

Settings

SettingDescription
Namecheap credentialA Namecheap credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List domains; List domains expiring soon; Get a domain; Check availability; Get a domain's contacts; Get the registrar lock; Lock a domain; Unlock a domain; Renew a domain; List TLDs. Default: List domains. Required.
DomainsChoices: All; Expiring; Expired. Default: All. (For: List domains.)
Sorted byChoices: Name; Name, descending; Expiry; Expiry, latest first; Created; Created, latest first. Default: Name. (For: List domains.)
ContainingA text in the name; empty: all. (For: List domains, List domains expiring soon.)
Within (days)Expiring in at most this many days. Default: 30. (Required for: List domains expiring soon.)
Expired ones tooThose already expired (while they can still be renewed). Default: on. (For: List domains expiring soon.)
DomainIts name, e.g. example.com; a domain of a list works too. (Required for: Get a domain, Get a domain's contacts, Get the registrar lock, Lock a domain, Unlock a domain, Renew a domain.)
NamesSeparated by commas, or a list; at most 50. (Required for: Check availability.)
YearsDefault: 1. (Required for: Renew a domain.)
Promotion codeEmpty: none. (For: Renew a domain.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the command's parameters, as Namecheap names them (e.g. {"SortBy": "NAME"}).
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List domains, List domains expiring soon, List TLDs.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: domains. Required.
On errorNamecheap's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, a weekly reminder: a Schedule trigger, then List domains expiring soon within 30 days, then Send email when {{ domains.count }} is more than 0.

Registering a domain needs four contacts: use the Namecheap API step with namecheap.domains.create.

pages.title: Namecheap DNS
pages.summary: Lists, adds, sets and removes DNS records, and changes name servers and email forwarding.
pages.html:
The Namecheap DNS step works with the DNS of a domain that uses Namecheap's name servers (BasicDNS, PremiumDNS or FreeDNS).

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Namecheap step: see Namecheap.

Operations

OperationNamecheap commandResult
List recordsnamecheap.domains.dns.getHosts{ domain, records, count, emailType, usingNamecheapDns }: each record with Name, Type, Address, TTL, MXPref, HostId. Of a host and type, when given.
Add a recordgetHosts, setHosts{ domain, records, count, added, removed, changed }. When the same record is there already, nothing is written and changed is false. The same value with another TTL replaces it.
Set a record (replace the host's)getHosts, setHostsThe same: the host's records of that type are replaced by this one. Use it to point a name at a new address.
Remove recordsgetHosts, setHostsThe same: the host's records of that type, or only those with the value given.
Replace all recordsgetHosts, setHostsThe same: the domain has exactly the records of the list.
Get name serversnamecheap.domains.dns.getList{ domain, nameservers, usingNamecheapDns }.
Set custom name serversnamecheap.domains.dns.setCustom{ domain, nameservers }. At least 2.
Use Namecheap's name serversnamecheap.domains.dns.setDefault{ domain, usingNamecheapDns }.
Get email forwardingnamecheap.domains.dns.getEmailForwarding{ domain, forwards, count }: each { mailbox, forwardTo }.
Set email forwardingnamecheap.domains.dns.setEmailForwarding{ domain, count }. The list replaces every forward.

How records are changed

Namecheap has no command to change one record: setHosts replaces all of them. So Add, Set and Remove read the records, change the list and write it back whole. The records they do not name are kept as they were. With MX records, the domain's mail setting is set to custom MX (EmailType MX), as Namecheap requires. When the last MX record is removed, it is set to none. Otherwise it stays as it was, such as email forwarding.

Note: two runs that change the same domain at the same time can lose one of the changes. Avoid running such workflows in parallel for one domain. Replace all records removes every record that is not in its list, including mail records.

Settings

SettingDescription
Namecheap credentialA Namecheap credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: List records; Add a record; Set a record (replace the host's); Remove records; Replace all records; Get name servers; Set custom name servers; Use Namecheap's name servers; Get email forwarding; Set email forwarding. Default: List records. Required.
DomainIts name, e.g. example.com; a domain of a list works too. Required.
Host@ for the domain itself, or a name such as www (List records: empty: all). (For: List records, Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's), Remove records.) (Required for: Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's), Remove records.)
TypeList records: empty: every type. Choices: (any); A; AAAA; ALIAS; CAA; CNAME; MX; MXE; NS; TXT; URL redirect (302); URL redirect (301); URL frame. (For: List records, Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's), Remove records.) (Required for: Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's), Remove records.)
ValueThe address, name, text or URL (Remove records: empty: whatever the value). (For: Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's), Remove records.) (Required for: Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's).)
TTL (s)Default: 1800. (For: Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's).)
MX priorityOf an MX record. Default: 10. (For: Add a record, Set a record (replace the host's).)
RecordsA list of { host, type, value, ttl, mxPref } (List records' records work too: Name, Type, Address, TTL, MXPref). Every other record is removed. (Required for: Replace all records.)
Name serversSeparated by commas, or a list; at least 2. (Required for: Set custom name servers.)
ForwardingA list of { mailbox, forwardTo }: info forwards info@<domain>. Every other forward is removed. (Required for: Set email forwarding.)
Other parametersA JSON object added to the command's parameters, as Namecheap names them (e.g. {"SortBy": "NAME"}).
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: dns. Required.
On errorNamecheap's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, a dynamic address: Set a record, host home, type A, value {{ ip }}, TTL 300. When the address has not changed, nothing is written.

pages.title: Namecheap Account
pages.summary: The account's balance, the prices of a TLD and the SSL certificates.
pages.html:
The Namecheap Account step reads the account.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Namecheap step: see Namecheap.

Other parametersA JSON object added to the command's parameters, as Namecheap names them (e.g. {"SortBy": "NAME"}).

Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.

For example, before renewals: compare {{ account.AvailableBalance }} with {{ account.FundsRequiredForAutoRenew }} and send an email when the balance is too low.

pages.title: Namecheap API
pages.summary: Runs any command of the Namecheap API.
pages.html:
The Namecheap API step runs any command: what the other Namecheap steps do not have, such as registering a domain, child name servers, transfers or SSL activation. It is an advanced step.

The credential, Other parameters, the results and the errors are the same for every Namecheap step: see Namecheap.

Settings

SettingDescription
Namecheap credentialA Namecheap credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Run a command. Default: Run a command. Required.
Commande.g. namecheap.domains.ns.getInfo. Required.
ParametersA JSON object, as Namecheap names them (empty: none), e.g. {"SLD": "example", "TLD": "com", "Nameserver": "ns1.example.com"}.
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: namecheap. Required.
On errorNamecheap's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

The result is the answer's CommandResponse: attributes and child elements by name, repeated ones as a list. For example, a child name server: command namecheap.domains.ns.getInfo, parameters {"SLD": "example", "TLD": "com", "Nameserver": "ns1.example.com"}, gives { DomainNSInfoResult: { Domain, Nameserver, IP, NameserverStatuses } }.

pages.title: Shopify
pages.summary: Orders, products, stock, customers and webhooks of a Shopify store, any GraphQL query, and an event trigger.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to a Shopify store through Shopify's GraphQL Admin API. Its steps are in the E-commerce group of the step list:

  • Shopify Orders: lists and reads orders, changes their note and tags, marks them paid, fulfills them with tracking, closes, reopens and cancels them.
  • Shopify Products: lists products and variants, creates, updates and deletes products, and sets a variant's price.
  • Shopify Inventory: a variant's stock at each location, and stock adjusted or set.
  • Shopify Customers: lists, finds (by email), creates and updates customers, and their tags.
  • Shopify Store: the store's details and its webhook subscriptions.
  • Shopify GraphQL: any query or mutation of the Admin API, such as refunds, draft orders, discounts or metafields.

The Shopify event trigger starts a workflow when the store sends a webhook: an order created or paid, a product updated, stock changed.

The app in Shopify

Rail22 signs in as an app installed on the store. Choose the access scopes the workflows need, such as read_orders, write_orders, read_products, write_products, read_inventory, write_inventory, read_customers, write_customers, read_locations, and for fulfillments read_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders and write_merchant_managed_fulfillment_orders. Orders older than 60 days also need read_all_orders, which Shopify grants on request.

  • A Dev Dashboard app (the way to make new apps since 2026): create an app in Shopify's Dev Dashboard, choose its scopes, release a version and install it on your store. Copy its Client ID and Client secret from the app's settings. Rail22 asks Shopify for a token with them when needed (a token lasts about 24 hours).
  • A custom app made in the store's admin (Settings > Apps > Develop apps), if you have one from before: its Admin API access token (shpat_…), and its API secret key for the webhooks.

The credential

Under Credentials & variables, create a Shopify credential, in the E-commerce group:

SettingDescription
StoreIts myshopify address, such as my-store.myshopify.com. The store's name, or its admin address (admin.shopify.com/store/my-store), works too. Shopify's API answers only at the myshopify address, not at the store's own domain.
API versionShopify's quarterly version, such as 2026-10. Each is supported for at least 12 months: move to a newer one before yours is retired.
Sign in withClient ID and secret (a Dev Dashboard app) or Admin API access token (a custom app of the store).
Admin API access tokenThe custom app's shpat_… token. Stored encrypted.
Client IDThe Dev Dashboard app's Client ID.
Client secretThe app's client secret, stored encrypted. It also checks the webhooks' signature. With an access token, give the custom app's API secret key here if you use the Shopify event trigger.

Test shows the store, its plan, the API version and the scopes the app has.

What the steps share

  • IDs: an order, product, variant or customer can be given by its number (450789469), its GraphQL ID (gid://shopify/Order/450789469) or as an object from a list or a webhook, so {{ item }} in a loop, or {{ shopify.data }} of the event trigger, names it. Orders also by name (#1001), products by handle, customers by email, variants by SKU.
  • Lists give { items, count, truncated }, at most At most (items). Search is Shopify's search syntax, such as financial_status:paid tag:wholesale created_at:>2026-01-01.
  • Results are what Shopify gives, with its field names (displayFinancialStatus, createdAt), with lists in place of connections and money as { amount, currencyCode }, such as {{ order.totalPrice.amount }}. Amounts are texts, such as "19.90".
  • Other fields, under Advanced…, is a JSON object merged into the input of a change, as Shopify's GraphQL names the fields, such as {"shippingAddress": {"city": "Cluj-Napoca"}} for an order.
  • Errors: Shopify's message, with the field it is about, such as email: Email has already been taken. A missing access scope is reported by Shopify, with its name. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.
  • Limits: Shopify gives each app a budget of query cost, refilled every second. When it runs out, the step waits and sends the query again, within its Timeout. A large list takes several requests.

Note: Cancel an order can refund the customer, and Mark as paid, the stock changes and the product changes are visible in the store at once. For an AI step they are write operations: not offered by default, and they ask for approval when approvals are on.

pages.title: Shopify Orders
pages.summary: Lists and reads orders, changes their note and tags, marks them paid, fulfills, closes, reopens and cancels them.
pages.html:
The Shopify Orders step works with the store's orders.

The credential, Other fields, the results and the errors are the same for every Shopify step: see Shopify.

Operations

OperationShopify GraphQLResult
List ordersorders{ items, count, truncated }: the orders the search finds, sorted. Each with name, email, displayFinancialStatus, displayFulfillmentStatus, totalPrice, customer, shippingAddress, tags; lineItems only with With line items (fewer orders per request).
Get an orderorderThe order with its lineItems (sku, quantity, originalUnitPrice), fulfillments (with tracking) and fulfillmentOrders.
Update an orderorderUpdateThe order. The note, the email and the tags (replacing them all) that are not empty; other fields with Other fields.
Add tags, Remove tagstagsAdd / tagsRemove{ id, tags }.
Mark as paidorderMarkAsPaid{ id, name, displayFinancialStatus }: a manual payment of what is due.
Fulfill an orderfulfillmentCreate{ id, name, fulfillments }: what is left of the open fulfillment orders, one fulfillment per location, with the carrier and tracking number when given. Nothing left: an error.
Close an order, Reopen an orderorderClose / orderOpen{ id, name, closed, closedAt }.

Settings

SettingDescription

OperationChoices: List orders; Get an order; Update an order; Add tags; Remove tags; Mark as paid; Fulfill an order; Close an order; Reopen an order; Cancel an order. Default: List orders. Required.

With line itemsFewer orders per request. Default: off. (For: List orders.)
OrderIts ID, its name (#1001), or an order of a list or a webhook. (Required for: Get an order, Update an order, Add tags, Remove tags, Mark as paid, Fulfill an order, Close an order, Reopen an order, Cancel an order.)
NoteEmpty: unchanged. (For: Update an order.)
EmailEmpty: unchanged. (For: Update an order.)
TagsSeparated by commas, or a list. Update: replaces them all (empty: unchanged). (For: Update an order, Add tags, Remove tags.)
Carriere.g. DHL Express, UPS; empty: no tracking. (For: Fulfill an order.)
Tracking number(For: Fulfill an order.)
Tracking addressEmpty: Shopify's for known carriers. (For: Fulfill an order.)
ReasonChoices: The customer changed their mind; Payment declined; Fraudulent; Out of stock; Staff error; Other. Default: Other. (Required for: Cancel an order.)
Staff note(For: Cancel an order.)
RefundTo the original payment methods. Default: on. (For: Cancel an order.)
RestockDefault: on. (For: Cancel an order.)
Notify the customerDefault: on. (For: Fulfill an order, Cancel an order.)
Other fieldsA JSON object merged into the change's input, as Shopify's GraphQL names the fields (e.g. {"templateSuffix": "special"}). (For: Update an order, Fulfill an order.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 250. Required. (For: List orders.)
Timeout (s)Throttled queries wait for Shopify's limit within it. Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: orders. Required.
On errorShopify's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, a step after the Shopify event trigger on Order paid: Add tags with order {{ shopify.data }} and tags to-pack, then a message to the warehouse.

Refunds, returns and order edits: use the Shopify GraphQL step.

pages.title: Shopify Products
pages.summary: Lists products and variants, creates, updates and deletes products, and sets a variant's price.
pages.html:
The Shopify Products step works with the store's products and their variants.

The credential, Other fields, the results and the errors are the same for every Shopify step: see Shopify.

Operations

Update a productproductUpdateThe product. The settings that are not empty are changed; tags replace them all.

Variant byChoices: Its ID; Its SKU. Default: Its ID. (For: Set a variant's price.)

Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: products. Required.
On errorShopify's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, prices from a supplier's file: Loop over its rows, and Set a variant's price by SKU with {{ item.sku }} and {{ item.price }}.

pages.title: Shopify Inventory
pages.summary: A variant's stock at each location, stock adjusted or set, and the store's locations.
pages.html:
The Shopify Inventory step works with the stock of the variants at the store's locations. The variant is given by its SKU (the default) or its ID; the location by its name or ID. With one location, it can be left empty.

The credential, Other fields, the results and the errors are the same for every Shopify step: see Shopify.

Operations

OperationShopify GraphQLResult
Get stock levelsproductVariant / inventoryLevels{ variant, sku, title, product, inventoryItem, tracked, available, levels }: available is the total; each level has location, locationId, available, on_hand, committed, incoming, reserved.
Adjust stockinventoryAdjustQuantities{ variant, sku, location, locationId, before, after, delta }: the available quantity changed by Change by (such as -2).
Set stockinventorySetQuantitiesThe same: the available quantity set to Quantity.
List locationslocations{ items, count, truncated }: each with name, isActive, fulfillsOnlineOrders and address.

A change is sent with the quantity the step has just read: from API version 2026-04, Shopify refuses it when the stock changed in between (an order placed at that moment), rather than overwriting it. Run the step again to retry. The variant must already be stocked at the location (in Shopify, the location is activated for the product).

Settings

SettingDescription
Shopify credentialA Shopify credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Get stock levels; Adjust stock; Set stock; List locations. Default: Get stock levels. Required.
Variant byChoices: Its SKU; Its ID. Default: Its SKU. (For: Get stock levels, Adjust stock, Set stock.)
VariantIts SKU, or its ID (a variant of a list works too). (Required for: Get stock levels, Adjust stock, Set stock.)
LocationIts name or ID; empty: the store's only active location. (For: Adjust stock, Set stock.)
Change bye.g. 5 or -2. (Required for: Adjust stock.)
QuantityAvailable. (Required for: Set stock.)
ReasonChoices: Correction; Received; Cycle count; Restock; Damaged; Shrinkage; Promotion; Quality control; Safety stock; Movement; Other. Default: Correction. (Required for: Adjust stock, Set stock.)
SearchShopify's search syntax, e.g. active:true; empty: all. (For: List locations.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 250. Required. (For: List locations.)
Timeout (s)Throttled queries wait for Shopify's limit within it. Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: stock. Required.
On errorShopify's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, stock from a warehouse system: a Schedule trigger, a database query, then a Loop with Set stock by {{ item.sku }} to {{ item.qty }}.

pages.title: Shopify GraphQL
pages.summary: Any query or mutation of Shopify's GraphQL Admin API.
pages.html:
The Shopify GraphQL step runs any query or mutation of Shopify's GraphQL Admin API: what the other Shopify steps don't have, such as refunds, returns, draft orders, discounts, collections or metafields. It is an advanced step.

Write the query as in Shopify's documentation, and give the values in Variables, a JSON object where {{ }} works, such as {"id": "{{ shopify.data.admin_graphql_api_id }}"}. The result is the answer's data, simplified unless Simplify is off (lists in place of connections, money as { amount, currencyCode }). A mutation's userErrors are not checked: they are in the result.

query($id: ID!) {
  order(id: $id) {
    name
    refunds { id totalRefundedSet { shopMoney { amount } } }
  }
}

Settings

SettingDescription
Shopify credentialA Shopify credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Run a query or mutation. Default: Run a query or mutation. Required.
QueryGraphQL, e.g. query($id: ID!) { order(id: $id) { name note } }. (Required for: Run a query or mutation.)
VariablesA JSON object (empty: none), e.g. {"id": "gid://shopify/Order/1001"}.
SimplifyConnections as lists, money as { amount, currencyCode }. Default: on.
Timeout (s)Throttled queries wait for Shopify's limit within it. Default: 60. Required.

pages.title: Jira
pages.summary: Issues (search, create, update, status, comments, links, attachments) and projects of Jira Cloud or Data Center, any REST request, and an issue trigger.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to Jira, Jira Cloud or Jira Data Center / Server, through its REST API. Its steps are in the Work management group of the step list:

  • Jira Issues: searches with JQL, reads, creates and updates issues, changes their status, assigns them, adds comments, labels, links and attachments, deletes them.
  • Jira Projects: projects and their issue types, fields (to find a custom field's ID), users, priorities and link types.
  • Jira API: any request of the REST API, such as worklogs, watchers or Jira Software's sprints.

The Jira issue trigger starts a workflow when issues are created or updated.

The credential

Under Credentials & variables, create a Jira credential, in the Work management group. The steps act as that user, with its permissions in Jira: a user made for Rail22 keeps its changes easy to tell apart.

SettingDescription
JiraJira Cloud (atlassian.net) or Jira Data Center / Server.
SiteThe address you open Jira at: https://example.atlassian.net, or your server's, with its context path when it has one.
EmailJira Cloud: the email of the Atlassian account.
API tokenJira Cloud: an API token made at id.atlassian.com > Security > API tokens. Data Center: a personal access token (Profile > Personal Access Tokens). Stored encrypted.
Trust the server's certificateData Center with a self-signed certificate only.

Test shows the site and the user. A Data Center server on a private address (inside your network) needs the account's Integrations may connect to private network addresses.

What the steps share

  • Issues are given by key (OPS-123), by address (…/browse/OPS-123), or as an issue of a search or of the trigger, so {{ item }} in a loop, or {{ issue }}, names it.
  • An issue is { key, id, url, summary, status, statusCategory, issueType, priority, project, assignee, reporter, labels, components, created, updated, duedate, resolution, parent, description, fields }. statusCategory is new, indeterminate or done; description is plain text; fields has every field as Jira gives it, custom ones by ID ({{ issue.fields.customfield_10016 }}).
  • Texts (description, comments) are plain text: paragraphs at blank lines. Jira Cloud stores them as rich text (Atlassian Document Format): Rail22 converts them both ways.
  • Users are given by email, by name or by account ID. A Jira Cloud user who hides their email can only be found by name or account ID.
  • Lists give { items, count, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Errors: Jira's message, with the field it is about, such as summary: You must specify a summary of the issue. When Jira's rate limit is reached, the step waits and sends the request again, within its Timeout. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

Note: for an AI step, creating, changing and deleting issues are write operations: not offered by default, and they ask for approval when approvals are on.

pages.title: Jira Issues
pages.summary: Searches, reads, creates and updates issues; status, assignee, comments, labels, links, attachments.
pages.html:
The Jira Issues step works with the site's issues.

The credential, the results and the errors are the same for every Jira step: see Jira.

Operations

OperationJira REST APIResult
Search issues (JQL)search/jql (Cloud), search{ items, count, truncated }: the issues the JQL finds, in its order. Fields adds fields to read, such as a custom field.
Get an issueissue/<key>The issue, with all its fields.
Create an issuePOST issueThe new issue. Project and type are required, and a summary. Custom fields go in Other fields, such as {"customfield_10016": 5}.
Update an issuePUT issue/<key>The issue. The settings that are not empty are changed; labels replace them all.
Change the statusissue/<key>/transitions{ key, status, from, transition, changed }. To is the transition's name or the status it leads to (In Progress, Done), in any case. An issue already there: nothing is done. A resolution and a comment can go with it.
List the transitionsissue/<key>/transitions{ items, count, truncated }: { id, name, to }: the statuses the issue can go to now.
Assign an issueissue/<key>/assignee{ key, assignee }. - unassigns it.
Add a commentPOST issue/<key>/comment{ id, key, author, body, created }.
List commentsissue/<key>/comment{ items, count, truncated }: the newest first, each with author, body (plain text), created.
Add labels, Remove labelsPUT issue/<key>{ key, labels }. The other labels are kept. A label has no spaces.
Link issuesPOST issueLink{ key, type, other }: this issue blocks (the link type's outward description) the other one.
Attach a fileissue/<key>/attachments{ id, filename, size, mimeType, content }: a project file, such as {{ file.id }}.
Delete an issueDELETE issue/<key>{ key, deleted }. An issue with subtasks only with With its subtasks.

Settings

SettingDescription
Jira credentialA Jira credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Search issues (JQL); Get an issue; Create an issue; Update an issue; Change the status; List the transitions; Assign an issue; Add a comment; List comments; Add labels; Remove labels; Link issues; Attach a file; Delete an issue. Default: Search issues (JQL). Required.
JQLe.g. project = OPS AND status != Done ORDER BY created DESC. (Required for: Search issues (JQL).)
FieldsMore fields to read, e.g. customfield_10016, timetracking (Get an issue reads them all). (For: Search issues (JQL).)
IssueIts key (OPS-123), its address, or an issue of a search or a trigger. (Required for: Get an issue, Update an issue, Change the status, List the transitions, Assign an issue, Add a comment, List comments, Add labels, Remove labels, Link issues, Attach a file, Delete an issue.)
ProjectIts key, e.g. OPS. (Required for: Create an issue.)
TypeIts name, e.g. Task, Bug, Story, Sub-task. Default: Task. (Required for: Create an issue.)
SummaryRequired to create; update: empty is unchanged. (For: Create an issue, Update an issue.)
DescriptionPlain text: paragraphs at blank lines. (For: Create an issue, Update an issue.)
PriorityIts name: Highest, High, Medium, Low, Lowest. (For: Create an issue, Update an issue.)
AssigneeAn email, a name or an account ID; - : unassigned. (For: Create an issue, Update an issue, Assign an issue.)
LabelsSeparated by commas, or a list (no spaces in a label); update: replaces them all. (For: Create an issue, Update an issue, Add labels, Remove labels.)
ComponentsTheir names, separated by commas. (For: Create an issue, Update an issue.)
Due dateA date (2026-12-31) or relative (+7 days). (For: Create an issue, Update an issue.)
ParentFor a sub-task, or an epic's child: the parent's key. (For: Create an issue.)
Other fieldsA JSON object merged into the fields, as Jira names them, e.g. {"customfield_10016": 5}. (For: Create an issue, Update an issue.)
ToThe transition's name or the status it leads to, e.g. In Progress, Done. (Required for: Change the status.)
Resolutione.g. Done, Won't Do; only when the transition's screen has it. (For: Change the status.)
CommentPlain text. Transition: optional, added with it. (Required for: Add a comment.)
Link typeIts name: Blocks, Relates, Duplicate, Cloners, …. Default: Relates. (Required for: Link issues.)
Other issueThis issue <outward description> the other, e.g. OPS-1 blocks OPS-2. (Required for: Link issues.)
Project fileThe id of a file of the project, e.g. {{ file.id }}. (Required for: Attach a file.)
Largest size (MB)Default: 10. (Required for: Attach a file.)
With its subtasksAn issue with subtasks cannot be deleted without. Default: off. (For: Delete an issue.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 100. Required. (For: Search issues (JQL), List the transitions, List comments.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: issues. Required.
On errorJira's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, alerts as tickets: a monitoring trigger, then Search issues for an open one (project = OPS AND labels = {{ alert.host }} AND statusCategory != Done); when {{ issues.count }} is 0, Create an issue, else Add a comment. When the alert clears, Change the status to Done.

pages.title: Jira API
pages.summary: Any request of Jira's REST API.
pages.html:
The Jira API step sends any request of the site's REST API, as the credential's user: what the other Jira steps don't have, such as worklogs, watchers, versions, filters, or Jira Software's boards and sprints (/rest/agile/1.0/…). It is an advanced step.

pages.title: HubSpot
pages.summary: Contacts, companies, deals, tickets and custom objects of HubSpot's CRM, notes and associations, any API request, and a record trigger.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to HubSpot's CRM through HubSpot's API, with a private app's access token. Its steps are in the CRM group of the step list:

  • HubSpot Records: searches, reads, creates, updates (or creates or updates by email) and deletes contacts, companies, deals, tickets and custom objects; associates them, and adds notes.
  • HubSpot CRM: properties (their internal names and choices), pipelines and their stages, owners.
  • HubSpot API: any request of HubSpot's API.

The HubSpot record trigger starts a workflow when records are created or updated.

The credential

In HubSpot, open Settings > Integrations > Private apps (a super admin can), create a private app, and choose its scopes: what the workflows may read and change, such as crm.objects.contacts.read and crm.objects.contacts.write, the same for companies and deals, tickets, crm.schemas.contacts.read (properties), crm.objects.owners.read. Copy its access token. Then, under Credentials & variables, create a HubSpot credential, in the CRM group, with that token. It is stored encrypted.

Test shows the account (its ID), where its data is hosted, its currency and time zone.

What the steps share

  • Properties are HubSpot's internal names, such as firstname, lifecyclestage, dealname, dealstage, hubspot_owner_id. HubSpot CRM List properties shows them, and an enumeration's values; List pipelines the stage IDs.
  • A record is { id, url, createdAt, updatedAt, archived, properties }, with its properties also at the top: {{ contact.email }}. url opens it in HubSpot.
  • Records are given by ID, or as a record of a search or the trigger ({{ item }}, {{ record }}).
  • Lists give { items, count, truncated }, at most At most (items); a search also gives its total. A search reaches at most 10,000 records.
  • Errors: HubSpot's message and its category, such as Contact already exists. Existing ID: 1001 (CONFLICT). A missing scope is reported by HubSpot. When HubSpot's rate limit is reached, the step waits and sends the request again, within its Timeout. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.

Note: for an AI step, creating, updating, associating and deleting records are write operations: not offered by default, and they ask for approval when approvals are on.

pages.title: HubSpot Records
pages.summary: Searches, reads, creates, updates and deletes CRM records; associations and notes.
pages.html:
The HubSpot Records step works with the records of one object type: contacts, companies, deals, tickets, or a custom object (its type ID, such as 2-1234567, or its name).

The credential, the results and the errors are the same for every HubSpot step: see HubSpot.

Operations

OperationHubSpot APIResult
Search recordsPOST crm/v3/objects/<type>/search{ items, count, truncated } and total: the records the filters find (all to match) and the text, sorted.
Get a recordGET crm/v3/objects/<type>/<id>The record, by ID or by a unique property in Find by (a contact's email). None: null, not an error, so the workflow can create it.
Create a recordPOST crm/v3/objects/<type>The new record.
Update a recordPATCH crm/v3/objects/<type>/<id>The record. Only the properties given change.
Create or update a recordsearch, then POST or PATCHThe record, with created (true or false). The record that has the value of Find by (such as the email in the properties) is updated; none: one is created.
Delete a recordDELETE crm/v3/objects/<type>/<id>{ id, deleted }. It goes to the recycling bin.
Associate with a recordPUT crm/v4/…/associations/default/…{ id, type, toId, toType }: the two types' default association (a contact with its company, a deal with its contacts).
List associated recordsGET crm/v4/…/associations/<type>{ items, count, truncated }: { id, types } of the records of the other type.
Add a notePOST crm/v3/objects/notes{ id, recordId, type }: a note on the record's timeline. Text (line breaks kept) or HTML.

Filters

One per line, all to match: <property> <operator> <value>. Operators: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, contains, !contains, in and !in (values separated by commas), has and !has (no value: the property is set or not). Dates are written 2026-11-01 or in ISO 8601. At most 6. For example:

lifecyclestage = lead
createdate >= 2026-11-01
hs_lead_status in NEW, OPEN

Settings

SettingDescription
HubSpot credentialA HubSpot credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Search records; Get a record; Create a record; Update a record; Create or update a record; Delete a record; Associate with a record; List associated records; Add a note. Default: Search records. Required.
RecordsChoices: Contacts; Companies; Deals; Tickets; A custom object. Default: Contacts. Required.
Custom objectIts type ID (2-1234567) or name.
FiltersOne per line, all to match: <property> <operator> <value>; =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, contains, in (a, b), has, !has; dates as 2026-11-01. e.g. lifecyclestage = lead. (For: Search records.)
TextWords in the default searchable properties (a contact's name, email, phone, …); empty: none. (For: Search records.)
Sorted byA property, then asc or desc, e.g. createdate desc. (For: Search records.)
PropertiesMore to read, separated by commas (the usual ones are read); associations: the other records' properties are not read. (For: Search records, Get a record, List associated records.)
RecordIts ID, or a record of a search or a trigger. (Required for: Get a record, Update a record, Delete a record, Associate with a record, List associated records, Add a note.)
Find byA unique property instead of the ID, e.g. email; upsert: required (its value is in the properties). (Required for: Create or update a record.)
PropertiesA JSON object, as HubSpot names them, e.g. {"email": "{{ form.email }}", "firstname": "{{ form.name }}", "lifecyclestage": "lead"}. (Required for: Create a record, Update a record, Create or update a record.)
Other recordsChoices: Contacts; Companies; Deals; Tickets; A custom object. Default: Companies. (Required for: Associate with a record, List associated records.)
Other custom objectIts type ID or name.
Other recordIts ID, or a record of a search. (Required for: Associate with a record.)
NoteText (or HTML); {{ ... }} for expressions. (Required for: Add a note.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 100. Required. (For: Search records, List associated records.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: records. Required.
On errorHubSpot's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, website leads: a Form trigger, then Create or update a record of contacts with Find by email and the properties {"email": "{{ form.email }}", "firstname": "{{ form.name }}", "lifecyclestage": "lead"}, then Add a note with the message.

pages.title: Salesforce
pages.summary: Records of a Salesforce org (SOQL, SOSL, create, update, upsert by external ID, activities), its objects and limits, any REST request, and a record trigger.
pages.html:
Rail22 connects to a Salesforce org through its REST API. Its steps are in the CRM group of the step list:

  • Salesforce Records: SOQL queries, finding and searching records, reading, creating, updating (or creating or updating by an external ID) and deleting them, and logging activities.
  • Salesforce Org: the org's objects, an object's fields and picklist values, the limits, the user.
  • Salesforce API: any request of the REST API, such as composite, Apex REST or reports.

The Salesforce record trigger starts a workflow when records are created or updated.

The app in Salesforce

Rail22 signs in with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow: as an app, acting as one user of the org (its run-as user). In Salesforce Setup:

  1. Open External Client App Manager and create an app (a Connected App works as well). Enable OAuth, with the scope Manage user data via APIs (api), and enable the Client Credentials Flow.
  2. In the app's policies, choose the run-as user: the steps do what that user may. An integration user (with the Salesforce Integration license and only the permissions the workflows need) keeps the access small and the changes easy to tell apart.
  3. Copy the app's Consumer Key and Consumer Secret, and the org's address from Setup > My Domain.

The credential

Under Credentials & variables, create a Salesforce credential, in the CRM group:

SettingDescription
My DomainThe org's address, such as https://acme.my.salesforce.com, or a sandbox's (https://acme--uat.sandbox.my.salesforce.com). The client credentials flow works only there, not at login.salesforce.com.
API versionSuch as 64.0.
Consumer key, Consumer secretThe app's. The secret is stored encrypted.

Test shows the org, whether it is a sandbox, the API version and the run-as user.

What the steps share

  • Objects and fields are given by their API names: Account, Lead, Invoice__c; LastName, StageName, ERP_Id__c. Salesforce Org Describe an object shows them, with the picklists' values.
  • A record has its fields as Salesforce gives them ({{ lead.Email }}; related records as objects: {{ contact.Account.Name }}), plus type (the object) and url (the record in Lightning).
  • Records are given by ID (15 or 18 characters), or as a record of a query or the trigger.
  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Errors: Salesforce's message, its code and the fields, such as Required fields are missing: [LastName] (REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING). With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.
  • Limits: every request counts towards the org's daily API requests (Salesforce Org Get the limits), the trigger's checks too.

Note: for an AI step, creating, updating, deleting records and logging activities are write operations: not offered by default, and they ask for approval when approvals are on.

pages.title: Salesforce Records
pages.summary: SOQL queries, finding and searching, reading, creating, updating, upserting and deleting records, activities.
pages.html:
The Salesforce Records step works with the org's records: of the chosen object (Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Cases, or another object by its API name), or of any object with a SOQL query.

The credential, the results and the errors are the same for every Salesforce step: see Salesforce.

Operations

OperationSalesforce REST APIResult
Run a SOQL queryquery{ items, count, total, truncated }: the records of the query, as written: any object, relationships (Account.Name), subqueries. All pages are read, up to At most.
Find recordsquery{ items, count, total, truncated }: the object's records that Where (a SOQL condition) finds, sorted by Order by, with the fields named (empty: the object's usual ones).
Search by textsearch (SOSL){ items, count, total, truncated }: the object's records with the text in any field.
Get a recordsobjects/<object>/<id>The record, with the fields named (empty: all). None: null, not an error.
Create a recordPOST sobjects/<object>{ id, type, created }.
Update a recordPATCH sobjects/<object>/<id>{ id, type, updated }: only the fields given change.
Create or update by external IDPATCH sobjects/<object>/<field>/<value>{ id, type, created }: the record whose external ID field has the value is updated; none: one is created with it.
Delete a recordDELETE sobjects/<object>/<id>{ id, type, deleted }. It goes to the recycle bin.
Log an activityPOST sobjects/Task{ id, recordId, subject }: a completed task, dated today, on the record's activity timeline (a contact's or lead's as its Name, another record's as Related to).

The fields to write are a JSON object of API names, such as {"LastName": "{{ form.name }}", "Company": "{{ form.company }}", "LeadSource": "Web"}. In a SOQL condition, put text values in single quotes; a value from a variable with quotes in it needs them escaped (\').
