An AI step can be set to ask before it changes something, such as blocking an address on a firewall. Its request arrives as a task titled Approve: …, for example Approve: Block IPs 203.0.113.7, Blocked on FortiGate fw-hq. The task shows:

  • which step asks, and why: the reason the agent gave;
  • the tool it wants to use and its arguments, one per line;
  • a choice Approve or Reject for each action (several actions asked together come in one task), and a comment.

When the action was asked for in a conversation and the step names no approvers, the person talking to the agent does not get the task: any other project member does. If nobody else can decide, it waits until its time limit.

Check the arguments, decide, and press Send. An approved action runs at once, as the agent asked. A rejected one does not run: the agent is told rejected by your name and your comment, so write in the comment what is wrong or what to do instead. The agent then goes on, and may ask again with other arguments.

A task with a time limit expires when it passes: its actions are refused. Your decision is recorded in the audit log, with the action and its arguments.

Note: users with the Participant role see Forms and My tasks. They don't see the workflows.

pages.title: Data tables
pages.summary: Simple tables inside Rail22: columns, rows, importing CSV or Excel, and using them in workflows.
pages.html:
Data tables are simple tables kept inside Rail22, one set per project. Workflows read and write them with the Data Table step, and you can browse and edit them by hand. Use them for lists of customers, processed orders, settings, logs of what a workflow did, and so on.

Creating a table

Open Data Tables in the sidebar. Create an empty table and add its columns, or Import a file to create the table from it.

Columns

SettingDescription
LabelThe column's title.
KeyIts name in workflows: {{ table.rows[0].email }}. Letters, digits or underscore, not starting with a digit. It cannot be changed later.
TypeText, Textarea, Number, Email, Url, Checkbox, Switch, Datetime, Date, Select (a list of choices, one per line) or Object (points to a user, a file, or a row of another table). It cannot be changed later.
RequiredRows must have a value in this column.

Each row also has an id, and the times it was created and last updated (created_at, updated_at).

Rows

Add, edit and delete rows on the table's page. The grid can be sorted and filtered. Values are checked against the columns' types and rules, both by hand and from workflows.

Views

A filter can be saved as a view. Apply the filter, open View next to Filter, type a name and save. The views are shared: everyone who can open the table sees them, uses them and can delete them. Choosing a view fills in its filter and reloads the rows. Changing the filter by hand leaves the view. When a table is deleted, its views go with it.

The number of rows per page is remembered in your browser, the same for every table. The page number can be typed or stepped with its arrows: the page changes a moment after you stop, or at once with Enter.

Exporting to Excel

Export, next to Filter, downloads the rows as an Excel (.xlsx) file. It holds every row the current search and filter find, across all pages, in one sheet. Numbers, dates and checkboxes keep their types, so they can be sorted and calculated in Excel. Selects and objects are written as the text the grid shows. A cell holds at most 32,767 characters, so longer text is cut, and a sheet holds at most 1,048,575 rows: filter a larger table first. Each export is recorded in the audit log.

Importing CSV or Excel

  1. Click Import and choose a .csv, .tsv, .txt or .xlsx file.
  2. In the preview, give the table a name, choose the sheet (Excel) and whether the first row is a header.
  3. Check the columns found: import each one or not, and set its name, key and type. The types are guessed from the values. The first rows are shown as they will be read.
  4. Click Import.

Limits

Your plan may limit the number of tables and the rows in one table. The Usage tab of Account settings shows where you stand.

AI steps can also work with data tables when you allow their tools: list and query tables, and insert, update or delete rows. See AI steps.

Designing tables, relations between them and the usual patterns are in Using data tables.

Moving to another project

In the table's row on the Data Tables page, Move takes the table to another project, with its columns, rows and views. You need permission to delete it in its project and to create tables in the new one. It keeps its shares with other projects; a share with the new project ends, as the table is now at home there. Personal projects cannot receive it, and the new project must not already have a table of that name.

Workflows of the old project that use the table fail at that step until they are changed or the new project shares it back. The dialog names them before you move.

Sharing with other projects

A table belongs to one project, and that project can share it with other projects of the account. In its row in the list, click Share, choose a project and what it may do:

LevelWhat the other project may do
Read rowsRead the rows, in the table's page and with the Data Table step.
Read and change rowsAlso add, change and delete rows.

Only the table's own project can change its columns, rename it, delete it or share it further. It appears in the other project under Shared with this project, and in the Data Table step with the name of its project. What each person can do still depends on their role in that project: a Participant gets nothing, and an Owner there cannot change rows of a table shared for reading.

  • Who can share: the permission Share data tables, which only Owners have by default. Personal projects neither share nor receive.
  • Who it reaches: a project, not a person: every workflow editor of that project can use the table in their workflows.
  • Stopping: the dialog shows which workflows use the table there. After you remove the share, those workflows fail at the step that uses it. A table cannot be deleted while it is shared.
  • Linked tables: if a column points to a table that is not shared, who reads this table also sees the labels of those rows. The dialog warns of it.
  • Logs: a share and its changes are in the audit log of both projects. Changes to rows are in the logs of the table's own project; those made by a workflow name the project it runs in.
  • Not shared: a shared table cannot be an AI step's long-term memory. Exports do not include it: importing such a workflow warns that the table is missing.

pages.title: Knowledge bases
pages.summary: Documents that workflows and AI steps search by meaning and by words: the embedding model, adding files, web pages and texts, re-indexing.
pages.html:
A knowledge base holds documents (files, web pages, texts) cut into short passages, so that workflows and AI steps can find the passages that answer a question. Each project has its own knowledge bases. Use them to answer customers from your manuals, to have an AI step follow your policies, to look up product sheets, and so on.

A search finds passages in two ways and merges the two lists: by meaning (a passage about "annual leave" answers "how many vacation days do I have?") and by words (exact names, codes and numbers). Workflows search with the Knowledge base step, and AI steps search on their own when you give them knowledge bases.

Before you start: the embedding model

Meaning is compared through embeddings: an embedding model turns each passage, and each question, into a list of numbers. The account has one embedding model, used by all its projects. Set it in the Settings menu, under Knowledge bases (users who may update the account's settings):

SettingDescription
ProviderWho makes the embeddings: a server of your own (Ollama, Lemonade server, LM Studio) or a provider's API (OpenAI or another OpenAI-compatible server, Google Gemini), with your key and at your costs.
Server URLEmpty: the provider's own address. It is reached from Rail22's server: localhost means that machine.
API keyRequired for OpenAI and Gemini. Ollama, Lemonade and LM Studio: only when the server asks for one. Kept encrypted; left empty, the saved key is kept.
Embedding modelClick Connect to list the server's models, the embedding ones first. For example nomic-embed-text or bge-m3 (Ollama), text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI), gemini-embedding-001 (Gemini).

Embeddings are made by your server or with your own key: they don't use the account's AI credits.

Note: a knowledge base remembers the model it was indexed with. After you choose another model, the knowledge bases that have documents must be re-indexed (see below) before they can be searched or added to again. The settings page lists them. Empty knowledge bases simply take the new model.

Creating a knowledge base

Open Knowledge bases in the sidebar, under the project's workspace, and click Create:

SettingDescription
NameHow the workflows name it: unique in the project, at most 80 characters. Required.
DescriptionWhat its documents are about. The AI steps read it to decide when to search.
Chunk sizeUnder Advanced…: the characters per passage, from 200 to 8000. Default: 1000. A small embedding model needs small passages (512 tokens are about 1000 characters).
OverlapUnder Advanced…: the characters repeated at the start of the next passage, at most half the chunk size. Default: 150.

A new chunk size or overlap applies to the documents added from then on. The others keep how they were cut until they are added again.

The Knowledge base step also creates a knowledge base: its first Add to a name the project doesn't have yet makes it, with the default chunk size and overlap.

Adding documents

Open the knowledge base and choose what to add:

  • Project files: PDF, Office or text files from the project's Files.
  • Upload files: files from your computer. They are saved with the project's files too.
  • Web page: the text of a page, from its address. Only public addresses can be read, unless the installation allows others.
  • Text: a title and a text, with an optional key (by default, the title).

The documents added on this page are indexed in the background: their status is Indexing, then Indexed, or Error (point at it to read why). The list refreshes by itself.

Each document has a key: the file's id, the page's address, or the text's key. Adding a document with the same key again replaces it; when nothing changed, it is left as it is. The text is read from:

  • PDF: page by page, so the results tell the page. A scanned PDF without text has nothing to add.
  • Office documents: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument files.
  • Text files: txt, csv, md, json, xml, html and the like.

Images have no text and are not added. Remove deletes a document's passages from the knowledge base; a project file stays in Files.

Trying a search

Try a search on the knowledge base's page finds what the workflows and the AI steps would find. Type a question or keywords: each result shows the passage, its document, its similarity to the question (from -1 to 1, higher is closer), and whether it was found by meaning, by words, or both.

Re-indexing

Re-index embeds every passage again with the account's embedding model, in the background. It is needed after the account's model changes. Until it is done, searches and additions fail with a message saying so.

Using them in workflows

  • The Knowledge base step searches a knowledge base and keeps the results, ready for the next steps; it also adds files, web pages and texts, removes documents and lists them. A workflow can keep a knowledge base up to date, for example from a folder of files or a list of pages.
  • The AI steps have a Knowledge bases setting: the model searches the chosen knowledge bases when it needs to, as many times as it needs, and answers from what it found.
  • AI assistants connected through the project's MCP server, such as Claude Desktop or Claude Code, list the knowledge bases (list_knowledge_bases) and search them (query_knowledge_base), with the permissions of the token's user.

Example: answer questions from your manuals

  1. Create a knowledge base Manuals, with the description "Product manuals and the support FAQ", and add the PDF manuals.
  2. Email (inbound) trigger, variable mail.
  3. Claude, with Knowledge bases = Manuals. Prompt: "Answer this customer's question from the manuals. Say so when they don't answer it.", then {{ mail.text }}.
  4. Send email: the answer, {{ ai.html }}, to the customer or to the support team for review.

For more control, search first with the Knowledge base step (Query {{ mail.subject }}) and put the passages found in the AI step's prompt: {{ kb.context }}.

Limits

WhatAt most
Text read from one document1,000,000 characters (the rest is left out)
Passages (chunks) in one knowledge base25,000
Results of a search50 (the Knowledge base step); 20 per search by an AI step
Files added by one step50

Knowledge bases are not part of a project's export and import. Who may create, view and search, change and delete them is set by the roles. Self-hosted installations need MongoDB 8.3 or later for them (see Requirements).

pages.title: Files
pages.summary: The project's files: uploading, previewing, and using them in workflows.
pages.html:
Files, in the sidebar, holds the project's files: those you upload, and those saved by workflows, such as email attachments, downloads and FTP files.

Uploading

Drag files onto the list, or use the upload button. These types are accepted:

KindExtensions
Imagepng, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, bmp, tif, tiff, svg, heic
PDFpdf
Word, Documentdoc, docx, odt, rtf
Excel, Spreadsheet, CSVxls, xlsx, ods, csv, tsv
PowerPoint, Presentationppt, pptx, odp
Text, Markdown, HTMLtxt, log, md, html, htm
JSON, XML, YAMLjson, xml, yaml, yml

The largest file depends on the server's settings. Your plan may limit the space used by all files.

Previewing and downloading

Click a file to open its page. Images, PDF, Word and Excel files are shown in the page. Every file can be downloaded.

Files in workflows

  • A File upload trigger starts a workflow when a file is uploaded.
  • Steps that save files give their id: {{ file.id }} (Download File), {{ mail.attachment_files }}, {{ ftp.files }}.
  • Steps that use files take these ids: email attachments and images, AI step files, FTP / SFTP Upload, Google Drive and OneDrive uploads.

pages.title: Credentials & variables
pages.summary: Storing passwords, API keys and OAuth connections for the steps, and the project's shared variables.
pages.html:
Credentials & variables, in the sidebar, holds what the project's steps need to connect to other systems, and the values its workflows share.

  • Credentials are stored encrypted. After saving, secret fields are not shown again. Leave them empty when editing to keep the saved value.
  • Steps refer to a credential by name, so a workflow never contains a secret.
  • A credential belongs to one project, and only that project's workflows can use it.

Kinds of credentials

GroupCredentialUsed by
HTTPAPI key, Basic auth, Bearer tokenHTTP Request, Download File
AIAnthropic (Claude), OpenAI API (or compatible server), Google Gemini, Ollama server, Lemonade server, LM Studio serverThe AI steps
AIMCP serverAI steps (the tools of an external MCP server)
EmailIMAP server (password), Google Mail (OAuth), Microsoft 365 Mail (OAuth)Read emails (IMAP); Google Mail also for Gmail
FilesFTP / SFTP serverFTP / SFTP, FTP / SFTP Upload
FilesDecryption key, Verification key, Encryption key, Signing keyDecrypting, checking signatures, encrypting and signing files in the FTP steps (PGP / GPG, OpenSSL, S/MIME)
GoogleGoogle Drive, Sheets, Calendar, Docs (OAuth)The Google steps
MicrosoftOutlook Mail, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive & SharePoint, Microsoft Teams (Microsoft Graph)The Microsoft 365 steps
MicrosoftMicrosoft IntuneThe Intune steps and the Intune device trigger (an app of the tenant, no user)
DatabaseMySQL / MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, Firebird, ODBC data sourceThe database steps: each takes the credentials of its kind
SecurityBitdefender GravityZoneThe GravityZone steps and the GravityZone event trigger
SecurityFortiGateThe FortiGate steps
SecuritySophos FirewallThe Sophos Firewall steps
SecurityWazuhThe Wazuh steps and the Wazuh alert trigger
MonitoringCheckmkThe Checkmk steps and the Checkmk problem trigger
MonitoringZabbixThe Zabbix steps and the Zabbix problem trigger
VirtualizationVMware vCenterThe VMware steps and the VMware alarm trigger
VirtualizationProxmox VEThe Proxmox steps and the Proxmox task trigger
VirtualizationHyper-VThe Hyper-V steps and the Hyper-V VM state trigger
Domains & DNSNamecheapThe Namecheap steps
E-commerceShopifyThe Shopify steps and the Shopify event trigger
Files & collaborationNextcloudThe Nextcloud steps and the Nextcloud file trigger
Work managementJiraThe Jira steps and the Jira issue trigger
Work managementGLPIThe GLPI steps and the GLPI ticket trigger
CRMHubSpotThe HubSpot steps and the HubSpot record trigger
CRMSalesforceThe Salesforce steps and the Salesforce record trigger
BackupVeeam Backup & ReplicationThe Veeam steps and the Veeam event trigger
DirectoriesLDAP serverThe LDAP step
OtherVariableAny expression, as {{ vars.<name> }}

Kinds that depend on the installation, such as the databases, appear only when available.

Testing

Most credentials have a Test button that tries the connection and shows the result. AI server credentials also record the models the server offers, so the AI steps can list them. The list shows when each credential was last tested and used.

OAuth credentials (Google, Microsoft)

OAuth credentials connect with an OAuth app that you register at the provider. Step-by-step guides: Google and Microsoft 365. In short:

  1. Create a web application OAuth app at the provider and enable the APIs you need, such as the Gmail API or Microsoft Graph permissions.
  2. Add the Redirect URI shown in the credential's form to the app.
  3. Copy the app's Client ID and Client secret into the credential and save.
  4. Click Connect. You are sent to the provider to sign in and consent, then back. Account then shows who the credential acts as.

Rail22 renews the access token by itself. If the consent is withdrawn at the provider, connect again.

Project variables

A credential of kind Variable is a shared value: a base URL, a team's address, a threshold. Its name must be a valid identifier. Every workflow of the project reads it as {{ vars.<name> }}, and its Description appears in the expression suggestions. Change the value once, and every workflow uses the new one at its next run.

Moving to another project

In the credential's row, Move takes it to another project, with its secrets. You need permission to delete it in its project and to create credentials in the new one. It keeps its shares with other projects; a share with the new project ends, as the credential is now at home there. Personal projects cannot receive it, and the new project must not already have a credential of that name. Variables are not moved: workflows read them by name, and each project has its own.

Workflows of the old project that use the credential fail at that step until they are changed or the new project shares it back. The dialog names them before you move.

Sharing with other projects

A credential belongs to one project, and that project can share it with other projects of the account, so its secret is kept and rotated in one place. In its row in the list, click Share and choose a project. The credential then appears in that project's steps with the name of its project, and under Shared with this project.

  • What the other project can do: use it in workflows, with its full rights. It sees the name, the type and the project; it cannot see the secret or the settings, and it cannot test, change, connect or delete it.
  • Who it reaches: a project, not a person: every workflow editor of that project can use it.
  • Who can share: the permission Share credentials, which only Owners have by default. Personal projects neither share nor receive.
  • Stopping: the dialog shows which workflows use it there. After you remove the share, those workflows fail at the step that uses it. A credential cannot be deleted while it is shared.
  • Variables are not shared: each project has its own.
  • Mailboxes: if several projects start workflows from one mailbox, each one reads the same mail.

Hosts of a shared API credential

The HTTP Request and Download File steps choose their own address, so a credential they can use (API key, Basic, Bearer, OAuth, AI providers) could be sent anywhere. When you share one, list the hosts it may be sent to, like api.example.com or *.example.com. A request to any other host fails before anything is sent, and such a request does not follow redirects. Its own project is not limited.

Warning: you can tick Allow any host instead. A workflow editor in that project can then send the secret to a server of theirs and read it. Use it only for a project you would give the secret to. The choice is recorded in the audit log of both projects.

pages.title: The Assistant
pages.summary: Building and changing workflows by describing them in your own words.
pages.html:
The Assistant builds workflows for you. Describe what you want in plain words, and it adds and connects the steps, fills in their settings, and explains what it did. You see the changes on the canvas as they happen. It is part of Rail22 itself, on every plan, Free included.

Using it

  1. In the designer, click the Assistant button (the stars icon) in the toolbar. The panel opens on the right.
  2. Describe the workflow or the change, for example:
    • "Every morning at 8, get yesterday's orders from https://shop.example.com/api/orders and email a summary to sales@example.com."
    • "Add an error output to the HTTP request that notifies me by email."
    • "Why does this workflow fail at the If step?"
  3. Press Send, or Stop to interrupt it.

Changes are saved like your own. If you don't like a change, press Ctrl+Z to undo it. Each workflow keeps its conversation with the Assistant.

Note: the Assistant uses the credentials and tables that exist in the project. It cannot create credentials: add them yourself, then ask it to use them.

What the Assistant may read

The account's owners choose it under Settings → Assistant, in Data access:

  • Structure only (default): the Assistant sees the project's data tables and their columns, workflows, step types, file names and variable names, and can create tables and columns and change other workflows. It reads no rows, file contents or images, does not run workflows or see their results, and doesn't see the variables' values. When a request needs data, it says so, or builds the workflow so that it reads the data when it runs.
  • Structure and data: it may also query, add and change rows, read files and images, run workflows and read their results, with the rights of the person asking.

In both cases it sees the workflow on the canvas, settings included. Everything it sees is sent to the Assistant's provider: with your own provider, under that provider's terms.

Settings

An owner sets up the Assistant under Settings → Assistant:

SettingDescription
ProviderWho runs the Assistant: System AI (provided by this installation, when it has one, paid with the account's AI credits), or your own account with Claude (Anthropic), OpenAI (or a compatible server), Google Gemini, Ollama, a Lemonade server or LM Studio (your key, your costs).
Server URL, API keyFor your own provider. The URL is empty for the provider's own API, or a proxy or local server.
ModelConnect to list the server's models.
EffortHow thoroughly Claude thinks: higher is better for large workflows, lower is faster and cheaper.
Monthly budget (USD)The most the Assistant may spend per calendar month, with your own key. Empty or 0: no limit.
Monthly credit limitWith the System AI: the Assistant stops once the credits the account used this month (by the Assistant and the AI steps) reach it.
May readWhat the Assistant may read of the projects: Structure only (default) or Structure and data. See What the Assistant may read above.

When the Assistant isn't set up yet, its panel says so and links to these settings.

pages.title: Signing in
pages.summary: The sign-in page, remember me, several accounts, forgotten passwords, two-factor codes and single sign-on.
pages.html:
Sign in with your email address and password. Depending on your account's settings, you may also sign in with your company directory (LDAP) or your identity provider (SSO).

The sign-in page

  • Remember me: stay signed in after closing the browser. Without it, closing the browser signs you out.
  • Several accounts: if your address is a user of more than one Rail22 account, you choose which one after signing in.
  • Two-factor code: if you activated two-factor authentication, you are asked for the code from your authenticator app.
  • Sign in with SSO: when your account uses SAML single sign-on, type your email. You are sent to your identity provider and back.

Forgot your password

Click Forgot username or password? and type your email. You receive a link to choose a new password, valid for a limited time. Setting a new password signs you out everywhere else.

Users who sign in with LDAP or SSO have no Rail22 password: they change it in their directory or identity provider.

Being signed out

Your account may sign you out after a period of inactivity, and after a maximum session length. Both are set by an owner in Account settings.

pages.title: Your profile and two-factor authentication
pages.summary: Your name and email, changing your password, and protecting your sign-in with an authenticator app.
pages.html:
Open your profile from the sidebar: click your name at the bottom, then Personal.

Basic information

Your first name, last name and email. Your role is set by an owner, so you cannot change it here.

Password

Click Change to set a new password. You type your current password, then the new one twice.

Two-factor authentication (2FA)

With 2FA, signing in also asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password or Authy. Someone who learns your password still cannot sign in.

  1. In Security, choose to activate two-factor authentication.
  2. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or type the key it shows.
  3. Type the code the app shows now, then click Activate.

To turn it off, deactivate it in the same place. It asks for a current code.

Warning: when your account enforces MFA, you must activate 2FA before you can use the app. The profile page says so, and you cannot turn it off.

pages.title: Users
pages.summary: The account's users: adding people, roles and states.
pages.html:
Users, in the Settings menu, lists the people of the account. Only users who may see all the account's users have this page, which by default means owners.

Adding people

There are two ways:

  • Invite them to a project (recommended): in the project's settings, Members → Invite by email. They receive a link, choose their name and password, and join the account as Members of that project. See Projects and members.
  • Create a user: on the Users page, click Create and give their first name, last name, email and role. They receive an email with a link to choose their password, valid once for 7 days.

With LDAP or SAML sign-in, users can also be created automatically the first time they sign in. See LDAP sign-in and SAML single sign-on.

Editing a user

Click a user, or Edit in their row's menu, to change their first name, last name, email, role and state.

  • Send sign-in link emails them a new link to choose a password, for example when the first one expired or they lost access. It is offered for active users who sign in with a Rail22 password (not LDAP or SSO users).
  • Setting a user to Disabled signs them out everywhere at once.
  • The account always keeps an active Owner: the last one cannot be given another role or disabled. Give someone else the Owner role first.
  • Your own user opens your profile: you cannot change your own role or state.

Roles

Each user has an account role: Owner, Member, Participant, or a role you create. It decides what they may do across the account. In each project, a member also has a project role. See Roles and permissions.

States

StateMeaning
ActiveCan sign in.
UnconfirmedSigned up but has not confirmed their email yet.
DisabledCannot sign in.

pages.title: Roles and permissions
pages.summary: The built-in roles, creating your own, and what each permission and scope allows.
pages.html:
What a user may do comes from their role. A role is a list of permissions, each with a scope.

The built-in roles

RoleFor
OwnerThe people who run the account: everything, including account settings, users, roles, logs and usage.
MemberThe people who build: workflows, credentials, data tables, knowledge bases and files in the projects they belong to. They see only their own user, and cannot change the account's settings.
ParticipantThe people who take part: they fill in the project's forms and complete the tasks assigned to them, and see no workflows.

Some permissions of the built-in roles are locked so that an account cannot lock itself out. They are shown greyed out.

Creating and editing roles

Open Roles in the Settings menu. Create a role, or open one to edit its permissions. For each permission, tick it to allow it and choose its scope, then Save.

Scopes

ScopeAllows the permission on
globalEverything in the account.
projectWhat belongs to the projects the user is a member of.
ownThe user's own record only (their profile, their password).

Permissions

AreaPermissionsScopes
AccountUpdate account settings; view the account's usage and its plan's limitsglobal
UsersCreate, view (and list), edit, delete users; change passwordglobal (edit, change password: also own)
ProjectsCreate, view (and list), edit, delete projects; export and import workflows, credentials (with their secrets) and data tables (Owner only by default)global
RolesCreate, view (and list), edit, delete rolesglobal
WorkflowsCreate, view (and list), edit, delete workflows; publish and unpublishglobal, project
CredentialsCreate, view (and list; secrets are never shown), edit / test / connect, deleteglobal, project
Data tablesCreate, view the columns (and list), edit the columns, delete tables; view the data; change the dataglobal, project
Knowledge basesCreate; view (and list), their documents, and search them; change their settings, add and remove documents, re-index; deleteglobal, project
FilesCreate (upload), view (and list), edit, deleteglobal, project
LogsView the audit log; view the execution log (project scope: the entries of the user's projects)global, project
MCP server tokensCreate, view (and list), delete (revoke); only in projects whose MCP server is on (Account settings, Data access)global, project

"View" also allows listing. For example, a role that may view workflows in project scope sees the workflows of its projects in the sidebar.

Project roles

In a project, each member has a role for that project. Inside a project, that project role decides what they may do. So the same person can be a Member in one project and a Participant in another.

The account role adds to this only through permissions with global scope, which apply in every project of the account, even for someone who is not a member. Project scope in the account role gives nothing by itself: it has effect in a role given to a member of a project.

pages.title: Account settings
pages.summary: Security (MFA, session limits), how long logs are kept, date formats, and the AI policy for agents.
pages.html:
Account settings, in the Settings menu, apply to every user of the account. Its tabs: Settings and Data access, described here, for users who may update the account (the owners), AI, for the owners, and Usage, for users who may view the account's usage (see Usage and AI credits). When the installation receives mail, the owners also have Inbound mail (see Inbound mail). Without the Multi-tenant plugin, the owners also have Services and Tool servers (see Administration).

Security

SettingDescription
Enforce MFAEvery user must activate two-factor authentication. Until they do, they can only reach their profile, to set it up.

Sessions

SettingChoices
Sign out after inactivity15 minutes; 30 minutes (default); 1 hour; 4 hours; 24 hours
Maximum session length8 hours; 12 hours (default); 24 hours; 7 days; 30 days. Counted from signing in.

The limits apply to every session, including Remember me sign-ins. Those differ only in staying signed in after the browser is closed.

Logs

SettingChoices
Keep audit log entriesForever (default); 1 year; 2 years; 3 years
Keep execution log entriesForever; 30 days; 90 days (default); 1 year. The agent traces of the AI steps are kept as long.

A shorter time also removes the older entries already written. Audit log entries are kept at least 1 year.

Dates

Date format and Date and time format set how dates are shown across the app, in lists, fields and date pickers. Each choice is shown with an example. Default uses the installation's format.

Integrations

Integrations may connect to private network addresses (off by default) lets integration steps reach servers in your own network, such as an on-premises Bitdefender GravityZone console, a Veeam Backup & Replication server, a FortiGate's or a Sophos Firewall's administration address, a Checkmk site, a Zabbix server, a Wazuh server, a VMware vCenter Server, a Proxmox VE cluster or a Hyper-V host. Off, they connect only to public internet addresses. Rail22's own server, loopback and link-local addresses are never reachable.

Data access

The Data access tab chooses which projects AI clients may reach through the MCP server.

SettingDescription
MCP serverA switch per project, off by default. On: the project's MCP server answers its tokens, and the project's menu shows MCP server, where its members make tokens. Off: the menu item is gone and the project's tokens are refused. They work again when it is turned back on.

What the designer's Assistant may read of the projects is set in its own settings: see Assistant.

AI policy

The AI tab, for the owners, sets what the agents of AI steps may do across the account. By default nothing is restricted. The designer's Assistant is not affected.

SettingDescription
Integrations agents may useA switch per integration family. Off: no agent may use it, for reading or for changing. Workflow steps of that integration are not affected.
Agents may use (tools that change something)All of them (default), None, or Only those chosen. The list has each integration's write operations, the project tools that change something, Workflows run as tools, and Tools of MCP servers and tool servers.
A person always approves them firstEvery tool that changes something waits for a person, whatever the step's Ask for approval says. Approvers are the step's, or any project member when it names none.
Monthly AI budget (USD)The most all AI steps with the account's own keys may spend in a calendar month (UTC), estimated from the tokens at the providers' list prices. A model whose price Rail22 does not know still runs, but is not counted: the designer warns about it on the step. Once it is reached, those steps stop before their next call to the model, with an error naming the budget. Models that cost nothing go on. The System AI is paid in credits and is not counted. Empty: no limit.

A tool counts as changing something when it is an integration operation marked as a write, a workflow run as a tool (it may do anything), or a project or MCP tool not marked read-only. An MCP server's read-only mark is the server's own claim: only use servers you trust.

The policy is checked on the server, twice. When a step is saved, anything beyond the policy is refused with the reason. When a step runs, the tools the policy does not allow are not offered to the model, so a policy made after the step was saved still holds, and the run's log names them. Tools of MCP servers are only known when the step runs, so only that second check applies to them. Changes to the policy are in the audit log.

The spending so far this month is shown under the budget. Budgets are an estimate: steps running at the same moment can pass one slightly.

Other settings pages

Depending on what your installation provides and your plan, the Settings menu also has:

  • LDAP sign-in and SAML single sign-on
  • Inbound mail: the email prefix of the Email (inbound) trigger
  • Assistant: who runs the designer's Assistant
  • Knowledge bases: the embedding model of the account's knowledge bases
  • Usage and AI credits

Tool servers

The Tool servers tab lists the installation's MCP servers that AI steps can use, such as a web browser. It is there for the owners when the installation has no Multi-tenant plugin; with the plugin, the super-admins manage the servers and choose the accounts that may use them.

  • This account: a switch per server. On, the account's AI steps list it under Tool servers. Off, the AI steps that use it fail until it is removed from them.
  • Add server, Edit, Remove: the servers themselves (an id, a label, the MCP endpoint, headers, the tools the model may use, the sessions at once). A server marked installed was added by a script, such as the web browser's, and is changed there.
  • Test: connects, lists its tools, and for a web browser opens a public page and checks that a private address is refused.

See Tool servers for the file the servers are kept in.

pages.title: LDAP sign-in
pages.summary: Letting people sign in with their directory password (Active Directory, OpenLDAP...), with roles from their groups.
pages.html:
With LDAP sign-in, the people of your account sign in with their directory user name and password, such as Active Directory or OpenLDAP. Their role in Rail22 comes from their directory groups, checked at every sign-in. Other users keep their own Rail22 password. Every account has it, whatever its plan.

Set it up under Settings → LDAP sign-in.

The server

SettingDescription
DirectoryThe kind of directory, such as Active Directory or OpenLDAP. Sets the usual attribute names and filters, each of which can be changed.
ServersHost names or IP addresses, optionally with :port, separated by commas. Tried in order until one answers.
PortEmpty: 636 for LDAPS, else 389.
EncryptionPasswords are sent to the server, so use None only on a trusted network.
Check the server's certificateTurn it off only for a test server. Without the check, anyone on the way can read the passwords.
CA certificateOptional: the certificate (PEM) of the authority that signed the server's, when it is not a public one, such as your company's CA.
Bind DN, Bind passwordThe account that reads the directory, e.g. CN=svc-netflow,OU=Service,DC=example,DC=com. Active Directory also takes svc-netflow@example.com. Empty: anonymous.
Base DNWhere searches start, e.g. DC=example,DC=com.

Finding people

SettingDescription
User filterFinds the person by the name typed at sign-in, written as {login}. Empty: the directory's usual filter, which is shown.
Name, email, first name, last name attributesEmpty: sAMAccountName / uid, mail, givenName, sn.
Groups fromRead memberOf, or search the groups. OpenLDAP shows memberOf only with its memberof overlay.
Group base DN, Group filterWhere and how to search a person's groups: {dn} is the person's DN, {login} the name attribute's value.

Groups and roles

A list of rows, each a directory group and a Rail22 role. A person gets the role of the first row whose group they are in, so put the most powerful groups first. Others is the role for people in none of the groups. Leave it empty to refuse their sign-in.

Users

SettingDescription
Create users on their first sign-inOff: only users already linked to the directory can sign in.
Link existing usersA user of the account whose email matches a directory person's signs in with LDAP from then on, and no longer with their Rail22 password.
Email domainsSomeone signing in as name@domain without a user yet is looked up in this directory when the domain is one of these.
Names without @domain are this directory'sA name such as jdoe, with no user yet, is looked up in this directory. At most one account of the installation can use this.

Use Test before turning sign-in on: it checks the connection, or tries a sign-in with a user name and password and shows the person found and the role they would get. LDAP users have no password to reset in Rail22. Two-factor authentication still applies if they activate it or the account enforces it.

Note: workflows reach a directory with the LDAP step and an LDAP server credential. That is separate from sign-in, and every account has it, whatever its plan.

pages.title: SAML single sign-on
pages.summary: Signing in through your identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, ADFS, Keycloak...).
pages.html:
With SAML single sign-on, the people of your account sign in at your identity provider (IdP), such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, ADFS or Keycloak. Rail22 trusts the IdP's answer and gives them the role of their IdP groups. Other users keep their own password. Every account has it, whatever its plan.

Set it up under Settings → SAML single sign-on.

Setting it up

  1. In your IdP, create a SAML application for Rail22. Give it the values shown on the settings page: this application's metadata URL, its entity ID and its reply (ACS) URL. Many IdPs can read them all from the metadata URL.
  2. Back in Rail22, paste the IdP's metadata URL and click Import. This fills in the IdP's entity ID, sign-on URL and signing certificates. You can also type them.
  3. Map the IdP's groups to roles (below).
  4. Click Test to try a sign-in, then turn on Sign in with SAML single sign-on.

Settings

SettingDescription
IdP entity ID, single sign-on URL, signing certificatesFrom the IdP. Several certificates are allowed during a rollover. Responses must be signed by one of them.
Service provider entity IDEmpty: this application's metadata URL.
NameID formatWhat identifies a person. Users are found by it, then by email.
Sign the requestsSign-in requests are signed with this application's certificate.
Assertions must be encryptedWith this application's certificate, published in its metadata.
Ask the IdP to sign in againForceAuthn: no single sign-on with the IdP's existing session.
Accept IdP-initiated sign-insFrom the IdP's portal (an app tile), without a request from Rail22. Less safe: the response is not tied to the browser that asked.
Email, groups, first name, last name attributesEmpty: the usual names (email, mail, groups, memberOf, givenName, sn…).
Groups and roles; OthersAs for LDAP: the role of the first row whose group the person has, with the group as the IdP sends it (a name, an ID, a DN). Others: the role of everyone else. Empty refuses them.
Create users on their first sign-in; Link existing users; Email domainsAs for LDAP. A linked user signs in only at the IdP from then on, and their Rail22 password is removed.
Ask this application's 2FA tooOff: the IdP's sign-in is enough, and it usually asks its own MFA. On: users with 2FA in Rail22 also give its code.

This application's certificate can be renewed from the settings page. Publish the new metadata to the IdP when you do.

Signing in

People click Sign in with SSO on the sign-in page and type their email. The account is found by its email domain, and they are sent to the IdP. Signing out of Rail22 ends the Rail22 session only, not the IdP's.

pages.title: Inbound mail
pages.summary: The email prefix of your account's Email (inbound) trigger addresses.
pages.html:
Each Email (inbound) step has its own address, such as acme-7f3k2m9q@in.example.com. The first part is your account's email prefix, set on the Inbound mail tab of Account settings. Each account has its own.

SettingDescription
Email prefixThe start of your inbound addresses (prefix-xxxxxxxx@domain). Changing it changes all of them, so update any system that sends to the old addresses.

The tab appears only when the installation receives mail. On a self-hosted installation, see Inbound mail.

pages.title: Usage and AI credits
pages.summary: What the account uses of its plan's limits, and its System AI credits.
pages.html:
Usage

The Usage tab of Account settings (Settings menu) shows what the account uses of its plan's limits. When the installation manages plans (the Multi-tenant plugin), it also shows the account's plan. Without plans, nothing is limited and the tab only shows what is used. The limits are for the whole account:

  • Data tables: how many there are, the largest table, and the tables close to the row limit.
  • Files: the space used by all files.
  • AI credits: used this month.
  • Features: the optional features the plan includes, when the installation's plans have some.
  • Per project: each project's share.

When a limit is reached, the action that would go over it is refused with a message: creating a table, adding rows, uploading a file, or an AI call on the System AI.

AI credits

When the installation offers a System AI, its use is paid with the account's credits: by the Assistant with the System provider, and by AI steps whose credential is System AI. Settings → AI credits shows:

  • The monthly allowance: credits given each month. Unused credits don't roll over.
  • Top-ups: extra credits, used after the allowance and valid for 12 months.
  • What was used this month, and the latest changes, with their balance.

Each AI call counts its tokens in credits according to the model. A run reserves credits before calling the model, stops before a call once its credits are used up, and is charged only what it used.

pages.title: Audit and execution logs
pages.summary: Who did what in the account, what its agents did, and the record of all workflow runs.
pages.html:
The audit log

The audit log records who did what, and when: sign-ins, changes to users, roles and settings, and the creation, change, publishing and deletion of workflows, credentials, tables and files. Each entry shows who acted, from which address, what changed, and the values before and after. Secrets are never logged.

Owners find the whole account's log in the Settings menu under System audit log. Users whose role allows the audit log in project scope see the entries of their projects.

Click an entry to see its details. The list can be filtered and sorted.

Agent actions

Every tool call an AI step's agent makes is an audit entry, action Agent action. The Agent actions button above the list shows only those, as does the Action filter. The entry shows:

  • the workflow, the execution and the step
  • the tool, and whether it reads or writes
  • the arguments, with secrets removed
  • the result: ok, error, waiting for approval, rejected, not approved in time or stopped by a limit
  • who approved it, if someone did

A call that asks for approval has two entries: one when it is asked, one when it is decided. Secrets are removed by the name of the argument (password, token, API key and the like) and by their form inside a text (bearer tokens, private keys, passwords in URLs), which cannot catch a secret with no such sign. Other values are kept, including personal data, even when masked for the provider. These entries are sealed and kept like all the others. Their arguments are longer than most: a value is cut at 2,000 characters, and arguments over 20,000 are not kept.

The execution log

The execution log records the runs of all workflows: when, which workflow and version, what started it and how it ended. A run that pauses (a Wait step, a task, another workflow) gets an Execution waiting entry with the step it waits at, the loop item when the step is inside a loop, and the time it is due. Each time it continues, an Execution resumed entry follows with how late it woke. A waiting entry with no resumed entry after its due time means the run is stuck, not sleeping. It also records requests refused by triggers, such as a webhook call or a GravityZone event push with a wrong secret or to an unpublished workflow, and GravityZone events left out above the limit of runs per request. Owners find it in the Settings menu under System execution log.

For the details of one run (its log lines and variables), open the workflow's Executions panel.

Retention

How long each log keeps its entries is set in Account settings. Audit entries are kept at least one year. The agent traces of the AI steps follow the execution log's setting. So do conversations with agents and the runs that hold their text.

pages.title: Plugins overview
pages.summary: The optional features of Rail22, what each adds, and how they are enabled.
pages.html:
Some features of Rail22 come as plugins: the administration of many accounts with the System AI, the steps of a country, and more. On a hosted installation they are managed for you. Whether you see a plugin's features depends on your plan and on what the installation provides. The Google and Microsoft 365 steps, the Assistant, the MCP server, LDAP sign-in, SAML single sign-on and inbound mail (when the installation receives mail) are not plugins: they are part of Rail22 itself, on every plan, Free included.

PluginAddsDepends on
Multi-tenantThe super-admins' pages (services, accounts, plans); as options, sign-up for new accounts and the System AI (an AI model offered by the installation, paid with credits)Super-admins; the System AI: the installation's settings
Romania (RegionalRO)The steps of Romanian institutions and services: ANAF (companies, e-Factura, e-Transport), BNR exchange rates, SmartBill, FGO, Sameday, FAN Courier, CargusThe services' accounts (credentials); none for the company lookup and the exchange rates
SAPSAP Cloud Integration: call iFlows, message processing logs, deployed artifacts, deploy and undeploy, any API call, and a trigger for failed messages (later SAP Business One and S/4HANA)Service keys of the Cloud Integration tenant (credentials)

Self-hosted installations

Plugins are folders in app/plugins/. They are enabled in plugins.json, next to app.env (none when the file is missing), in order (some use others). Each plugin is an entry named after its folder, holding its own settings:

{
  "MultiTenant": {
    "enabled": true,
    "config": { "registration": false, "system_ai": true },
    "tiers": { ... },
    "credit_rates": { ... }
  }
}

Set "enabled": false, or remove the entry, to turn a plugin off: its menus, steps, credentials and pages disappear. Its data stays in the database. A plugin that is listed but not installed is left out (and logged). Restart PHP-FPM and the daemon after a change.

The Multi-tenant plugin comes from its own repository: clone it into app/plugins/MultiTenant and add its entry first in plugins.json.

The steps of a country or region come as regional plugins, one each, named Regional and the country's code: RegionalRO for Romania. Each has its own repository; install only those of the places the installation serves.

The SAP plugin has its own repository too: clone it into app/plugins/SAP and add "SAP": { "enabled": true } to plugins.json.

plugins.json is the installation's own: it is not in git, so updating Rail22 (git pull) never overwrites it and never is blocked by it. Keep it in your backups.

To write your own plugin, see Plugins and hooks.

Tool servers (MCP servers the installation offers to the AI steps, such as a web browser) are not a plugin: every installation has them. See Tool servers.

pages.title: Multi-tenant
pages.summary: For an installation that hosts many accounts: the administration, and as options sign-up and the System AI.
pages.html:
The Multi-tenant plugin is for an installation that hosts many accounts. It adds the super-admins' administration, and two options the installation turns on or off: sign-up for new accounts, and the System AI.

Administration

The plugin adds Settings → Administration for super-admins. There they see the installation and manage all the accounts with their plans, limits, credits and tool servers, and can suspend or view an account. With the plugin, Settings → Services (start, stop and restart the installation's services) is for super-admins only; without it, the accounts' owners have it as the Services tab of Account settings. See Administration.

Sign-up (option)

With sign-up on, the sign-in page has a link to create a new account. People enter their email and receive a confirmation link. The link's page asks for the account's name (their company or team), their name and a password. They become the new account's Owner. With sign-up off, there is no sign-up page.

System AI (option)

With the System AI on, the installation offers an AI model it runs to every account. AI steps can use it as their credential, and the Assistant as its provider, without an API key of your own. Use is paid in AI credits: a monthly allowance plus top-ups, shown under Settings → AI credits. See Usage and AI credits, and for self-hosted installations System AI.

Self-hosted installations

The plugin is kept in its own repository. Clone it into the app's plugins folder, then add its entry first in plugins.json, next to app.env. The plugin's plugins.json.example holds the entry as shipped:

git clone <the plugin's repository> app/plugins/MultiTenant
cp app/plugins/MultiTenant/plugins.json.example plugins.json      # or add its "MultiTenant" entry first in your plugins.json

Update it with git pull in app/plugins/MultiTenant, along with Rail22's own update. Then restart PHP-FPM and the daemon.

Its settings are in its plugins.json entry (not in git: updates don't overwrite them):

  • config: the options, registration (sign-up, off as shipped) and system_ai (on as shipped; it also needs the System AI settings in app.env).
  • tiers: the plans: default, the plan of the accounts that have none, and tiers by name, each with a label, limits (datatables, datatable_records, files_bytes, ai_monthly_credits; null: no limit) and features. Without it there are no plans: no limits.
  • credit_rates: what the System AI's models cost in credits: credit_usd (what 1 credit is worth), default_margin, and models by model id prefix, each with a margin over the provider's price (0.3 = 30%) or its own in, out, cache_read credits per 1M tokens. ./v MultiTenant::credits::rates shows them.

Restart PHP-FPM and the daemon after a change.

pages.title: Romania (RegionalRO)
pages.summary: The regional plugin for Romania: ANAF, BNR exchange rates, SmartBill, FGO, Sameday, FAN Courier and Cargus.
pages.html:
The RegionalRO plugin adds the steps of Romanian institutions and services: ANAF (companies, e-Factura, e-Transport), the National Bank's exchange rates, the SmartBill and FGO invoicing services, and the Sameday, FAN Courier and Cargus couriers. It is one of Rail22's regional plugins: one per country or region, so an installation adds only the ones of the places it serves.

Its steps are in the Regional group of the step list, and its credentials in the Romania group. They are available to every account of an installation that has the plugin.

The steps

StepWhat it doesCredential
ANAF Company LookupCompanies by CUI / CIF: name, address, VAT, e-Factura registration.None
BNR Exchange RatesThe reference rates of a day; conversions.None
ANAF e-FacturaUpload invoices, their status, messages, downloads; validate, PDF.ANAF (SPV); none to validate and for the PDF
ANAF e-TransportDeclarations of transported goods: the UIT code.ANAF (SPV)
SmartBillInvoices, proformas, payments, PDFs, emails, series, VAT rates, stocks.SmartBill
FGOInvoices, PDFs, status, cancel, reverse, payments, AWBs, nomenclatures.FGO
SamedayAWBs, costs, status, labels, easyboxes.Sameday
FAN CourierAWBs, tariffs, tracking, labels.FAN Courier
CargusAWBs, prices, tracing, documents.Cargus

Installing

On a hosted installation, the plugin is there when the installation serves Romanian accounts. On a self-hosted one, clone it into the app's plugins folder and add its entry to plugins.json, next to app.env (see Plugins overview):

git clone <the plugin's repository> app/plugins/RegionalRO
# add to plugins.json:  "RegionalRO": { "enabled": true }

Restart PHP-FPM and the daemon. Update it with git pull in app/plugins/RegionalRO, along with Rail22's own update.

Credentials

Create them under Credentials & variables, in the Romania group. Test on each one signs in and reads something small.

ANAF (SPV)

For e-Factura and e-Transport. The holder of a qualified certificate registers an OAuth app in ANAF's portal (anaf.ro > Servicii online > Înregistrare utilizatori > Editare profil Oauth), with the services E-Factura and / or E-Transport, and with the redirect URI shown on the credential's form. Save the credential, then use Connect: ANAF's sign-in page asks the browser for the certificate, so plug in its token first. The connection lasts a year; then use Connect again. The certificate must have rights on the company in SPV.

SettingDescription
Client IDOf the OAuth app registered in ANAF's portal (Editare profil Oauth), with the services E-Factura and / or E-Transport. Required.
Client secretStored encrypted. Required.
CIFThe company the steps act for when they name none (its CUI / CIF, without RO); the certificate must have rights on it in SPV.
ANAF test environmentapi.anaf.ro/test: invoices and declarations sent there are not real (the OAuth app and the certificate are the same). Default: off.

SmartBill

The account's email and its API token, from SmartBill: Integrari > API.

SettingDescription
API tokenSmartBill: Integrari > API. Stored encrypted. Required.
Company CIFThe company the documents are issued for, as in SmartBill (e.g. RO12345678). Required.

FGO

An API user of the FGO account (Setari > Utilizatori; production needs a PRO or PREMIUM subscription) gives the private key. Test only shows that FGO answers: the key is checked at the first invoice operation.

SettingDescription
Company CUICodUnic: the company's fiscal code, without RO. Required.
Private keyOf the API user (FGO: Setari > Utilizatori). Stored encrypted. Required.
Platform URLPlatformaUrl, the calling application's address FGO is told; empty: https://dev.example.com.
FGO test environmentapi-testuat.fgo.ro, with an account made at testuat.fgo.ro (not synchronised with production). Default: off.

Sameday

The API user and password from Sameday. A demo user works only with Demo environment on; its pickup points and services have other ids than production's.

SettingDescription
API userRequired.
PasswordStored encrypted. Required.
Demo environmentsameday-api.demo.zitec.com, with a demo user: AWBs there are not real (its pickup points and services have other ids). Default: off.

FAN Courier

The selfAWB user and password, and the client id of the sender's branch. API access needs a contract with FAN Courier; its selfAWB department sends the user.

SettingDescription
selfAWB userRequired.
PasswordStored encrypted. Required.
Client idThe sender branch's client id (clientId), from FAN Courier. Required.

Cargus

In Cargus's API portal (urgentcargus.portal.azure-api.net), subscribe to StandardUrgentOnlineAPI; once approved, copy its Primary Key. The user and password are those of WebExpress.

SettingDescription
Subscription keyCargus's API portal: Products > StandardUrgentOnlineAPI, the Primary Key. Stored encrypted. Required.
UserThe WebExpress user. Required.
PasswordStored encrypted. Required.
Pickup location idWhere the AWBs leave from when a step names none (Cargus step: List pickup locations).
API addressEmpty: https://urgentcargus.azure-api.net/api/.

What the steps share

  • Lists give { items, count, total, truncated }, at most At most (items).
  • Files: PDFs, labels and downloaded XML are saved in the project's Files; the result is { id, filename, size, contentType }, ready for Send email or an upload step.
  • Call the API (SmartBill, FGO, the couriers) makes any call of the service through the credential: a method, a path after the service's address, a query and a JSON body. Use it for what the operations do not cover.
  • Errors: the service's own message, such as FAN Courier: These credentials do not match our records. With On error set to continue, the step goes on through its error output.
  • Sign-in: Sameday, FAN Courier and Cargus give a token for a day; the daemon keeps it while it runs, so the steps do not sign in for every call.

AI steps

An AI step can use these steps as tools, in its Integrations… section. ANAF Company Lookup and BNR Exchange Rates need no credential: choose Used. Issuing, uploading, deleting and Call the API count as changing something: they are not offered by default, and ask for approval when approvals are on.

IntegrationTool namesOperationsCredential
ANAF Company Lookupro_company_…, e.g. ro_company_lookup1 (1 read)None: Used
BNR Exchange Ratesro_bnr_…, e.g. ro_bnr_rates2 (2 read)None: Used
ANAF e-Factura / e-Transportanaf_…, e.g. anaf_efactura_upload9 (7 read)ANAF (SPV)
SmartBillsmartbill_…, e.g. smartbill_invoice15 (6 read)SmartBill
FGOfgo_…, e.g. fgo_invoice12 (5 read)FGO
Samedaysameday_…, e.g. sameday_awb10 (7 read)Sameday
FAN Courierfan_…, e.g. fan_awb9 (6 read)FAN Courier
Carguscargus_…, e.g. cargus_awb10 (7 read)Cargus

pages.title: ANAF Company Lookup
pages.summary: Romanian companies by CUI / CIF from ANAF's public register: name, address, VAT status, e-Factura registration.
pages.html:
The ANAF Company Lookup step reads Romanian companies from ANAF's public register (the VAT payers' web service). It needs no credential.

Give one or more codes, separated by commas or new lines, or a list (of codes, or of objects with cui or cif), with or without RO. Each code's control digit is checked first. ANAF answers 100 codes a second; the step sends longer lists 100 at a time, a second apart, at most 500.

The credential, the lists, Call the API and the errors are the same for every step of the plugin: see Romania (RegionalRO).

Operations

OperationCallsResult
Look up companiesPlatitorTvaRest/v9/tva{ items, count, company, notFound, invalid }

Settings

SettingDescription
CUI / CIFOne or more, separated by commas or new lines (or a list); with or without RO. At most 500; ANAF answers 100 a second.
On dateYYYY-MM-DD; empty: today.
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableWhat the operation gives. Default: companies. Required.
On errorThe service's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

The result

Each company in items has short names: cui, name, address, regCom, phone, postalCode, caen, iban, registeredOn, registrationStatus, taxOffice, legalForm, vatPayer, vatFrom, vatTo, vatOnCollection, splitVat, inactive, inactiveSince, deregisteredOn, eFactura, eFacturaSince, the headOffice and the fiscalAddress (county, countyCode, locality, street, number, details, postalCode), and anaf: the record as ANAF gives it. company is the first one found (null when none).

Codes ANAF does not know are in notFound, and texts that are not valid codes in invalid: neither is an error. A step with no valid code at all fails (or continues on its error output).

For example, before issuing an invoice: look up {{ order.cui }}, then use {{ companies.company.name }} and {{ companies.company.vatPayer }} on it, or stop when {{ companies.company.inactive }}.

pages.title: BNR Exchange Rates
pages.summary: The National Bank of Romania's reference exchange rates of a day, and conversions between currencies.
pages.html:
The BNR Exchange Rates step reads the reference rates the National Bank of Romania publishes each banking day, about 13:00 Romania's time. It needs no credential.

A day without rates (a weekend, a holiday) gives the banking day before it; date in the result says which day was used. The files read are kept for a while (the latest one 10 minutes, the current year's 30 minutes), so many runs do not read them again.

The credential, the lists, Call the API and the errors are the same for every step of the plugin: see Romania (RegionalRO).

Operations

OperationCallsResult
Get exchange ratescurs.bnr.ro: nbrfxrates.xml, or the year's file{ date, requested, base, rates }: rates are RON for 1 unit of each currency (HUF, JPY and the others BNR gives for 100 are divided).
Convert an amountthe same{ amount, from, to, rate, result, date, requested }: result rounded to Decimals, rate is 1 from in to.

Settings

SettingDescription
OperationChoices: Get exchange rates; Convert an amount. Default: Get exchange rates. Required.
On dateYYYY-MM-DD; empty: the latest rates. A day without rates (a weekend, a holiday): the banking day before. (For: Get exchange rates, Convert an amount.)
Currenciese.g. EUR, USD; empty: all. (For: Get exchange rates.)
Amount(Required for: Convert an amount.)
DecimalsOf the result, 0 to 8. Default: 2. (For: Convert an amount.)
From currencyDefault: EUR. (Required for: Convert an amount.)
To currencyDefault: RON. (Required for: Convert an amount.)
Timeout (s)Default: 30. Required.
Result variableWhat the operation gives. Default: rates. Required.
On errorThe service's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

For example, an invoice in EUR to RON: Convert an amount with {{ invoice.total }} from EUR to RON, then {{ rates.result }}.

pages.title: ANAF e-Factura
pages.summary: RO e-Factura: upload invoices, check their status, list and download messages; validate an invoice and make its PDF.
pages.html:
The ANAF e-Factura step works with RO e-Factura, the national system of electronic invoices. Uploading, the status, the messages and the downloads go through an ANAF (SPV) credential; validating an invoice and making its PDF are public and need none.

The XML is a text (an expression, e.g. the output of a template), or a project file: {{ file }} of another step, or its id. The step sends the XML as it is: it does not build the UBL invoice from fields.

The credential, the lists, Call the API and the errors are the same for every step of the plugin: see Romania (RegionalRO).

Operations

OperationCallsResult
Upload an invoice (changes)upload?standard=&cif= (+ extern=DA, autofactura=DA){ uploadId, date }. ANAF checks the invoice afterwards: see Status.
Get an upload's statusstareMesaj?id_incarcare={ state, ready, ok, downloadId, errors }: state is ok, nok, in prelucrare (being processed) or XML cu erori nepreluat de sistem.
List messageslistaMesajePaginatieFactura{ items, count, total, truncated }: each with id (for Download), uploadId, cif, created, type, details.
Download a messagedescarcare?id={ files, invoice, signature, xml }: the ZIP's XML files saved in Files, and the invoice's (or the errors') XML as text, up to 1 MB.
Validate an invoice (without sending)validare/FACT1 or FCN (public){ valid, state, messages, traceId }. Not valid is a result, not an error.
Make an invoice's PDFtransformare/FACT1 or FCN (public)The file saved in the project's Files: { id, filename, size, contentType }.

Settings

SettingDescription
ANAF credentialA credential of the project. (Required for: Upload an invoice, Get an upload's status, List messages, Download a message.)
OperationChoices: Upload an invoice; Get an upload's status; List messages; Download a message; Validate an invoice (without sending); Make an invoice's PDF. Default: Upload an invoice. Required.
XMLThe invoice's XML (UBL 2.1, CIUS-RO), or a project file: {{ file }} of another step, or its id. (Required for: Upload an invoice, Validate an invoice (without sending), Make an invoice's PDF.)
DocumentValidate and PDF: invoices and credit notes in UBL only. Choices: Invoice (UBL); Credit note (UBL); Invoice (CII); Buyer's message (RASP). Default: Invoice (UBL). (For: Upload an invoice, Validate an invoice (without sending), Make an invoice's PDF.)
CIFThe seller's (upload) or the company's (messages); empty: the credential's. (For: Upload an invoice, List messages.)
Buyer outside Romaniaextern=DA. Default: off. (For: Upload an invoice.)
Self-invoiceIssued by the buyer for the seller (autofactura=DA). Default: off. (For: Upload an invoice.)
Upload idindex_incarcare, from Upload. (Required for: Get an upload's status.)
DaysThe last 1 to 60 days. Default: 7. (For: List messages.)
MessagesChoices: All; Invoices sent; Invoices received; Errors; Buyers' messages. (For: List messages.)
Download idid_descarcare (Status), or a message's id (List messages). (Required for: Download a message.)
Validate firstOff: the PDF of an XML that may not be valid. Default: on. (For: Make an invoice's PDF.)
File nameEmpty: from ANAF's names (download), invoice-<date>.pdf (pdf). (For: Download a message, Make an invoice's PDF.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List messages.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: efactura. Required.
On errorThe service's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

A typical flow

  1. Validate an invoice with the XML; stop when {{ efactura.valid }} is false.
  2. Upload an invoice; keep {{ efactura.uploadId }}.
  3. A Wait of a few minutes, then Get an upload's status in a Loop until ready.
  4. Download a message with downloadId: the invoice signed by ANAF, or the errors.

Note: turn on ANAF test environment in the credential while you build the workflow: invoices sent there are not real.

pages.title: ANAF e-Transport
pages.summary: RO e-Transport: declare transported goods and get the UIT code, check an upload, list the declarations.
pages.html:
The ANAF e-Transport step sends the declarations of goods transported in Romania and gets the UIT code the transport travels with. It uses an ANAF (SPV) credential whose OAuth app has the E-Transport service.

The XML (schema eTransport v2: a notification, a correction, a deletion, a confirmation or a vehicle change) is a text or a project file, as for e-Factura.

The credential, the lists, Call the API and the errors are the same for every step of the plugin: see Romania (RegionalRO).

Operations

OperationCallsResult
Upload a declaration (changes)upload/ETRANSP/<cif>/2{ uploadId, uit, date, warning, traceId }: uit for a new notification.
Get an upload's statusstareMesaj/<id>{ state, ready, ok, errors }
List declarationslista/<days>/<cif>{ items, count, total, truncated }, each declaration as ANAF gives it.

Settings

SettingDescription
ANAF credentialA credential of the project. Required.
OperationChoices: Upload a declaration; Get an upload's status; List declarations. Default: Upload a declaration. Required.
XMLThe declaration's XML (eTransport v2), or a project file: {{ file }} of another step, or its id. (Required for: Upload a declaration.)
CIFThe declarant's; empty: the credential's. (For: Upload a declaration, List declarations.)
Upload idindex_incarcare, from Upload. (Required for: Get an upload's status.)
DaysThe last 1 to 60 days. Default: 7. (For: List declarations.)
At most (items)Of a list: more are left out (truncated). Default: 1000. Required. (For: List declarations.)
Timeout (s)Default: 60. Required.
Result variableA list: { items, count, total, truncated }; otherwise what the operation gives. Default: etransport. Required.
On errorThe service's errors, or no connection. Choices: Fail the step; Continue on the error output. Default: Fail the step. Required.

pages.title: SmartBill
pages.summary: SmartBill Cloud: invoices, proformas and payments, their PDFs and emails, series, VAT rates and stocks.
pages.html:
The SmartBill step works with SmartBill Cloud (API V1), for the company of its credential.

To issue a document, give it as a JSON object with SmartBill's field names in Document, such as client and products. companyVatCode comes from the credential, and Series, when given, sets seriesName. The names of the series, VAT rates (taxName) and units (measuringUnitName) must be the ones of your SmartBill account: List document series and List VAT rates show them. Prices are without VAT unless the product has "isTaxIncluded": true.

{
  "client": { "name": "Client SRL", "vatCode": "RO12345678", "address": "Str. Exemplu 1", "city": "Cluj-Napoca", "county": "Cluj", "country": "Romania" },
  "issueDate": "{{ today }}",
  "products": [
    { "name": "Consultanta", "code": "C01", "quantity": 2, "price": 100, "measuringUnitName": "ora",
      "currency": "RON", "taxName": "Normala", "taxPercentage": 21, "isService": true }
  ]
}

The credential, the lists, Call the API and the errors are the same for every step of the plugin: see Romania (RegionalRO).

Operations

OperationCallsResult
Issue an invoice (changes)POST invoice/v2{ series, number, url, documentUrl, documentId, ... }
Issue a proforma (changes)POST estimate/v2the same
Issue a payment (receipt) (changes)POST paymentSmartBill's answer
Reverse an invoice (changes)POST invoice/reversethe reversing invoice: { series, number, ... }
Cancel a document (changes)PUT invoice/cancel, estimate/cancelSmartBill's answer
Restore a document (changes)PUT invoice/restore, estimate/restoreSmartBill's answer

pages.title: FGO
pages.summary: FGO invoicing: issue invoices, their PDFs, status, cancel, reverse, payments, AWBs, nomenclatures and articles.
pages.html:
The FGO step works with the FGO invoicing API (v7), for the company of its credential. Each request is signed as FGO asks (an SHA-1 hash of the company's code, the private key and the client's name or the invoice's number), and carries the Platform URL of the credential.

To issue an invoice, give it as a JSON object with FGO's field names in Document. Series, when given, sets Serie; Valuta is RON and TipFactura is Factura unless the document says otherwise. The values of countries, counties, VAT rates and payment types come from FGO's nomenclatures (List a nomenclature).

{
  "Client": { "Denumire": "Client SRL", "Tip": "PJ", "CodUnic": "RO12345678", "Tara": "RO", "Judet": "Cluj", "Localitate": "Cluj-Napoca", "Adresa": "Str. Exemplu 1" },
  "Continut": [
    { "Denumire": "Consultanta", "NrProduse": 2, "UM": "ORE", "CotaTVA": 21, "PretUnitar": 100 }
  ]
}

The credential, the lists, Call the API and the errors are the same for every step of the plugin: see Romania (RegionalRO).

pages.summary: Sameday shipments: create AWBs and estimate their cost, track them, print labels, easyboxes and pickup points.
